## CLAUDE.md, audited a second time (2026-08-29, entry 201)

The second pass over `CLAUDE.md`, applying the entry-47 audit's proposal (`design/spec-pass/claude-md-audit.md`, Q943) together with Ed's rulings of 2026-08-28 and 2026-08-29 — **Q1003** *move the governance rules out; pointers only, SPEC is the source*, **Q1051** *the byte count is a consequence, never a criterion*, **Q1052** *you mark the keepers first*. Ed's own vetoes in the same sitting are honoured and nothing below touches them: **Q1001** keeps the card lifecycle stated twice, **Q1002** keeps *One card per decision* whole with both its examples, and **Q1000**/**Q1035** were folded before this pass ran.

Everything below stood in `CLAUDE.md` and is reproduced verbatim. What is **not** here is the material that left because another document already states it in the same words — SPEC §9.6 and §9.6a's two kinds, routes and eras; SURFACE C1's *every surface is the session-view*, C8 and E5's acknowledgement rule; STYLE.md T6–T9's power-clause copy and §8's T1–T35 — which is a duplicate removed, not a reason moved. Nor is the history narration (dated changelog clauses in *Documents*, a directory tour of `design/*.html`), which git holds.

**The pen hold captured its button at `pointerdown`** (Gotchas, *Nothing rebuilds under a press*; guard `npm run journey`):

> The **pen hold captured its button at `pointerdown`** and called `b.click()` a second later; a poll in between left `b` detached, and a click on a detached element never reaches the `document` listener that commits. The act vanished in silence — no command, no error, the card just sitting there. The hold belongs to the **open card**, not to one DOM node, so it re-finds the live commit control when its own has gone.
>
> **Both polls now defer while a hold is in flight** (`penHold || SESSION.holding`). `SESSION.holding` is a module-level flag because the propose hold's own state lives inside `renderDoc` and is re-created by every render.

**The day the no-defaults retirement was half-applied** (*The two kinds of decision*, rule 4, since reduced to *Nothing arrives delegated*):

> It was retired at the surface first and left in the module for a day, where it did real damage: ten questions collected from the instant of creation, and because `settled()` counts a members-held setting as settled, the live page released the whole constitution at once instead of a clause at a time.

The rule it retired, stated in full before its retirement and now stated only in SPEC §9.0a:

> 4. **Constitutional settings default to the members, ordinary ones to the founder** — the room can take an ordinary one back cheaply and cannot take a constitutional one back at all. **Retired everywhere, 2026-08-21** (Ed's no-defaults instruction; SPEC §9.0a amended, v0.63, closing Q511)

**⏩ keeps 🌍 with the founder** (Gotchas; a reason rather than a post-mortem — nothing broke):

> **⏩ keeps 🌍 with the founder** (Ed, 2026-08-22, asking whether the tooling could be more useful for this work). ⏩ already left four power cards live — title, link, rate, machines, being the settings it keeps — so the gap was never *no power card*; it was that every **constitutional** setting was delegated, and delegation is the state of holding neither power, so a constitutional 🛡️ card, the 👑 mark and the whole crown-question route were unreachable by hand in a settled document. Keeping 🌍 costs the fixture nothing it was saying (the value is the same `closed` the room was answering its way to, so every visibility sentence reads as before); what changes is the governance half — the clause gains its deviation and Ash is a 👑 rather than a 📯. Note the **setup-probe is unaffected**, and for a reason worth knowing: its founding scenario sets 🌍 by hand before pressing ⏩, and SEED only fills a key that is still empty — so the probe was always running on a founder-held 🌍 and this changes only the press-⏩-from-blank path. Power cards remain outside probe coverage by Ed's call.

**A lapsed member is owed an acknowledgement too** (Gotchas; the rule itself is SPEC §9.6a and SURFACE C8/E5/Y10, the argument is here):

> **A lapsed member is owed an acknowledgement too** (Ed, 2026-08-22). E excludes the lapsed, and for every other purpose that is right — they are out of the quorum base and out of the electorate, because those are about who is *deciding*. An acknowledgement is not a decision: it is owed to somebody about a document they are **still a member of**, and lapse is a stall with an alarm rather than a departure (§9.5a) — revival is just logging in and their cast judgments keep counting. The person who was living under the old rule and went quiet is exactly the one a change ought to find. The exclusions that stay are the ones that mean something: a **removed** member is gone, and somebody who was **not yet here** never knew the old rule, so the change is not news to them — it is simply what the document says. Since Q842 that second one covers the joiner as well as the never-arrived: a member who turns up afterwards inherits every rule set before them and is owed nothing for any of it, so **the test is one question — were you here when it was set?** The whole shape of the rule is *what happened while you were here*, which is also why a grant is different: a power handed to you is addressed to you whenever it arrives.

**🍾 has no wallet, and that is where the family stops** (Gotchas; a reason, and an argument against a design nobody built):

> **🍾 has no wallet, and that is where the family stops** (Q516, Ed: *am I going overboard with the wallets*). The four wallets are the four verbs, and the four verbs are a ladder of *who has to agree*; each is a **capacity you hold**. Beginning is not a level of authority and not a capacity — it is a moment that happens once, so a wallet for it is a button with a balance drawn on it, and it would beg a 🥂 wallet for the act nobody performs. What 🍾 does have is **its own glyph on its own commit** (it had borrowed ✒️, a category error: beginning is what *ends* the founding) and its own flight — **the cork leaves the button and lands in the document**. A pop, not a spend.

**An address is checked because it is the address, not because it was typed** — the largest line in `CLAUDE.md` at 2,167 B, and the clearest eviction in the file: `scripts/slug-walk.mjs` fails on the pre-fix page at *the commit is dark on a typed address that is taken*, which is this failure exactly.

> **An address is checked because it is the address, not because it was typed** (Ed, 2026-08-22: *the address was taken — we shouldn't allow it to be set if it's taken*). 📍's commit has always been gated on `slugRefused()`, but the only caller of `checkSlug` was the **input** handler — so an address the founder never edited had no verdict at all and the gate stood open on an unasked question. The birth pre-fills 📍 from the title, and `suggestSlug` consulted the fixture's Hollow Oak `TAKEN` set, which knows nothing about the live host; accept the suggestion unedited and the first thing in the world to ask about the address was the **send**, answering truthfully *that address is taken* and walking the founder back to 📍 — the right answer to a question the card should have asked first, arriving at the one step that mints the document. (It is the same surface bug as the double send of the same morning, by a different road: both end at a correct 409 that reads as the page malfunctioning.) Four rules now hold it shut. The check is **idempotent and callable from anywhere** — `S.slugSeen` is the address the last verdict was about, whatever it said — and **`render` asks whenever there is an address to ask about**, which covers the pre-filled one and every path that sets it without a keystroke; only typing debounces. The commit additionally waits for a verdict (`slugKnown()`), which closes the window between a keystroke and the answer about it, but **a verdict that cannot be got counts as one**, so an unreachable host can never leave the founder at a permanently dark 📍 — the send's 409 stays the backstop it always was. **A creation's own reservation is not somebody else's**: the first send reserves the address, so asking the server about it afterwards is told, truthfully, that it is taken *by us* — the page answers for `api.birth.slug` itself rather than refusing the founder their own document (Q462b, on the check rather than the send). And a refusal **offers the nearest free address** — `GET /api/slug/:slug` carries a `suggestion` like the 409 does, because a block naming no way forward is worse than the bug.

**Two sessions often run at once** (Conventions) — the three rules stay in `CLAUDE.md`; the evening that produced each is here:

> **Commit before compacting or clearing** — not because compaction touches the disk (it does not; files survive), but because it takes with it the only record of *what* the half-finished file in the tree was for: this session found `CLAUDE.new.md` and `part2.md` untracked with nothing to say what they were. **Claim a question number by writing it into QUESTIONS.md**, never by using it in a commit message or in chat — two sessions took 482 for the same question within an hour, because one of them held its numbers in prose where the other could not see them. And **re-read a long shared file immediately before editing it**, since the other session may have rewritten it since you last looked; the loser of a concurrent write is whoever wrote first.

**The applicant's walk, and why it exists** (Conventions; the walk's own header carries it too):

> **No other harness has ever had an applicant in it**, which is how Q900 stayed invisible; it fails on the pre-entry-96 page at *the application raised no entry in the rail*.

**The seat matrix's payload** (Conventions and the `seat-matrix.mjs` entry both stated it; the fact was wrong, `--out` defaulting to a gitignored path):

> after every step snapshots each seat's rail and `view()` to `design/tools/seat-matrix.json` … It fails on the pre-Q639 page at *E8 grant-pen · early carries it, outside the audience (the holder)*.

**The tab you click does not move** moved *within* `CLAUDE.md` rather than out of it — from *The two kinds of decision*, where a CSS measurement had been sitting in a section about governance because its headline sentence sounds like a principle, to *Gotchas · Design system* beside its own consequence. Its bytes stay in the file.

**The arithmetic.** 102,887 B before, 94,007 B after: **−8,880 B, 8.6%**. Nothing was removed because the file is long (Q1051). No glossary entry was deleted — 147 before and 147 after — and no name left the file; *Retired names* is untouched, having gained nothing because nothing named a part that is gone. The gotcha count went **up**, 61 to 62, and the guarded count from 20 to 24, because the eviction rule was applied by naming guards rather than by deleting them.

## A member convenor resigns like anybody after the start (2026-08-29, entry 248)

**Written under the recommended reading of entry 248, with Ed's ruling asked and not yet given** — so a later reader can tell an assumption from a decision. SPEC §9.6a says a resignation is *free, immediate and nobody's to refuse*, the one act that is always at ✒️, and in the same paragraph that *the convenor's membership, if any, is ordinary membership*. `resign` in `packages/constitution/src/session.ts` said otherwise: it refused the convenor outright with *the convenor unticks their own row instead (§9.6a)*. Entry 248, found while writing the R-060 plan, put the disagreement to Ed and asked which of the two should move. **The spec was right and the code moved.** The refusal it pointed at is the pre-start route — untick 🎩 and the record is deleted, leaving a clerk convenor whose shield stands (X15) — and 🎩 is locked at the start (§9.6a), so after 🍾 the sentence named no route at all: the only way a member convenor could leave the membership was a carried 🥾 removal motion against themselves.

**The refusal becomes pre-start only, and nothing else is added.** Two things make that the whole change. First, `crownSeatVacated` was already written to be called by whatever empties the seat, and `convenorSeatVacant()` is a claim about *state* — the convenor's own record present and wearing `removed` — never about which event produced it, so a resignation and a carried removal say *vacant* in exactly the same way, and R-060 needed no second rule and no second predicate to cover this door. `resign` gains one call to it, placed as the `remove` arm of `settleCarriedEffects` places it: after the roster's own follow-ons and never inside them. Second, `member-removed` with `by: 'self'` for the convenor's id replays through the arm every resignation already replays through, so the fold, `departures()`, the server's door sentence and the mail fold all take it unchanged.

**The pre-start refusal stays, and its sentence is still the right advice.** Unticking deletes the record; resigning would mark it `removed` and manufacture a vacant seat in a document that has not begun, which is a state nothing was designed for. `uninvite`'s twin refusal is untouched for the same reason, and `remove`'s stands because exile at will is somebody else's act on you.

**The office is not re-assigned, and nothing here creates a second convenor.** A vacated seat is what R-060 already defines: the shield reads down for the rest of the document's life and parked *text* questions auto-pass. What a vacated office keeps was left open — `seatAlive` in the server says the convenor always has a live seat, so a resigned convenor still opens the document, still holds ✒️ and 🛡️ on every setting they never laid down, and 👑 still marks them, while `viewerIsMember()` goes false and their row leaves *Members*. Whether a resignation ends the **office** or only the **membership** is §9.3's foundership question and is not answered here.

On the surface, `leaveBtn` in `design/session-view.html` drops its `!amFounder()`: the button is drawn into `meBlock`, the viewer's own row, which is where `founderMark()` is printed too, so a member convenor's row carries *Leave* after the start with no relocation. `constituted()` excludes the pre-start founding and `viewerIsMember()` excludes a clerk, so the two epochs and the two hats are already said by the predicate that was there.

## The text is the open card: 📝, edit mode, the riding tab, and gap sites (2026-08-29, backlog 204, plan 129)

Two complaints from live use (Ed, 2026-08-28): members do not realise the charter text can be clicked and typed into, and adding a clause at the end or between two clauses means editing a neighbour and pressing Enter (Q261). And 📄 *starting text* had always been confusing — a card in the constitution band *about* the text, standing apart from the text it governs, asking an OK nobody understood. Entry 204 is Ed's design, which **deliberately reverses entry 36** (📄's task as an acknowledgement, 2026-08-25, Q797–Q800) and keeps entry 56 (the column stays live until 🍾). The rules are SURFACE K31; this is why they are shaped as they are.

**Two modes rather than a card that opens and closes.** A race card or a band card *replaces* its paragraph and closes back into it; the text's paragraph is the whole column, so a card that opened and closed would swallow the document and give it back. What changes when you press 📝 is not what is on screen but what you may do to it — so the text is *always* the card, and the door is between reading and writing. Read mode has **no caret** because a caret is the offer of an act (2026-08-21's rule), and the complaint was that the offer went unnoticed: a column that only ever has a caret in edit mode makes entering edit mode the visible event. A click in read mode **beats the tab** and says nothing, on the palette's own terms — the ring is `room-pulse`'s gesture, an event and not a state, in the tab's own colour so the eye is led to the door; copy was declined (Ed: *no copy, ever*), as the `dead-click-nudge` declined it (Q653). A keystroke in read mode enters edit mode with the character applied, so a member who simply starts typing loses nothing to the mode (Q1085: the listener is the document's, since a non-editable column is not a keydown target, and it filters by reading position — nothing else focused, no card open, the selection in the column).

**The tab rides.** The 📝 tab is the only way into edit mode and the only way out, and a reader forty screens down a charter should not have to travel to the heading to find it. `position: sticky` in the section's gutter, and the tab is a direct child of `.doc` rather than of the band's row, because a sticky element rides only within its parent's box and the band's row ends where the prose begins. At rest it sits exactly where 📄's tab sat beside the charter heading — the same 30px-on-30px measurement setup.css records — and detached it wears the active treatment. **Q1087 answered by keeping one meaning**: M12's grow means *this is the open card's tab*, and in edit mode the text is the open card; a detached tab in read mode is that same tab having left its heading to stay with you, and giving it a second look would have been a fourth thing for the gutter to say. It lifts over the piles it passes and displaces none, being out of flow.

**The row is the proposal-row, not a toolbar.** Everything on the surface commits from one row (§9.1) and the text is no exception: 🗑️ at the very left, the commit at the very right greyed until something changed, the middle stating what will go — *n places changed*, in K15's own word for a site (Q1089: *sites* is engine vocabulary and never reaches a member). It sticks to the foot of the window because the viewport is the card — tab at its top edge, row at its bottom — and rests at the section's foot once that is on screen. Nothing about the commit changed: pressing it opens the editing card, where the rationale, the sign choice, the speaker's disc and the hold live exactly as entry 160 and K30 left them; post-🍾 its glyph follows entry 160 (✒️ under `MAY_PEN`, ✏️ otherwise), and K29's *the Text's pair is the editing card's* stands — one commit on the row, never two.

**Where 📄's OK went, and where the confirm went.** The OK was the confirm (`confirmStartingText`), and §9.0b makes the start wait on a confirmed decision. Ed's ruling (2026-08-29 21:20, Q1080): the founder's ✒️ on the row pre-🍾 is the confirm, every press, and 🍾 confirms whatever stands if nothing ever did — chosen over *🍾 stays held until one ✒️*, which would have made the row's ✒️ a task under another name. The confirm lives in `begin()` in the module (R-081, Q1081), not on the page's flush, because `begin` has three callers and only one of them is the founder's press. On the page the text is **settled from the save** (`settled()`'s own rule, Q1082): it is never a task, so nothing below it in `ORDER` waits on it and the live path needs no `S.seen` to rebuild it — the 🎩 lesson. `pwHasValue` keeps reading `textConfirmed` (Q1083): laying a power down still wants a set, and the text's set is its confirm.

**Two columns, one row helper (Q1088).** `syncCharter` mounts the charter from `constituted()`, so pre-🍾 the column is `#prose` with Q821's write channel and post-🍾 it is session.js's host — and the plan's host predicate had a pre-🍾 clause that could never fire. Ed chose the two-column reading: the page draws the tab, the lift and the row around `#prose` before the start, session.js draws them under the charter after it, and `proposalRowHtml` in session.js is the one helper both call. Mounting the charter from the save was the other reading and was declined as wider than the design: it rewrites the write channel, the stash restore and every walk that types into `#prose`.

**Gap sites (Q261).** A gap is the place between two clauses, or after the last: key `G<n>`, `n` the engine line the insertion goes before, read off the neighbour's line and never off the next rendered block (blank lines are lines the engine counts). The engine needed nothing — `Hunk { start === end }` is a pure insertion and does not conflict with a neighbour's rewrite — so the whole of it is on the page: Enter at the very end of an unmodified clause opens a draft on the gap after it, at the very start on the gap before it, mid-clause keeps the split; a gap site never merges with a neighbour, because joining it to the clause beside it would turn an insertion into that clause's rewrite; its card renders in the read side's existing `.insert-anchor` shape, which is what Q261 asked for a way to *create*. The trailing gap block is drawn only in edit mode (the closed page, the door's bars and the TOC never see it) and reuses the empty document's `blank` treatment with its own sentence (Q1090: the rule is the geometry, the sentences differ).

**What the empty column says (Q1084).** The grey invitation was keyed on 📄's turn; with no turn it is keyed on the column being the founder's and empty, until 🍾, and Q518's placeholder (answered the same evening) lands on that hook — the sentence there now is a holding one and says so in the CSS.

**Declined**: registers (one face throughout); a hover treatment; nudge copy; inline drafting (the draft rendered in the prose, the card deferred) — only what is above. **The walks moved with it**: `journey-walk` writes the text at the save through 📝 and the row, asserts the charter mounts in read mode and that 📝 lifts it, and gains `--new-clause`; `founding-walk`'s `afterTextOk` became `afterFirstPen`; `setup-probe`'s founding drives 📝 rather than an OK; `probe-coverage` exempts `text`, there being no card DOM to open. The founding golden, the copy golden and the probe references re-freeze with QA (`npm run qa:freeze`), not in the build.

**✒️ is the only save (Ed's QA, 2026-08-30).** Q821's write channel re-confirmed the pre-🍾 column on a debounce after the first ✒️ — every pause in typing was a `confirm-starting-text` — so the text was saved before the founder's hand reached the row, and `syncProseRow` greyed ✒️ as *Saved* the moment the column matched. Ed met it as a dead control: *I click 📝, write text, click 📝 again, and the text is saved. The ✒️ control does not respond* — the tooltip reading *Saved*. Three readings were put: ✒️ as *save and stop writing* over the auto-save; ✒️ as the only save; keep the mechanism and say it better. Ed chose the second: the stash still carries keystrokes until the first confirm, so a reload before anything was ever saved loses nothing; after it nothing is sent until ✒️ (every press) or 🍾 and ⏩, which confirm whatever stands (R-081). The accepted cost is a tab closed mid-edit after a first save losing what was typed since. Guard: `npm run journey`'s save step presses ✒️ on a changed column; `founding-walk` no longer waits for a debounce.

## 2026-08-31 — one card width, one tab column

**One card width, one tab column (Ed's QA, 2026-08-31: *cards in the central column are different widths, which means that tabs don't line up vertically — make them all the same as the wider width*).** Both facts were one asymmetry. A charter `.anch` hangs `--s3` left of its own text and a charter card runs a full measure-gutter past the text on each side; a band `.cpara` sat flush on the axis and its `.setupcard` overhung 14px left and nothing right (the 2026-08-18 fix for tabs touching the text, which stopped at 14 where the charter goes to 24). So the constitution's cards were 34px narrower than the charter's, off-centre against them, and every band tab — the pile at a paragraph's head, a member row's, the riding 📝 — stood 12px right of the column the charter's tabs make. The band now takes the charter's geometry wholesale rather than a parallel derivation: the open card's margins are the measure-gutter on **both** sides (the box `.sugg` already draws in the charter), which lands head, body and strip on the text axis by construction and **deletes** the two `14px - var(--s5)` compensations (the head's rtext and the body's) instead of re-deriving them; the closed tabs take the `14px + --s3` chipcol correction charter headings already take (Q897), on `.constsec .cpara > .chipcol`, `.constsec .memrow .chipcol` and `.ridetab .chipcol` — never on the strip's, which hangs off the `.headclause` and follows the card wherever the card is. In edit mode the riding 📝 additionally takes `.clausehead .achip`'s own −2px tuck-under, since the lifted text *is* the open card and every tab's right edge lands on the card's left edge (Ed, 2026-08-17); detached over the prose there is no card edge and it rests on the closed piles' own column. **Cost, accepted for uniformity**: the band's press now carries the charter's 2px sideways glyph move — the tuck-under trait `card-audit`'s P2 has always reported on every charter card — so P2 widened from the charter's 63 cards to the whole surface, and the switch pass P7 reports the same 2px on band-to-band switches. Uniform, not new. **Verified**: the audit census reads one box (478..1130, w652 at 1600×1000) and one open-tab x (436) across all eight walks and 270 card openings, where the band had read 488..1106 w618 tab@446; on the page every closed tab family — clauses, headings, the riding 📝 — measures one left edge, and the founder's walk and `spec-check` stay green. The probe's new DIFFs against the (already stale, pre-freeze) reference are geo-only on setup-side steps; they re-freeze with the batch's QA (`npm run qa:freeze`), not here.

**Tabs always tuck (Ed, 2026-08-31, answering (a) of three).** The tuck-under put `journey`'s edit-mode step 2px red — the walk had encoded *its gutter is the constitution's* (2026-08-30) as `rideRight === consRight`, written before the strip model reached the riding pile. Ed's ruling: the tuck wins, everywhere — the walk asserts `consRight + 2` now — and the whole editing pile tucks, ✒️ 🛡️ included, exactly as `.clausehead .achip` gives the −2px to resting strip tabs too (Ed's same message: *the ✒️ and 🛡️ tabs in the 📝 pile don't tuck when 📝 is active*). Declined alongside: reverting the 2px (📝 the one active tab short of its card) and removing the tuck surface-wide (undoes the 2026-08-17 seam decision; would have cleared card-audit's P2). The text card's own width was the same morning's third find: the edit-mode `::before` was inset to the *old* band-card box — a second copy of card geometry, drifted when the original moved — and its insets are 0 now, the painted card being the prose box itself.

## 2026-08-31 — the card pattern (Q1096–Q1102)

Ed, opening pass 4: *Decision cards are very inconsistent. There are special cases to deal with, but even so… We must be consistent or users will be confused.* His written target: standing text at the top, alternatives below with a hairline between and *Prefer this* under each (later clarified: radios, with a separate commit step), a rationale input unless the founder is setting for the first time, 🗑️ bottom-left and the commit family bottom-right, and member-related cards leading with the avatar-and-name list. Read against SURFACE §9/§9.1/§9.2 it split into restatements (K1, K12/C11, C4, the judgment lanes' own *Prefer this*), genuine amendments, and one on-paper contradiction (§9's table gave judgment cards no 🗑️ while C4 grants an exemption only to Y20's five). Seven questions were put one at a time; the rulings are SURFACE §9.3's CP1–CP7. What was declined, and why:

**CP1 (Q1096) — unify fully.** Declined: *settings keep lanepick* (two selection grammars is the very inconsistency complained of — a member meets click-the-sentence on settings and press-the-radio on texts); *layout-only unification* (cards that look alike but select differently is worse than cards that look different). Cost accepted: band cards grow a control per option, `lanepick` retires as a distinct control, all three goldens re-freeze.

**CP2 (Q1097) — *Prefer this* everywhere, against the recommendation.** The recommendation was a preference/consent split: the constitutional-motion card's *Keep what stands / I accept the change / Abstain* states a binding act where a preference binds nobody, and STYLE's title rules want the label to state the act. Ed chose uniformity; the consequence folded with it is that the binding nature of accepting a constitutional change must now be stated in the card's body copy, since the label no longer carries it. *Choose this / Chosen* on the power cards folds into *Prefer this / Preferred* the same way; K4's other-half rule (what stands stays visible, marked) survives with relabelled words.

**CP3 (Q1098) — rationale rides acts that propose or change.** Declined: judgment rationales (new mechanism, not styling — the engine records judgments as bare pairwise preferences, so a rationale needs a home in the log and an answer under §3.5 blindness before it can exist; filed as its own question if ever wanted) and a page-only note field (a field that goes nowhere invites writing for an audience that does not exist). Blind answers stay rationale-free — a rationale would leak what the blind collection seals.

**CP4 (Q1099) — Ed's own shape, better than the three offered.** Indifferent as a full option block — hairline like the others, **no text**, the radio itself labelled *Indifferent* in place of *Prefer this*. Declined: row placement beside 🗑️ (a radio among buttons, one exception to the block grammar); a block with *Prefer this* under an "Indifferent" text (you would be preferring indifference); a standalone third zone. The shape keeps the blocks perfectly uniform while the label states the act — the two goods the offered options traded against each other.

**CP5 (Q1100) — the commit list was illustrative; the 👑 question takes the pattern whole.** Ed: *My list was not exhaustive. Sometimes there are multiple options, e.g. ✏️ and ✒️, or ✒️ and 🏛️, for a founder who is also a member. 🛡️ commits on 👑* — refined the same day into the full shape: *🗑️ should be in the bottom left to close the card, and both 🛡️ and ✒️ in the bottom right to refuse or accept.* So 🪶 🍾 📨 and the Take-verbs stand as §9.1 has them, K29's pairs are confirmed as the pattern's own case, and the 👑 card sheds its word-buttons entirely: 🗑️ closes it pending (Y20's 👑 exemption struck at the build), ✒️ accepts — the pen is what makes it pass — and 🛡️ refuses, the one place the veto acts wearing the veto's glyph. The counter-argument (a refusal overruling a passed motion is the moment that most deserves plain words) was put and outweighed: the two reserved powers *are* the two answers, which states the act better than the words did — the founder is shown exactly which retained power each press exercises.

**CP6 (Q1101) — the list is the head.** Today a decision card *replaces* its paragraph, so opening ❌ could hide the very list of people being acted on — likely the observed inconsistency. Declined: opening below the subsection (breaks the one opening-geometry promise the surface makes everywhere); keeping as-is. Cost accepted: the list is drawn twice in spirit (subsection closed, head open) and a long roster makes a tall card. `adm:` keeps its one-applicant head, being about one person.

**CP7 (Q1102) — C4 wins.** 🗑️ on every card but Y20's five, judgment cards included; on a judgment it clears the selection and closes. The near-duplication with closing-by-tab was weighed against one learnable rule — a member should never have to study which cards carry the bin — and lost. Whether the built page actually lacks 🗑️ there (the table's claim) is deliberately left to the census: §9's rows keep describing the page as built, and move with the fixes.

**The pass's shape**: fold the target first (this entry and §9.3), then a census — `card-audit` grown a grammar recorder measuring every card in every reachable state against CP1–CP7, with probe-coverage-style completeness so an unopened card cannot read as clean — then the reading as a pass-4 artifact (findings vs questions, Q1103–Q1115 reserved), then fixes as per-family batches, then the recorder kept as the standing guard.

**The census's answers (same day).** The census ran the same afternoon — card-audit's existing payload already carried buttons, radios and strings, so the recorder was a reducer, not a tool — and Ed answered the artifact in one paste-back. Every finding stands: the band takes the block grammar, the power cards relabel, the judgment cards gain 🗑️ and the Indifferent block (the census proved the C4 contradiction was page drift — no judgment card has a 🗑️), the doors head with their people, and the two-size commit split (band word-commits at `--t-cap` via session-view.html's `.setupcard .btn:not(.glyphbtn)` override, the charter's at `--t-ui`) is fixed to `--t-ui` both sides. **F-F resolved as an exemption**: *📧 can be used twice* — the stranger's login and your own email card share the glyph deliberately; the audit's G2 rule takes the recorded exemption rather than a new glyph. Two answers went **against the recommendation**, both widening CP1. **Q1103 (b)**: 🍾's power table is not exempt — it becomes the surface's one **two-column** card, a ✒️ column and a 🛡️ column of option blocks, retiring the `switch` control (and superseding the plan-queue backlog entry that asked for the lanepick-drawn toggles to become proper switches — blocks, not switches, is the ruling now). **Q1104 (b)**: the numeric settings are not exempt either — the named rungs return as option blocks whose text is the rule as it would stand, `meaningOf`'s sentence with the number stated (*"Nearly all the members must be sure a proposal is better for it to pass (80%)"*), with *A number of my own* as the last block carrying the field. The pattern's reach after both: every choice on the surface is option blocks with *Prefer this*, no exceptions by control kind, only Y20's five by card. The three recommended-and-taken answers became CP8 (the row states the act, the title the state) and CP9 (a card that can never commit shows no commit), and CP7's site-sub-block clarification.

**Plan A lands the block grammar on the band (2026-08-31, same evening).** One restructure in four renderers — `opt` and `ansRow` (setup.js), `pctRung` and `consentPicks` (session-view.html) — plus the admit lanes, an Indifferent block in `motionBody` (out of the ordinary motion's commit row), the power cards' relabel, 🍾's table as the two-column blocks, and 🌡️'s rungs as sentences (`BAR_RUNGS.sentence`; 🪜's starting rungs deliberately keep the short labels — a *passing* sentence would misstate a bar that only opens the vote). The `.switch` control and its CSS went with its one user; rhythm moved off `.choice`'s flex gap onto `.pick + .pick` margins so bare sequences and wrapped ladders read one gap (audit P5). What the build taught: **the option's name moved off the button, and everything that read it there broke silently** — journey's `options`/`delegLabels`/`pickOption` found every rung named *Prefer this*, always clicked the first, and stalled at ⏰ where the first rung needs a date; the fix reads `.opttext` with the button as the textless-block fallback. Found beside it, pre-existing: slider-walk still asserted *In a room of one* five months of copy after entry 215 renamed the room to the membership (slider-walk is not in CI's walks job); and the setup-probe's four dead 💤 steps reproduce on the pre-change tree (stash-verified) — both are instrument debts, the second filed to plan D. Accepted deviation: the two-column 🍾 card puts two radio columns on one card, so audit P1 reads two left edges on `founding·begin` — the ruling's own cost, to be EXEMPTed with plan D's grammar guard.

**Plan B lands on the charter (same evening).** `commitRowHtml` (cards.js) puts Indifferent in a textless `.vinblock` under the lanes' own hairline and 🗑️ at the row's far left — `clear-close` in session.js clears an uncommitted pick and closes, a cast vote staying, the bin putting back un-actioned input only (C4). The band's `--t-cap` button shrink (session-view's `.setupcard .btn:not(.glyphbtn)`) is overridden for `.commitrow .btn`, so a commit word is `--t-ui` on both surfaces (census F-E); `.rsub`'s 2px joins the grid (F-G). **Two of the census's readings dissolved on contact**: the judged card's *Recorded — choose again to change it* was already the ✓'s `title`, never its label — the census's `foot` field falls back to the title when a label is a drawn glyph, so CP8's charter half was built all along; and F-G's second nit, `.pick > .inner > .choice`'s −2px, is the deliberate optical takeback that keeps nested radios on the card's left edge (P1) — fixing it would trade a 2px grid deviation for a visible misalignment, so it stays and plan D's guard EXEMPTs it.

**Plan C lands on the doors, the lock and the 👑 (same evening).** Both crown cards shed their word-buttons: 🗑️ closes with the question kept pending (Y20's 👑 clause struck), 🛡️ refuses and ✒️ accepts, each stating its act in the title — the founder is shown exactly which retained power each press exercises. 🎩 after 🍾 shows no commit at all (CP9): the permanently dark ✒️ promised a thaw that never comes, where a closed document's cards already committed nothing (powers-walk's 19 of 19). The doors head with their people (CP6): `doorPeople` puts the invitees on ✉️ and the proposed-for-removal on ❌ above the rule sentence in the one head, so opening ❌ never hides the people it acts on; an empty pile says so in a quiet line. Q1105 dissolved like B's *Recorded* finding: the direct ✉️'s row label was already the drawn ✓ — "Done" was its title, which is where C4 now points. And one more walk taught the block lesson: applicants-walk read lane names off `.lanepick span:last-child` and saw *Preferred* everywhere; it reads `.opttext` now, like journey's three helpers — all three prices green.

**Plan D closes the pass (same night): the census instrument keeps the guard.** `rulesFor` gains the pattern's three standing rules — CP7 (🗑️ leads every row that commits anything besides OK; Y20's five stay out by shape, an OK-only row asking nothing), CP2 (a dotted radio says *Prefer this / Preferred / Indifferent* and nothing else) and CP8 (no state-worded commit labels) — and the closing run is silent on all three. The exemptions Ed ruled are in the instrument with their reasons beside them: G2 skips 📧 (F-F, *used twice* deliberately), P1 skips 🍾 (the one two-column card), S1 skips the `.choice` −2px takeback, and B6 stops comparing glyph-only labels across surfaces (B5's own silhouette rule — the charter's 19.2px 🗑️ against the band's 14px is two boxes, not two sizes). Coverage grew by seeding rather than sampling: 🌍 carries both the post-start set (E5's news) and the crown-parked motion — the one setting ⏩ leaves in the founder's hand, which is why a carried motion parks there and nowhere else on the file page — and 👤 carries the mid-flight consent under a second mover (one 🏛️ per member, §9.6, found by the seed's own refusal). The applicant seat is EXEMPT, not fixed: `allApplicants` reads the remote view, so the file page can never seat one, and applicants-walk owns that coverage on the live path. T5's false positives went with the same lesson every walk learned — the option's name is the block's, so the instrument's `strings.options` reads `.opttext` now. What stays unmeasured is named in pass-4.md with its reason, none of it silent.

## 2026-08-31 — Ed's QA of the card-pattern batch: the register returns, the grants go quiet

**CP2 re-ruled the same day it was ruled.** The morning's Q1097 chose one radio label everywhere, *against* the recommended preference/consent split; Ed's evening QA reverses it to the split — *"it should be Prefer this / Preferred when it's something you're voting on; if you're the only person who decides then it should be Choose this / Chosen"* — which is also the 2026-08-27 power-card register (*choose* a rule, *prefer* a proposal) that plan A had flattened. The line falls on **who decides**, not on what kind of card: the founder's settings, the power cards, 🌡️/🪜's rungs, 🍾's Kept/Laid-down table and the delegate rung take *Choose this / Chosen*; judgments, the admit lanes, consent answers and the composer keep *Prefer this / Preferred*. Two cases sit on the line and are asked rather than guessed: the blind answer rungs (your answer is yours alone; the rule it produces is the room's — Q1110) and nothing else — the sign-control and Indifferent already name the act, a third register that stands. `card-audit`'s CP2 lens admits both vocabularies and still refuses everything else.

**The grant cards lose their lockline.** Ed: *"Grant queue-cards have text ('You hold the pen' etc), please remove this."* The text was `gateBody`'s lockline printing the card's `done` sentence once open — a state line restating what the wallet says the moment the grant is taken, on a card whose take-sentence already states the whole ask. Gates keep theirs: a gate's lockline is what the card is waiting for, which nothing else says. The `done` strings went with their one consumer; `VALUE`'s grant entries stay, feeding nothing visible today, because `clauseText`'s DECIDED-miss fallback reads `value()` and a true sentence there beats an empty one. And the pair stop being possessives — **The Pen, The Shield** (the ✒️-commit tooltip's *your pen* with them): the object exists apart from whoever holds it, which is the whole point of a power you can lay down. Whether 🏛️ follows (*The Voice* reads like a broadcaster) is Q1111.

**The delegate rung draws the hairline.** Q761 set the second radio group apart with a bigger gap when options were pills; once CP1 gave every block a hairline, apart-with-no-line read as unattached (Ed: *"doesn't have a hairline"*). The rung keeps its `--s4` apartness and gains the same `border-top` the blocks share — the two statements (*apart from the values* and *one of the card's choices*) turn out to be compatible, one on the margin and one on the line.

**What Ed's 🪪/🤝 finding actually names is Q1109.** The two cards conform to CP1 as built — plan A restated only the numeric rungs as the rule-they-would-stand (Q1104 (b)); the enumerated class kept label + explainer + why + title-head, which SURFACE §9's setting row itself prescribed. The gap is the ruling's reach, and the scope of closing it (clause-head, constitution sentences as option text, the helper prose gone) is asked as Q1109 rather than built on spec.

**Q1109 answered (a) within the hour and built the same night: the founder's decision cards read as the document.** The clause sentences were lifted out of `DECIDED` into shared tables (`ADM_RULE`, `REMOVAL_RULE`, `AUTH_RULE`, `JUDG_RULE`, `CHAMBER_RULE`, `APPL_RULE`, `ENDING_NEVER`) so the option a founder reads and the paragraph the document states are one string; the ten enumerated bodies dropped their `why` paragraphs and per-option explainers; 🎩 and 👥's form pair, having no clause to borrow, got clause-voice sentences written fresh (STYLE audit item 74, below). The head half turned out to be **already built**: `headFor` returns the clause for any settled card open included, and "the title while open" was only ever true of a card nothing stands on — SURFACE's row now says so. **Deliberately not done tonight**: the value labels' other homes (the member's ladder, the composer's `MVAL`/`PROPOSE` pair that `checkComposer` asserts both ways, the settled strip, the readbacks — item 72's twelve sites) keep the T41 gradient labels; whether they follow is Q1112, asked rather than swept at midnight, because item 72 measured strip widths before freezing and that diligence deserves daylight. The reading that keeps T5 whole meanwhile: the founder's radio no longer shows the value's *label* at all — it shows the *rule* — so the label still has one spelling everywhere a label is shown.

## 2026-09-01 — T43: the constitution speaks for itself

**The principle, in Ed's words**: *the document's constitution speaks for itself, and shouldn't need extra explanation… we can start by not sneaking explanation elsewhere.* Folded as STYLE **T43**, with the boundary drawn where his surveyed items drew it: a rule the document states is never restated beside itself; what may stand near a rule is the document's own sentence (Q1109) or a consequence computed from the room (`meaningOf`, T39); cards may still explain **tasks** — what a press does, what is waited on — that being the card's voice about an act.

**Built under it the same night**: the power cards' `PWWHY` paragraphs deleted entire (the head and the two blocks already state the rule both ways — the why was the older wording standing inches away, the exact drift the 2026-08-22 veto-vocabulary entry had already trimmed once); 🌡️ 🪜 ⏱️'s whys likewise, with ⏱️'s clause absorbing the one fact its why alone carried (*A proposal costs one ✏️…*) under Ed's explicit licence to extend clause sentences; and the delegated-pending state became a clause in Ed's own sentence — *The Founder is letting the membership decide this rule themselves (x of y have answered so far)* — replacing *The Founder has delegated to members to decide…*. His draft's verb was *voted*; built as *answered* because every count over blind answers on the surface says answered (T5's one-word-per-act), flagged to him in chat. 🌍's delegated form keeps Q618's interim visibility sentence, taking the same parenthetical.

**Your Consent (Q1111).** Ed floated *Your Veto*; declined on two grounds he accepted by picking consent: **veto is already the shield's word** (🛡️'s tab is *Does the Founder Have a Veto?* — one word answering for two different powers is the vocabulary form of the name-two-things-answer-to gotcha), and **the token says yes as often as no** — it is flown to accept a member as much as to refuse one, so *veto* names its dark half only. *Your Consent* is SPEC's own word for the rule the token serves. Surface strings only: `grant-voice`, `voicewallet`, `voiceHost` and SURFACE §7's `🏛️ voice` row label stay as code and mechanism names, like `roster` and `convenor` before them. The standalone clause was upgraded while touched: *Each member holds one voice in every constitutional question.* described an arrangement; *Nothing constitutional passes without every member’s consent.* states the rule with its teeth.

**CP9's closed half, finished (2026-09-01).** Plan C had recorded the closed-document half as needing nothing — *a closed document's cards already committed nothing (powers-walk's 19 of 19)* — and SURFACE §9.3 kept CP9 marked **Unbuilt**, which was the more honest of the two. The claim rested on the wrong instrument: powers-walk's `pen` probe is `[data-confirm]:not([disabled])`, so it reads *no **live** commit* and a permanently dark one passes it silently — exactly the thing CP9 exists to remove. Two sites were still drawing one. On the band, `founderHandOff` excludes the power tabs and the two doors **by name**, so those fell past the bin-alone branch to the fall-through's ✒️, dark for ever because `mayPenOn` carries `docOpen()`; the fall-through now takes a bin alone once `cs.closed`, placed **below** the news branch so 🥂's OK survives — `acknowledgeClose` being the one command the close does not refuse, and that OK the signature. On the charter, every judgment card on the closed page still drew its ✓ — greyed where nothing was picked, and **live** where something was, which is Q470's *asks nothing* broken rather than CP9's dark commit. The fix reuses what was already there: a locked card renders 🗑️ alone, so a closed document simply locks. It could not ride `closedMode`, which means *the wallets are gone* and which the host also sets for the stranger's door where nothing has closed; `docClosed` is its own fact, set from `cs.closed`, a second name for a second thing on the file that already carries the two-things-one-name post-mortem. Measured on card-audit's `closed` walk: 26 judgment cards went from 🗑️ · ✓ to 🗑️, the four sealed records kept their OK. What is **not** touched: the deadlock desk's dark ✏️ on a closed page (`race-sanctions`), which is the proposal row's own object and K17–K18's rule, not the commit row's.

**Q1112 answered (b) and filed, not built**: clause sentences in every label home — ladder, composer, strip, readbacks — extending the clauses where a value lacks one. Batch-sized (STYLE audit item 72's twelve producing sites — below, its strip-width measurements to redo), so it went to plan-queue's backlog (entry 262) for a batch with its own QA sitting rather than a midnight sweep. **The package-level `clauseOf` move stays deferred** (survey item 10): Ed declined to rule (*I don't feel qualified*), so the recommendation stands — no second consumer exists until the closing record wants the sentences, and architecture without a customer is how files rot.

## 2026-09-01 — a gate never withholds from the seat that set it (SURFACE Y27)

**The symptom** (Ed, over a dev.docs.vote ladder document at `session`): as the founder, the rail draws no open race item at all — only news, filed ⏳ entries, motions and 👑 — while the view is serving four `raceCards` and seven clauses, four of them unjudged. As a member of the same document the two gate cards arrive, and the OK on ⚖️ fills the rail immediately. Reproduced here on a local ladder document, founder seat, fresh browser profile.

**Three things withheld it, and any one of them is enough.** `mayJudge()` has been `canJudge() && viewerIsMember() && acked('canjudge')` since Q448/453, and `acked` reads `S.okd`, which is per browser, per document, per seat. So the founder can only reach judging by pressing an OK on a card that must first be *reachable*: 💡 and ⚖️ sit below ✒️ in `ORDER` and the pen's grant **blocks** it, so an unacknowledged pen hides both gates outright (this is what the local reproduction hit — `canpropose vis=0 … blk=1` on ✒️); a gate is staged behind owed news besides (`staged`/`owedNews`), so a founder owed a pile of `res-*` resolutions or a 👑 batch is served no gate either; and because the press is remembered only in `grantsKey()`, a new browser, a cleared profile or a second device puts the founder back behind the same card. The ladder's server-side `give-ok` at the `ready` rung does not touch that store, which is why the ⏭ path and a fresh profile disagree.

**The ruling** is C8's own test turned on the seat that made the decision: *were you here when it was set?* — and for the founder the answer is *I set it*. Both gates open on 🍾, the founder's own press, whose card states the pair as part of its batch (C8a). So `acked()` is satisfied for the founder on `canpropose` and `canjudge` with no card and no press, and the three other places that asked *has this been acknowledged* about a gate — `settled`, `mustAct`, `news` — ask `acked()` too, so the founder's gate reads settled rather than standing as a task that withholds nothing. A member is untouched in every particular: they were not here when it was set, and the gate is exactly the thing that tells them.

**Rejected: making the exemption conditional on nothing being delegated.** The plan's ruling carried a caveat — *where a gate's question was delegated, the founder answered blind like every member and stays owed the outcome, no exemption* — and the first build implemented it by asking whether any decision the gate waits on was the room's (⚖️'s `ceremony`, 💡's text and start). It is wrong twice. A gate is not a setting: neither key is in `DELEGABLE` or in the catalogue, so there is no delegated gate to except, and the caveat has no referent. And read as *the questions beneath it*, it fires on no real document — the founding ceremony delegates something by definition, the ladder's own room holding three of ⚖️'s six — so it would have left the reported defect standing while looking like a fix. The boundary the caveat is really about is untouched and needs no code: a question the founder answered blind is still owed to them as that question's own `res-<key>` resolution news, on its own card, which is most of what was already in the founder's rail.

**The second defect: a boolean where the rail wanted a sentence, and it took the whole rail with it.** Seeding the founder's `draft:grants:<slug>:founder` key by hand emptied the rail completely — every item, not just the gates. The cause is not the grants store. `itemsFromView` built each live item with `shifted: !!r.shifted`, following the server's flag (*a judgment of mine locked by a ground shift*); `renderQueue` has five readers that only ask whether `shifted` is truthy and one that **prints** it as the entry's tooltip, the fixture having always supplied the story there. `esc` throws on a non-string, and it throws in the middle of building the rail's HTML — so one shifted judgment anywhere in your feed cost you the news, the motions, the ⏳ entries and the 👑 as well. Seeding the acks only made it visible, by letting the shifted item reach the rail at all; it is reachable by any seat that has judged a race whose ground then moved, which is E16's ordinary case, and it is the reason the gate fix alone would still have shown the founder nothing. Fixed on both sides, deliberately: the live item carries the sentence, and the renderer no longer lets a data shape it was handed kill the surface.

**What moved as a consequence**, for whoever reads the next freeze: the founder's 💡 and ⚖️ clauses read settled from 🍾 instead of standing as tasks, and the founder's ✏️ wallet arrives with no press and so no pencil storm (SURFACE E8). `founding-golden` and the setup-probe references move with them.

## 2026-09-01 — 📝 is the door (SURFACE K13 amended, entry 136)

**The ruling.** Put the choice between *typing should still work* and *design moved*, Ed answered **"Design moved: click/📝 first."** The page had been right since backlog 204 and the spec had not caught up: `design/session.js`'s `beforeinput` handler refuses a keystroke outside edit mode, deliberately and with a comment saying so, while SURFACE K13 still promised that the same keystroke would open the door for you.

**What the old rule was, and why it went.** Always-on-typing came from the composer's founding idea — *you compose by editing the charter*, so there is no separate editor to go to and no button to find. The read-mode keystroke was the strongest form of that: you put a caret in a clause, typed, and the editing card assembled itself around the character you had already committed to. What it cost was the thing the door buys back. A column that takes a caret everywhere cannot be *read*: a stray keypress, a paste, an IME, a browser extension, a phone's autocorrect all became proposals-in-waiting, and the page had to intercept every one of them to stay honest — the refusal, not `contenteditable`, was always the lock. With two modes the reader's column is inert and the writer's is live, and which one you are in is a thing you did rather than a thing you have to remember. The interception survives whole; it now lives one press further in.

**Nothing in the mechanism moved**: the editing card, draft sites, the proposal row, the gap sites of Q261 and the one-draft-at-a-time rule (K14–K26) are untouched, and 📝's own rules were already written as K31. K13 was the only sentence that still described the old door, plus one clause inside K31 and the *opened by* cell of §9's `editing` row.

**What it cost to find.** Three instruments had gone stale against a page that was right, and CI had been red on all three since the card-pattern pushes of 2026-08-31 — a red build that says *the page is wrong* when the page is the only thing that is right is worse than no build at all, because it trains you to read the red as noise. `journey-walk`'s ordinary typing step drove the retired read-mode door while its own `--new-clause` branch had already been modernised, so the walk contradicted itself in the same function. The setup-probe's four 💤 steps were dead for a reason nobody had guessed: the scenario picks a **shape**, and a *meeting* `hides: ['lapse']` by Ed's own ruling — *a decision nobody has* — so the card the probe was asking for could not exist. The founding now takes **custom**, the one shape that hides nothing and pre-sets nothing, which is what the scenario's own header had claimed all along.

**And two label-shaped traps, both the same trap.** `journey-walk` held a frozen map of the five 👤 rung labels; Ed's copy sweeps turned every rung into a clause sentence, the map matched nothing, and the walk quietly took the first option on the card and then reported the missing sign control as the page's fault. Fixing the wording would have been fixing the symptom: the label is now read off the card by `data-val`, which CP1 deliberately left on the button, and a rung the card does not offer is a FAIL line rather than a fallback. Underneath it was a second one — the picker cut every label to 48 characters for the log, and as sentences 👤's `sealed` and `sealedElective` share their first sixty-four. Matching is exact now and cutting is the printing's job. This is entry 87's delegate rung and CLAUDE.md's own *a walk that identifies an option by the button's text* gotcha, arriving for the third time; the general lesson is that **a walk may print words and must not decide on them**.

**One measurement was not stale, only taken in the wrong place.** `journey`'s edit-mode step read the riding tab 81px below the document's first line and blamed the page. The tab rides with the reader by design (K31, `position: sticky`), so *rests level with the first line* is only a claim about the rest position; measured from wherever the walk's previous steps had scrolled to, it was reading the sticky clamp. The step scrolls to the top before measuring, and the page was never wrong.

## The watch-half retires, and the strip with it (2026-09-02 pm, Ed's QA of the rebuilt sheet — Q1176)

**What stood.** Once a delegated question closed, the card grew a second half
under its own body: *What the membership said*, the distribution strip (the
shape of what people asked for, without names — `distHtml`, and 🌡️'s rung
strip `rungStripHtml` off the room's real answers), the *Answered n of n*
line, the taken line and the meaning line. While it still collected, the same
half showed pips and the running count. One implementation (`watchBody` in
setup.js), appended under three different upper halves.

**What Ed ruled.** Remove all of it, on every settled delegated card, the
running count included — his framing for the whole round being *I am trying
to strip copy right back … using the clause text to explain everything as
much as possible*. Provenance survives as the standing block's own radio,
*Chosen by the membership*, drawn disabled at full strength (the locked-card
rule); the counts move to 🍾 as one sentence per still-collecting question
(*X out of Y of the membership have voted on whether…*, subject derived from
the `DECIDING` table so it cannot drift); and the blindness story — the other
thing the watch half used to carry — returns with 🍾's redesign (Q1169,
backlog 269).

**What was lost, knowingly.** A member no longer sees the *shape* of the
room's answers anywhere on the card — the strip's whole argument was that a
consent rule's number is one person's and the strip showed how far it sat
from the rest. If that account is wanted back, it belongs to the 🍾 redesign
or the record, not to the settled card. 🌡️'s method note also left the
member's read-only path with the watch half (it rode `withMethod`); the
answer card and the founder's card still carry it, so the `/pairwise` link
survives where the number is chosen.

**Code.** `watchBody`, `distHtml` and `rungStripHtml` are deleted, not
stranded; the card literals keep their fixture `dist`/`taken` fields, now
unread. The chosen-radio provenance is `chosenRadio` in session-view.html,
worn by the settled head (room-settled option-block cards), the parked 👑
pair and the record card.

## Card review round 3 (2026-09-05, Q1181–Q1188 and readings 1189–1194)

Ed's forty-four notes on the re-captured sheet, under the same framing as
round 2 — *strip copy right back, communicate through consistency and careful
use of words, using the clause text to explain everything*. The rules land in
SURFACE §9, §9.1 and §9.3, STYLE T48 and audit item 82 (below), and SPEC §9.7 rule 3
(R-087). The reasons, in the order the questions were asked.

**🍾's power table: six blocks with glyph toggles, not twelve radios and not
a table** (Q1181). The two-column form CP1 gave it — a ✒️ column and a 🛡️
column of *Kept* / *Laid down* option blocks — was the surface's one card
that did not read as a card: three rows × two columns × two radios is twelve
controls and twenty-four words for six binary facts, and the words are the
ones the surface uses nowhere else. Ed's own reading was that the switches it
replaced were better and that something better still might exist. What the
card is actually saying is six sentences of the constitution — *the Founder
may amend the Text at will*, and its five siblings — so each becomes an
option block stating the **kept** rule as a clause, with the power's own
glyph standing where the radio would sit: plain for kept, wearing the
wallets' `--slash` strike for laid down. The glyph is already the surface's
word for that power in five other places (the wallet, the tab, the commit,
the mark, the clause), and the strike is already its word for *not held*
(§7.1), so nothing new is learned to read it. Six blocks is half the
controls, no register words at all, and the same grammar as every other
card. Rejected by construction: keeping the table (the note that opened the
question), and toggles with *Kept* / *Laid down* labels beside them, which
would have kept the vocabulary that made it read as a form.

**The consent card takes the settled card's shape** (Q1182). The specimen was
the settled setting card *while a constitutional motion is in flight on it*,
and it carried a *Re-opened…* paragraph, a count line, the blind sentence,
three bare-word blocks each with an explainer, a *🗑️ Withdraw* and an
unlabelled commit — every one of them a thing rounds 1 and 2 removed from
some other card. Ed's *this doesn't conform to the pattern at all* is
therefore a census finding, not a taste: the card had simply not been visited.
It is the settled card with one more block, so it is drawn as one — the
standing rule, the proposed rule with its proposer's sealed rationale,
Abstain as a textless block on CP4's placement — and the register names the
**act** rather than the preference, because *Keep this* and *Prefer this* are
what the two blocks mean when a rule is being replaced. The count goes with
the rest of the watch half (Q1176) and the blindness story belongs to 🍾's
redesign (Q1169). **The mover's 🗑️ stays, wordless**: Ed's *no "withdraw"* was about the
word on the button, not the act (corrected the same night) — the mover's
🗑️ at the very left still withdraws and hands the 🏛️ back, and T47
strips its word there — and on the ordinary motion's card too, Ed
closing the exception the same night so the two motion cards match.

**And the commit is 🏛️** (Q1182's second half, Ed making his own earlier
sentence literal). SURFACE §7 had said *the founding answers are a kind of
🏛️* since the wallets were designed, while the cards committed answers with
✓ — the mark for *this binds nobody but me*. An answer to a constitutional
question binds the document: it is a member spending their consent, which is
exactly what the 🏛️ wallet holds one of. So 🏛️ commits every answer to a
constitutional question — the founding blind answer and the consent answer
alike — and ✓ is left to ordinary judgments and the cards about yourself.
C4's sentence is the amendment; the raise was already 🏛️, so the glyph now
means one thing on this surface rather than two thirds of one.

**The stranger's door prints the settled card** (Q1183). *Set to … / Set by
the founder when the document was made.* was written before the settled card
existed and survived because no walk seats a stranger at a paragraph tab. It
tells a stranger something the constitution's own clause already tells them,
in a second vocabulary, and it is the only card on the surface with a shape
of its own for no reason. Since `hydrateFromModule` already prints what the
module holds through the member surface's own mapping (Y15), the door can
open the settled card read-only: the standing rule with its provenance radio,
the power and record tabs in the strip, and a close-only OK. One card fewer,
and a stranger reads what a member reads.

**No release card at 🍾** (Q1184) — the reasoning is R-087; in surface terms
it is the same *three cards for one press* finding that A5 keeps making about
words, made about cards.

**The record card loses its head** (Q1186). Its head repeated the value the
blocks beneath already carried, in the short label form (*Anyone with the
link*, *82% sure at the end*) that A3 was cutting everywhere else — so
removing the label form removed the head's whole content, and with it the two
hairlines that bracketed nothing (Q1173's general rule). What is left is what
a record is: a date, an outcome, the two rules, who chose, and why. **Passed
and rejected are one shape** because the difference between them is which
block wears the provenance radio and which wears the rationale — not a
different card.

**Provenance on every standing rule** (Q1188). CP2's third form was drawn
only where the *membership* chose the value, so a founder-set rule — the
common case, and the whole of a document before the start — had a bare block
and the reader had to infer who set it from the absence of a label. One
wording covers both eras (*Chosen by the Founder ✒️*), because the era is not
what the reader is asking: they are asking whose rule this is. The record
card's *Chosen by Founder Action ✒️* was a second spelling of the same fact
and goes.

**The tense reversal** (Q1185). Q1150 chose *the membership are deciding* to
say the collection is running now; Ed's own sentences on 🌍 twice read *will
decide*, and the reason is the reader: a founder meeting the delegate rung is
choosing what *will* happen, not being told what is happening, and the same
sentence is read on a card where nothing has been collected yet. Naming both
answers on the binaries is the same instruction as A3 — a sentence that names
one alternative describes a choice the reader cannot see the shape of. The
ladders and the numbers have no pair to name, so they keep a one-clause
subject; that asymmetry is deliberate and is why the ruling names the five.

## Quorum is the adoption floor; the freeze and sign-out retire (2026-09-06, Q1196–Q1199)

Ed opened the session with a proposal to remove 👥 altogether: *I have
realised that I misunderstood what Quorum does. I don't think we need it; the
functionality I want is covered by Lapse and Leave, and we won't have "Sign
Out". I think we should set it to 0 and then remove it from the surface and
path. Fewer options is good!* He was told that 👥 did two jobs. The first was
the **freeze** (SPEC §9.5 as it stood): when the counted base — E minus the
members who had signed out abstaining — fell below quorum, the document parked
its races and cut the record until enough people returned. That was the job he
meant, and it was already nearly dead: sign-out never had a surface — no card,
no control, no copy ever offered *holding* or *abstaining* to a member — so the
only way a real document could freeze was a fixed count larger than its roster,
which the 👥 meaning line already described in words. The second was the
**adoption floor** (§4.2, §8.2): `F = max(Q, min(⌈E/3⌉, F_max))`, the number of
distinct members who must have judged a race before it may adopt — the one job
Lapse and Leave do nothing about, since they remove the absent from E and say
nothing about how many of the present must have been heard. Offered four
options, he chose: **keep 👥 as the floor, remove the freeze** — the card stays
and its copy says plainly what it does, sign-out and the freeze go, `/pairwise`
is corrected, and the form-and-number exception (Q1162) stays with the card.
The mechanism reason is R-088: the freeze and lapse pulled opposite ways (*stop
until they return* against *carry on without them*), and a document that had
consented to 💤 was being asked to do both about the same quiet member.

He then found where the misreading had come from. `design/pairwise.html`, under
*Nobody has to be present at once*, said that 👥 *asks a different question:
whether enough of the membership is still here for the document to go on at
all. It is about the membership being present, never about how many votes one
proposal has* — the last clause flatly false against §4.2, and contradicting the
card's own meaning line beneath it (*at least q of you must have voted on a
change before it can pass*). Ed: *Then the explainer is wrong I think!* It was,
and it is the product's own text that taught him the wrong quorum (Q1198). The
parenthesis now says what the quorum is: *the floor under all of this: the
number of members who must have voted on a change before it can pass, however
sure the document already is. It never decides a proposal; it only says how
many people the document must have heard from first.* The paragraph after it,
*An absent member is not a vote against*, was read against §8.2 and left alone:
a race short of the floor waits and degrades to backlog at the close, and the
absent decide nothing, which is what it says.

Two readings were built as resolved rather than asked, since each was the
smaller change and Ed had not overruled them in QUESTIONS.md. **The topbar's
*quorum n of E* stays** (Q1197): `renderClock` prints `cs.v.floor`, which *is*
the floor, and Q860 had already made it a sentence about a decision rather than
about the room. **The clause sentence stays** (Q1199): *Quorum is n of the
membership.* keeps *Quorum* a noun that plainly wants a number (STYLE §4), and
the meaning line beneath it is where *what it does* is said (T39) — three of its
branches had ended in *the document freezes*, and every branch now ends in the
floor. Rejected: making the clause sentence carry the floor itself, which would
have moved one sentence into four homes (the composer's block, `copy.js`, the
clause and the meaning line) to say what the line beneath already says.

What the mechanism keeps for the record: `signed-out`, `frozen` and `thawed`
stay in the event union and replay as no-ops, because a log written before v0.99
may carry them and a hash-chained file is never patched; `legacy-events.test.ts`
builds one and loads it. The golden walk lost its sign-out and, with it, the
return that had nothing left to revive — two entries, not one — and
`founding-v0.jsonl` was regenerated in step, since Q767 derives it from the walk
beside it. Q463 (d) had named *the freeze alarm* as one of two mails that exist
by necessity; it no longer exists, and Q463 is a design pass of its own.

## The card is a deck, and the ⏳ card is your ledger (2026-09-06, Q1200–Q1201)

Ed: *The reason I wanted to use Bradley-Terry is for when there are many
alternatives to the same clause, we have a pairwise system. Come to think of
it, I haven't been served multiple pairs from one clause yet.* He had not been,
and the cause was the page, not the engine. `Session.feed()` deals a hand of up
to ten cards and excludes every pair the member has already judged on the
current ground (`bestPairFor`, SPEC §8.3); §8.3b even assumes the member is
served pair after pair from one race, since a deadlock is disclosed only once
the race has *nothing left to ask you*. The page took the first served card
touching each race (`cards.findIndex`), mapped the server's per-race `judged`
flag — *any standing vote of mine on this race* — to `state: 'deciding'`, and
kept its provisional `resolved` / `verdicts` / `picked` / `committed` maps keyed
by item id, which is the race id. So one comparison per member per race, for
the life of the race, whatever the engine was holding; the rival ranking
Bradley–Terry is there for rested on almost nothing.

**Three shapes were put to him.** A **stack** of tabs, one per pair: a busy
clause becomes ten same-mark tabs the rail cannot fit, and a count that reads
as importance against the margin index (M1–M6). A **switcher** on the card, a
control to step among the dealt pairs: a new control whose main job is
overriding the router's order, and §8.3 is active pair sampling — the order is
the information. And the **deck**: one entry per clause, lit while the router
holds an unjudged pair for you on the race; judging closes the card and the
next press opens the next pair in the router's order; ⏳ only when none is
left; no new control. He chose the deck, and on what the entry shows while the
deck is not empty — *it should show you the pair that you would vote on next* —
so the teaser is the front pair's case, exactly what `teasersFor` already
printed, and the count the option text had floated is withdrawn. His ruling of
2026-08-17 (*💡 doesn't need to say how many left to decide*) stands: nothing
counts what is behind the front pair.

**Then the ledger.** Ed: *Is there a way I can go back to see pairs that I've
already judged?* There was not, live: the server sent *you have voted on this
race* as a flag and never which pair or which way, so the ⏳ card's verdict
lived only in the page's memory for the current visit, and `LIVE_HOOKS.judge`
warned *no card served* on any ⏳ card at all — the engine having, correctly,
dealt nothing — so a live judgment could never actually be revised from the
page. Offered the ⏳ card as the member's own ledger — every pair they judged
there, verdict marked, revisable — he folded it into the deck plan, so the
deck's accepted cost (an earlier pair out of reach while later pairs are dealt)
never shipped. **The view carries `myJudgments` per race**: the member's own
standing judgments touching it, ids and verdict, oldest first, superseded ones
gone. It is §3.5-safe by construction — every line is the member's own act, and
the blind guard (`not.toMatch(/leaderP|certification|author|"value"/)`) covers
it. The ledger's blocks are drawn from `proposalHtml`'s own pieces — a
`propblock` per pair, `rtext` wordings, `wordingHtml` for a candidate's change
against the clause, the lane radio's dot as an inert mark on the chosen side —
rather than through `proposalHtml` itself, since a pair is two wordings under
one press and a proposal block is one wording under a speaker. A press makes
that pair the card's active pair with the verdict pre-selected (`activeLedger`
in session.js, cleared as the card closes), and ✓ sends `judge-race` on the
same pair, the revision §4.4 already allows. One commit row on the card at all
times (§9.1): the ledger's blocks are a switcher over what you have *already*
answered, never over what the router has not yet asked. A locked (↻) block
takes no press and carries the ground-shift sentence.

**What the build found.** The plan's context said one hand could hold
incumbent-vs-A and incumbent-vs-B from one race at once. It cannot:
`bestPairFor` returns one best pair per race and skips only pairs already
*judged* (`servedOut`), never pairs already dealt in the same hand, and the
hand de-duplicates by pair — so the same race yields the same pair on every
slot and a hand holds one pair per race. The deck therefore reads **across
views**, not within one: judge, and the command's own refresh deals the next.
That is the design rule 1 already stated, and nothing on the page depends on
the hand's size; the server test asserts what the mechanism keeps. And the
rival pair needs no gate: with a member's incumbent pairs exhausted,
`bestPairFor`'s second scan deals A-vs-B whatever the gate says (the
"sparingly" of §8.3) — so two challengers on one clause are **three** presses
on one entry, quick, quick, then the race card, and a race card is reachable
on a live document with a room of two. The journey walk's deck step is exactly
that, the guest proposing a second wording on the clause of its first.

**Provisional state keyed by pair.** `pairKeyOf(g)` is the item id plus the
pair's ids where an item carries a pair and the id alone where it does not, so
the fixture's items, the diagonals and the motions key exactly as before —
`session-probe` IDENTICAL, `setup-probe` 0 diffs. The rail's state and receipt
read the **front** pair (`frontKeyOf`): after a judgment the entry wears
*still deciding — click to change your mind* until the refresh deals the next
pair, and re-lights the moment it does. The charter column's data key
(`syncCharter`) hashes the text, the close and the two capabilities, not the
items — but the items are rebuilt from the view on every poll and every
command's refresh regardless of the key, except under a draft being typed, so
the served pair did not need adding to it.

No SPEC change and no R-number: the mechanism is unchanged, and §8.3 and §8.3b
already say it.

## STYLE.md §7, the audit log, lifted 2026-09-07 (the docs pass)

Lifted verbatim from `design/STYLE.md` §7 by the docs pass of 2026-09-07 (Ed,
2026-09-07: *looking especially for things that are no longer relevant that
can be removed, and attempting to synthesise the rest*), on the pass's rule
that history moves out of rule files: the audit log is history, STYLE.md is
the checklist. STYLE.md §7 is now a pointer here, and **every new audit item
is appended to this section, numbered on from 84**. Inside the items, *§n*
and *Tn* mean STYLE.md's sections and rules as they stood when the item was
written, *item n* means this list, and *above* and *below* are as written.
The original heading follows, demoted one level.

Each sentence starts with who can do what, and every noun in it is something the reader can point at — the text, a setting, a ✒️ tab, the membership, an address. **Held and not-held differ by subject**: holding it, the sentence is about *you*; not holding it, it names *who can*, which is the question a struck-through tool actually raises, answered without a word of apology.

Each proposal costs one ✏️.** — 68 characters against 139, the refund moving to the act, where §5 already puts the price, and to the settled clause, which says it. ✒️, 🛡️, 🏛️ and 💡 lose their issued-when and their parenthetical histories. **T37** is the rule and **H4** the ceiling, at 200 characters: two sentences do not run past it, so anything that does is carrying a third thing.
