530. **Even a ✒️ decision should offer a rationale, and a change should announce itself.** (Ed, 2026-08-22, backlogged as he raised it.) Two halves of one idea. **(a)** The pen commits with no rationale lane, where every motion carries one — so the one route that changes a rule *without asking anybody* is also the only one that leaves no reason behind, which is exactly backwards: a change nobody got to argue about is the one most worth explaining. **(b)** A change should generate an acknowledgement — *The Founder has changed the visibility from x to y* — presumably the news card the surface already has, pinned until OK, which is the same object an unacknowledged constitutional decision uses. **The exception is the founder deciding something for the first time**, which is not a change at all: at the founding a setting goes from unanswered to answered, there is no *from x* to state, and a room being told that the founder has decided fifteen things they were never asked about is noise rather than news. So the trigger is *a settled value being re-set*, not *a value being set* — which is a distinction §9.6a already draws, since before the start nothing is amended, only set. Open inside it: whether the rationale is required or offered (offered, on the surface's own rule that a blank rationale is a real proposal); whether the acknowledgement goes to every member or only to those who had a say; and whether it stands in the rail as news or only in the record.

    **Investigated 2026-08-22 (Ed: *investigate this change*).** Findings, in the order they change the shape of the work.

    **Half of (b) is already built, and nobody noticed.** `setSetting` ends with `if (CONSTITUTIONAL.has(setting)) this.oweOks(t, setting)`, and the fold deletes every member's `okGiven` for that setting — so a founder changing a **constitutional** setting already owes every other member an acknowledgement, *and an OK given before the change is dropped, so it is owed again*. That is the news card pinned until OK, the object this asks for. What is genuinely missing is narrower than the note implies: **ordinary settings owe nothing at all** (⏱️ the rate, 🤖 machines, 📈 the ramp), so a founder re-setting the proposal rate tells nobody; and **the card states the rule, not the change** — `headFor` serves the clause's own sentence, so it reads *Only members can see the document* where Ed wants *The Founder has changed the visibility from x to y*.

    **The "from x" costs no event change.** Nothing anywhere projects a previous value, but every `setting-set` is already in the log, so the previous value folds into `SettingState` exactly as `arrival` and `powerFrom` folded in Q524 — a projection over events that already exist, hash chain untouched, golden log unedited.

    **And the exception is already implemented, by a different rule.** The page withholds *all* news until the document begins (`news()`'s `!constituted() ? false`), on §9.6a's ground that the founder re-sets freely until the start — which covers "the founder deciding for the first time" for everything decided during the founding. It does **not** cover a setting first decided *after* the start (delegated, never resolved, reclaimed, set), where a true first-time test wants `previousValue === null`. So (b) and the exception are the same piece of work: the fold that gives you *from x* is also what tells a first decision from a change.

    **(a) the rationale needs one optional field, and it is hash-safe.** `setting-set` carries `{type, t, setting, value, by}` and no reason. `stableStringify` **drops undefined keys**, so adding `why?: string` leaves an event without a rationale serialising exactly as it does today: every existing log replays bit-identically. The precedent is in the same file — `motion-opened` has carried `why?: string` since it existed.

    **One real design question inside (a), and it is not a small one.** The rationale lane the surface already has (`whyLane`) draws the `sealed-speaker` — the featureless disc — because authorship is sealed until the record (§3.4). A ✒️ act is attributed **by construction**: only the founder can perform it, and the acknowledgement names them. So a founder's rationale must not wear the sealed disc; it is the one voice on this surface speaking in its own name. Either a named speaker treatment (the founder's own avatar, which exists) or no speaker at all — but the sealed disc would be a lie the first time it was drawn.

    Sizing, then: the acknowledgement half is one fold field, one view field and copy, and it brings the first-time exception with it. The rationale half is one optional event field, one lane, and a decision about whose face is on it.

    **Built 2026-08-22** (Ed: *let's do 530; the rationale should have the founder's name and avatar on it, and 👑 so people know that it was a founder action, even if they have no name or avatar*). Module: `setting-set` gains an **optional** `why?`, hash-safe because `stableStringify` drops undefined keys; `SettingState.previousValue` and `setWhy` fold from events the log already carried, so **the golden log passed unedited**. The acknowledgement widens by one clause — constitutional settings owe an OK on any set as before, ordinary ones only when the value **changed** — which is Ed's exception stated in the module rather than in copy. Server: `set-setting` takes `why`, capped like every other rationale. Page: `WORDS` (a typed value in words, its own map because `RESULT` reads the current value out of `S` and `MVAL` only knows what a motion may offer), `changeHalf` (the founder's lane, or the change note and the reason), `founderSpeaker` / `founderSpeakerLane` (avatar, name, 👑 — never the sealed disc, since a ✒️ act is attributed by construction), and `syncOwedOks`, which makes the module the truth about what is owed on the fixture path as `hydrateS` now does on the live one — it had only ever *added*, so an acknowledgement could never be taken back and a change could not announce itself. 13 new module tests; verified end to end on the fixture: a first decision shows neither half, a change shows the lane to the founder and the note to a member, and the member's OK clears it. **Still open inside it**, and unbuilt: whether the acknowledgement reaches every member or only those who had a say (it reaches every member), and whether the reason belongs in the record as well as in the rail.

    **The two residuals closed 2026-08-22, and the second reframed the first half of the build.** Ed: **(a)** *owe the lapsed too* — E excludes them and for deciding that is right, but an acknowledgement is not a decision; it is owed to somebody about a document they are still a member of, and the person who was under the old rule and went quiet is exactly the one a change ought to find. Removed members and never-arrived members stay excluded, each for its own reason. **(b)** *both clause and record* — the reason stops vanishing at the OK: the clause keeps a dated **Last amended** block permanently, and the closed record grows an **Amendments** section. Then, mid-build: ***a unilateral rule change by the founder is still just a kind of amendment and so should be treated in the same way in terms of how it's communicated and reported*** — which retired the bespoke change list this had been growing. A pen change now **joins the motions**: `MotionRoute` gains `'pen'` (the four verbs' ladder of who had to agree), `RaisedRoute` narrows anything that raises one, and the record is **folded from the `setting-set` event** rather than emitted, so the hash chain is untouched and the golden log unedited. The dividend was immediate and is the point of his framing: the clause's history line now serves **both routes** with one shape, naming the founder where the pen is attributed by construction and the membership where the mover is sealed (§3.4).

    **Answered and built 2026-08-22.** Ed chose **the lean** (of glow · ring · spin · lean), **🪶 ✒️ ✏️ only** (🍾 and 🏛️ deferred), and **his two mechanisms alone** — no empty track, no button-side fill — *then look*. Then, unprompted, the two proposals themselves: *when you mouse over a 🪶✒️✏️🏛️ button, the token in the topbar that will be spent is somehow highlighted*, and *when someone just clicks and doesn't hold, the token jumps 1/4 the way towards the button, so that it's hard to miss that you're making something happen*. Both put the teaching on **the thing being spent** rather than on the button, which is more on-metaphor than anything on the original list: the price is an object, so the object reacts. Named `spend-preview` and `short-press-nudge`; see the glossary.

    **What the ground survey found, which changed the job.** (a) **There was no return flight on ✒️ or 🪶 at all** — `penRelease` called `flight.cancel()`, which removes the glyph outright — so a tap on the two buttons a founder meets *first* made a feather appear near the wallet and vanish. The nudge is those buttons' first fly-home, not an adjustment to one. (b) **Every wallet token's animation was being destroyed on a timer**: the ✏️ row rebuilds its innerHTML every second on the drip, the power wallets on every render, and only `#quill` had an idempotent write guard — so no transition on a ✏️ or ✒️ token could ever run to completion. Latent, and the lean walked straight into it. (c) `flyGlyph`'s safety timeout owns its traveller, so a release at 990ms of a 1000ms flight would have had the glyph deleted in mid-air at 1080ms while it was still rewinding; it now hands ownership over (`disarm`).

    **Three things settled during the build.** **"A quarter of the way" is ambiguous by 60%** — the pen flies `linear` but the pencil flies `cubic-bezier(.45, .05, .3, 1)`, whose slow start makes a quarter of the *duration* only 18% of the *arc*. The floor is **distance**, because there is no track on the surface and nobody can perceive a fraction of a duration: 250ms of 1000 for the pen, 864ms of 3000 for the pencil. **The throw needs a minimum rate, not a fixed duration** — measured at 0.94x on the pen, i.e. the token drifting forward *slower* than the hold moves it, which is the exact opposite of the point; a 1.8x floor means the flick is always a speed the hold cannot produce, which is what makes the exaggeration read as momentum rather than as progress. And **the preview must not key on `:hover`**: the first version self-healed by testing `leanBtn.matches(':hover')`, which is **false in headless Chromium with the pointer parked on the button** — so every harness would have been blind to the feature, and correctness would have rested on a paint state. It tracks the pointer from the events instead (a `pointerover` on anything that does not spend is itself the proof the pointer has left), with `isConnected` as the structural self-heal for the case that actually happens: a card committing and closing under the cursor.

    **Honesty note, since the floor over-reports.** Position on an arc is only a progress *reading* if there is a scale to read it against, and Ed's own answer forbade the things that would supply one. What a viewer can perceive is departure, distance and return — not "this is 25%". The lie is confined to releases below a quarter, where the truthful alternative is showing nothing, which is the bug. A floor on *time in the air* instead would be unimpeachable and useless: 100ms of the pencil's easing is 3% of the arc, under 20px, invisible at the corner of the eye.

    **Verified**: session-probe IDENTICAL (43 cards, all geometry) — the hover and nudge work is entirely invisible to it, by design; setup-probe 42 steps, 0 diffs, 0 allowed after the re-freeze the ✒️∞ markup required; `npm run journey` exit 0 with `errors · none` and `refused · none`; lint, typecheck and 480 tests green. Directly measured, since no harness covers either mechanism: the lean's keyframes point at the button, its `startTime` survives repeated wallet rebuilds unchanged, moving away leaves zero animations running, the throw runs at 1.8x, the ghost clears only when the token lands, and under reduced motion the lean is pure opacity and the nudge is a quarter of a fade.

    **Left open.** (a) **The empty track at rest** is still the only signal that works before the user has done anything and the only one that works on touch, where neither of these exists — held in reserve pending Ed watching testers meet the built version. (b) **🍾 and 🏛️** keep their deferral for the *preview*; note the **nudge reached 🍾 anyway** (its cork now flies back to the button on a short press rather than vanishing), since it rides `penRelease` — which is what Ed asked for in *clearly the others should also fly back*. 🏛️'s assembly-press is untouched and still shows nothing for a tap. (c) The two flight paths **disagree about reduced motion** and always have: `flyStart` fades out at the *source* and never appears at the destination, `flyGlyph` fades in at the *destination* and never appears at the source, and the comment above the first describes a third behaviour it does not have (*"fades at the wallet and arrives at the button"*). Pre-existing, deliberately left alone rather than changed in a batch about something else.

532. **The topbar as a toolbar: every wallet visible from the start, empty ones shown empty.** (Ed, 2026-08-22, mid-build on Q531: *perhaps we should give all of the wallets to all users at the beginning, and explicitly show that empty ones are empty; the topbar is a toolbar, and tools are added and taken away depending on what's happening; I hope this makes it clearer to users why we're going to such effort making a distinction between them. More evidence for 🛡️ as a tool perhaps.*) Raised, not built — it **reverses a rule from the day before** and deserves its own decision rather than being folded into a build about holds.

    **The rule it meets.** *A power is not held until it has been acknowledged* (2026-08-21) and its consequences: **an offer disappears**, and **a question you may not answer is not shown at all** — Ed's own words, *I shouldn't be shown actions that I can't do*. `.navbar .powerwallet:empty { display: none; }` is that rule in CSS, and the grant machinery is built on the wallet *appearing*: each grant is a task, acknowledged, and only then does the glyph fly into a wallet that did not exist a moment earlier.

    **Why it may not be a reversal at all, which is the interesting part.** That rule is about **actions and questions** — things you could press, answers you could give. An **empty slot is neither**: it asks nothing, offers nothing and cannot be pressed. And the gain Ed names is real and is not available any other way: the four wallets are **the four verbs**, a ladder of *who has to agree*, and a member who only ever sees the ones they hold never sees the ladder — so the distinction the whole design is built on is invisible to exactly the people it governs. There is a second, unlooked-for gain: the pen currently flies to a wallet that **does not exist until it lands**, which is why `renderPowerWallets` has to conjure it mid-flight; a permanent slot makes the destination visible *before* the flight, which is the same argument Q531 just made about the button. So the grant moment probably gets **stronger**, not weaker: the topbar stops changing shape, but the flight gains a target you can see it aiming at.

    **Three things need Ed's answer before it can be built.** **(a) Who sees the empty slots?** Members plainly. A **stranger** and an **applicant** are not in the room and three empty slots would be noise about a document they cannot act in. A **clerk** is the hard one: by design they have no ✏️ and no 🏛️ for the life of the document (*a clerk's topbar holds nothing but 🪶*), so a permanent empty pair is either honest information about what a clerk is or a standing reproach on every screen. **(b) What does empty look like?** The surface already has both halves of the answer and they disagree: grey means *nothing is being asked of you*, and `.gone` is a slot that keeps its width at `visibility: hidden`. A dimmed glyph is probably right and a dashed box certainly wrong, but an empty slot must not read as a control that is merely disabled. **(c) Does 🛡️ join now or later?** It is coherent — ✒️ and 🛡️ are the two powers, held per setting, *one pen many locks* — and it would make the toolbar the complete statement of what you hold. It is also an ∞ wallet like the pen, since a veto is never spent; it acts by existing. Ed's parenthetical suggests he already thinks so.

    **One consequence to fix rather than ask about.** `holdWallet` tests **the existence of `#penwallet i`** as its proxy for *you hold a pen*, and the guard that swallows a hold's trailing click reads `isPenCommit(held) && …`. If an empty wallet renders a token, that test silently becomes always-true — and Q531's `spend-preview` inherits it, since the preview is gated on the same function. Both must re-base on `mayPen()` / `mayVoice()` rather than on DOM presence, in the same change.

    Related: this is also a partial answer to **531(a)**, the empty track at rest — an always-visible wallet is an at-rest affordance for the *powers*, though not for the *hold*.

    **Answered and built 2026-08-22.** **(a) Everyone** — *a row of empty bars explains to you what your role can do, and "nothing" is a useful answer.* **(b)** each wallet is **a pill with an inner shadow**, a depression saying *something goes here*; an unheld tool is drawn in its socket **with a diagonal red line across it**; and **clicking a socket opens a speech bubble** explaining what it means. **(c) 🛡️ goes in** — *let's put it in and see how it looks.*

    **The distinction the build added, which Ed's phrasing collapsed.** *Empty* is two states and only one of them is a slash. A member who holds ✏️ and has spent them all still **holds the power** — the drip is running and the tray already says when the next lands — and that is `.empty` plus a countdown, as it always was. A clerk, a stranger, an applicant, a member before 🍾 or before accepting the grant **does not hold it at all**, and that is `.notheld`, struck through. A slash across both would tell a member they had lost a power they still have. So `walletHeld` is its own piece of wallet render state beside `walletShow` and `walletGhost`, never a class the page toggles from outside — `renderWallet` rewrites `className` wholesale and would wipe it.

    **The red is built as asked and is the only red on the surface**, which is worth keeping in view: the palette is three hues and a grey, and 🗑️ was deliberately *not* red on the argument that discarding is an ordinary thing to do rather than a danger. Not holding a power is the same kind of fact — the shape of your role, not an error — and a clerk wears two of these all session. **`?slash=muted`** renders the identical toolbar with the strike in the surface's own muted ink, the same shape as the stranger's door's `?bars=black`: an experiment you can look at rather than an argument.

    **Three things found in the building.** **The slash came out grey**, because a `::after` on the `<i>` is inside the box carrying `filter: grayscale(1)` — the one colour decision in the rule, quietly undone by the line above it. It hangs on the socket now. **`holdWallet` was inferring the pen from the DOM**: it tested `document.querySelector('#penwallet i')`, a true proxy for *you hold a pen* only while an unheld wallet rendered nothing — with every socket now drawing its tool that test would be permanently true, so an unacknowledged pen would have become a working hold, and the guard that swallows a hold's trailing click reads `isPenCommit(held)`. It asks `mayPen()` now, which was always the question. And **the navbar's height is load-bearing**: it is sticky and everything below is measured against it, so a socket taller than the 26px the avatar already sets would have moved every card on the surface. 24px, measured at 48.5px navbar before and after.

    **🛡️ needed nothing from the module.** `pwPair(k)` is the single place a setting becomes a `{u, a}` pair, covers every `PW_KEYS` entry including the Text, and reads the same off the blind projection in live mode — so `PW_KEYS.some(k => pwPair(k).a)` is the exact mirror of the fold the pen was already doing. It takes the ∞ too, being equally perpetual.

    **Verified**: navbar 48.5px unchanged in every state; session-probe IDENTICAL (43 cards, all geometry); setup-probe 42 steps, 0 diffs, 0 allowed after the re-freeze; journey exit 0, `errors · none`, `refused · none`; lint, typecheck and 480 tests green.

    **Residuals.** (a) **The closed page keeps its old answer** — the farewell flies the tools out and the sockets go with them (`.gonewallet`). Ed's rule arguably reaches there too, and rather well: the tools *were* taken away, which is exactly what a row of empty sockets says. Not done, because it changes a finished ceremony rather than a live toolbar, and four red strikes on a grey filed page is a different aesthetic question. (b) **🛡️ rides `grant-pen`'s acknowledgment** rather than having a grant of its own. Defensible — both powers arrive in the founder's hands by one act at one moment, and the save is when that becomes real — but the purer reading of *no power arrives without acknowledgment* gives it its own card, its own flight and its own place in the founding order. (c) **The quill's link now lives inside its bubble**, since a bubble over the logo would otherwise swallow the one capability it carries. That is a real improvement hiding in a side effect: a founder mid-birth who clicked the mark used to be navigated away from the document they were making.

    **The three residuals answered 2026-08-22, and two of them built.** **(a) The closed page keeps hiding its sockets** — Ed: *agree, the sockets only make sense when the document is in session.* No change; `.gonewallet` is the rule. **(b) The strike is dark red** (`#8e2116`), chosen with both versions on screen: at full saturation four strikes read as four errors, where the fact being stated is only that this is not your tool. `?slash=muted` stays reachable for comparison. **(c) 🛡️ has its own acknowledgment** — Ed: *a founder should have to acknowledge both separately; it's very important for them to understand what they can and can't do.* Its own card (`grant-shield`, 🛡️ *Your Shield*), its own key in `GRANT_KEYS`, its own flight into its own socket, its own clause. It stands **immediately after ✒️** in `ORDER`, so the pen is met, accepted, and then the shield is met alone — and it **does not block** the queue, keeping 🏛️'s rule rather than the pen's exception, because you cannot commit anything with a shield. That also leaves the rail at the save holding the pen alone, which the journey walk asserts. Measured on the live path: `at save · rail ["grant-pen"]`, then `ok · grant-pen`, then `ok · grant-shield`.

    **The bubble says the symbol and the verb** (Ed, 2026-08-22: *don't name the item — just have the symbol, larger than in the wallet, and then explain what it is using the verb; keep the language as clear and functional as possible, using verbs and nouns that relate to concrete things on the page*). So no *"The shield."* opening: naming a thing is not explaining it, and the glyph has already said which one it is. Each sentence starts with **who can do what**, and every noun in it is something the reader can point at — the text, a setting, a ✒️ tab, the membership. **Held and not-held differ by subject**: holding it, the sentence is about *you* and says what it spends and what comes back; not holding it, it names *who can*, which is the question a struck-through tool actually raises. One table (`SAY`) feeds both the bubble and the tooltip, so the two channels cannot drift — which needed a seam in session.js (`setWalletTitle`), since the ✏️ socket is rendered there and the drip rewrote its title every second.

    **Residuals now.** (a) The grant flight's destination table replaced a pen-or-voice ternary pair; three of them agreeing by hand was one place two would drift. (b) 🛡️'s clause and card copy have not been through a STYLE.md pass with the rest of the founding — `npm run founding` prints them in order and is the tool for it.

533. **`design/setup.notes.md`'s dependency tree describes a surface that no longer exists.** (Found during housekeeping, 2026-08-22; claimed here rather than fixed, because it is a rewrite rather than a correction.) CLAUDE.md lists the notes as *kept current at Ed's ask — the shared task grammar and the founding dependency tree*, and the tree is the half that has rotted: it is the **wave graph**, retired on 2026-08-21 when the founding went single file, and `ORDER` in session-view.html has been the dependency list ever since. It also predates the glyph batch (🏷️ and 🔗 for what are now 🪶 and 📍) and every grant that has since taken a place in the order. Marked *superseded, kept as history* at its head for now, which is honest but leaves a load-bearing document half-true. **(a)** Rewrite it as a description of the single file, which is mostly a matter of transcribing `ORDER` and saying what each card genuinely needs from the ones above it. **(b)** Delete the tree and let `ORDER` plus the CLAUDE.md entry be the whole answer — the reasoning about *literal* dependencies (the mail names the document; nothing is saved before the address is proven) would need somewhere to go first. **(c)** Leave the marker and let it rot as history. I would do (a): the literal-versus-pacing distinction it records is the reason the single file is safe to reorder, and that argument exists nowhere else.

534. **Should the address 📍 pre-fills be free by construction?** (From the fix of 2026-08-22, below.) 📍 is born pre-filled with `slugify(title)` and the card now asks the server about it on arrival, so a founder whose title collides with an existing document meets a task that is refused the moment it opens — correct, honest, and still a small unpleasantness at the third step of the birth. The server already computes the nearest free address twice (for the 409 and now for the check), and `uniqueSlugAsync` is exactly the function that would answer this. **(a)** As built: suggest the plain address, check it, and let the founder read *taken* and take the offered alternative. It is one extra press, and it shows them the address is a real, contested thing rather than a slot the machine fills — which is arguably worth teaching at the birth. **(b)** Ask the server for the suggestion at title-time, so the pre-filled address is free when it arrives and the refused state is only ever reached by typing. Costs a request per title, and the suggestion can still go stale between the fill and the send, so the check and the 409 both stay regardless. **(c)** (b) plus a note saying why the address is not simply the title — *docs.vote/charter is taken, so this one is charter-2* — which is the honest version of (b), since silently handing somebody a suffixed address is the machine making a decision without saying so. I lean (a): the refusal is rare, it is now legible and actionable, and (b) buys a smoother path at the cost of a request on every title keystroke's settle and a suggestion that can lie by the time it matters. Worth your call because it is a founding-experience question rather than a correctness one. **Ed, 2026-08-22: (c)** — the address moves, and the move says so. Built on the distinction the fix already needed: **the address is the machine's until you touch it**. A *suggested* address that comes back taken moves to the nearest free one before the founder meets it; a *typed* one never moves, because there the address is theirs and a collision is a refusal to read and correct. `S.slugAuto` is the whole of it, set in `fillSuggestedSlug` — the one place a suggestion is applied, where there had been three copies of the same three lines — and cleared by the one act that can make the address yours. The note names both addresses (*Suggested from the title — docs.vote/charter is taken, so this one is docs.vote/charter-2*), which is what makes it (c) rather than (b). No new endpoint and no request per keystroke: the `suggestion` the check already carries is what it moves to, so the cost worried about in (b) never arrives. Two guards: the address it moves **to** is asked about in its own right on the next render rather than trusted from the response that offered it, and `autoSlugMoves` caps the chain at three, past which the collision is simply shown — a server that kept offering an address it then refused would otherwise be a request storm.

535. **Does `scripts/slug-walk.mjs` stay?** (Raised with the same fix.) It drives a live birth onto an address that is already reserved and asserts 📍 refuses it *there* — the commit dark, the note naming the nearest free address, nothing sent at the wire — then corrects the address and walks the birth through clean. It is the walk that fails on the pre-fix page, which is the only reason to trust it. It exists because `npm run journey` births with a unique title and so can never meet a taken address, and both probes drive the fixture, where the check is synchronous and the live path is never touched. **(a)** Keep it as its own script with an npm entry beside `journey`, which is what it is: a second live-path walk, for the birth's refusals rather than its happy path. **(b)** Fold its assertions into `journey-walk.mjs` — it would have to reserve an address first, which makes the journey no longer a single straight line but keeps one live harness rather than two. **(c)** Drop it; the server test pins the endpoint and the surface rule is written down in CLAUDE.md. I recommend (a): this is the second bug in two days that ended at a correct 409 reading as the page malfunctioning, and neither existing harness could see either of them. It is committed with the fix so it is not an unexplained untracked file; say the word and it goes. **Ed, 2026-08-22: (a)** — kept, with `npm run slug-walk` beside `npm run journey`. Q534 (c) changed what it walks, and for the better: it now covers **both** halves of the rule rather than one — that a *suggested* address moves off a collision, naming both addresses, and that a *typed* one is refused and stays refused with nothing sent at the wire. It fails on the pre-fix page at *the commit is dark on a typed address that is taken*. It needs a reserved address to walk against, so its header carries the one-line `curl` that makes one.

**649 is the free-typing fix's residual** (2026-08-22), raised by Ed's live walk — *when the document has begun, as a founder, I can still write freely in the text area, and my edits don't create amendments.* Two holes found and shut in one commit: the charter's `beforeinput` let a host-caret keystroke through to the browser (the bug Ed hit), and the module's `begin` never waited on the confirmed text (§9.0b), so a wire-level start could wedge a document with no text and no way to propose one; `#prose` also ships read-only now, and `npm run journey` asserts the begun state and types on the host. What the refusal left open was the confirmed-**empty** text, filed as 649 and **answered by Ed the same night as (a)**: an empty document renders one empty clause keyed to engine line 0, wearing a grey invitation, so the first keystroke opens the editing card like any other. Built 2026-08-23 — and it found a second truth on the way: the engine holds an empty document as **zero** lines, so the proposal is an insert at [0, 0), and every hunk is now clamped to the line count the engine actually holds. `npm run journey -- --empty-text` walks it.

**650–654 are the dead-click nudge** (2026-08-23), raised by Ed — *users in the birth phase don't always realise they should be clicking on tasks in the rail, as they have just started using the product and we are teaching them new behaviour* — and reframed by him the same evening into something better than the intermittent jiggle he first asked for: *how about a settleLift nudge on the "Title" queue-card when someone clicks over where the "Untitled" helper text is? That's the most common behaviour, because they expect to be able to edit it directly.* The mechanism is confirmed in the code, and it is worse than *not noticed*: `#doctitle` is a bare `<h1>` with no `data-card` and nothing listening above it, so **clicking "Untitled" does nothing at all**. The tester Ed watched reached for the obvious door, got no response, and went looking for the nearest thing that would accept typing — the prose column underneath. **650** answered **(a)**: the 🪶 tab in the gutter and the 🪶 rail entry beat **together**, so the beat teaches that the tab, the rail entry and the card are one thing rather than merely pointing at a location. **651** answered: the idle jiggle is **dropped** — every motion on this surface is a consequence (a clause fades because it was born, an entry lifts because it was pressed, the pulse beats because somebody acted), an ambient jiggle would be the first thing on the surface to move for no reason, and the birth has no clock to ride anyway, the 4s poll being live-mode only. **652** answered: the nudge **never opens the card**, however many times they click — it stays a teacher, which is C1/F10's whole point. **653** answered: the trigger is **any dead click in the document during the birth**, not the heading as a special case. **654** is open above.

**674–682 are the phase ladder** (2026-08-23), raised by Ed — *it would be good to have a test harness that with repeated button clicks could go from {fresh document} to {start of the constitution} to {begin with a variety of constitutional settings} to {halfway through a session with a long document with a load of active amendments} to {a session that closes in 5 minutes} to {closed session with comments}*. **674–678 are his answers**, given the same day: **674** the ladder walks a **live** document, not the fixture, since the fixture is what every live-only bug this project has hit was invisible to; the fixture stays as it is for design work. **675** one document **evolves**, a rung per press, rather than a menu that builds a fresh document at each phase — so the phase boundaries are watched rather than skipped. **676** the constitution is **seeded random, generated from the catalogue itself** rather than from named presets, so a setting added next month is randomised the day it is added and the surface is fuzzed against combinations nobody hand-picked; the seed shows in the bar and can be typed back. **677** it is a **test** as well as an instrument: a walk asserts the surface at each rung, not in CI for now. **678** — the correction that mattered — **rung 3 stands immediately before 🍾 is pressed**, not after it, because the start is the most interesting transition on the surface and a stagehand that spends that press hides it; and the session carries **~20 members and at least 30 live proposals of different kinds**, which is the first time the rail's fit cap, `fitStacks` and the tab stacks meet a roster that size on a live document. **679–680 are the two production defects the design review turned up**, each fixed on its own before the ladder: the minute tick has no per-document guard, so one document that throws stops the clock for every document after it in insertion order, once a minute, for ever; and mail needs refusing at the mailer for RFC 2606 reserved TLDs, which is how the ladder's cast is silenced in a way that survives a restart, a later tick and the close, where a build-time flag survives none of them. **681–682 were the build's own findings**, both real and both fixed. **681** — *reading a document is a write.* Presence stamps `now` (§9.5a), so merely looking at a ladder document pinned its log to the present and the next rung had no past left to write into; since the bar reloads after every press, that happened between every pair of them, and the elapsed session the whole instrument exists to show was impossible. A ladder document's clock is the ladder's now: the view path skips presence for it, dev-only, inside the label. **682** — *🎩 records the act, not the value*, found by the ladder on its first outing and the sharpest kind of find, because the comment directly above the line describes this exact bug class and had fixed only the begun case. Pre-🍾 the surface kept 🎩's settledness in `S.seen` alone, which no reload rebuilds, so **a founder who answered *am I a member?* and reloaded was asked again — and since 🎩 blocks the founding order, the whole constitution below it was withheld again with it.** Measured by the walk: acknowledging the pen used to release seven band tabs and no cork, and now releases twenty and offers 🍾. The module folds `membershipSet` from the events the log already carried; `setConvenorMembership`'s no-op short circuit was the other half, since a founder who was already a member and answered *member* emitted nothing at all.

**Open from the build, for Ed by number.** **683** — the ✒️ grant's OK lives in `localStorage`, and it is `blocksOrder`'s one blocking grant, so rung 3 hands the founder a document whose constitution is withheld until they press OK on their pen. That is the founding order working and it is pleasant to watch, but it means rung 3 is not quite *immediately before 🍾* as Q678 asked: **(a)** leave it, the grants being real news worth meeting; **(b)** have the bar seed the acknowledgement in `localStorage` so rung 3 is exactly the cork and nothing else. Recommend (a). **684** asked what *n still to confirm or answer* counted, and is **closed by the note's removal** (plan 15, 2026-08-25 — see 783–784 below): the count is gone from all three of its states, so there is nothing left to count.

**732–735 are the 🖼️ Your Picture card** (2026-08-23) — the review, the resize, the repicker and the upload (Ed), built the same day. **Claimed first as 685–688 and renumbered here: the same collision for the fourth time in two days, and the first one no second session caused.** The claim was written at 03:12 and the build then stopped on a question it could not answer alone, so it sat on a branch for four hours where nothing else could see it, and the card audit and the documentation refactor took 685–731 in the meantime. The rule above says to claim a number by writing it into this file; what this adds is that **a claim only counts once it is on the branch the next writer will read** — work that parks takes its claim out of sight with it. The commits carrying this work, `8f79ddd` and `e0ca3d1`, still say 685–688 in their messages; the numbers below are the ones that count. **732 — a full in-page emoji picker**: search box plus the standard Unicode categories, lazy-rendered, reserved and taken glyphs greyed **in place** with their reason. The curated six rows are gone. Three things the build learned. **Only the open category may be drawn**: this body is rebuilt by every `render()` and the live page polls every four seconds, so 1906 buttons is not a thing to build on a keystroke — the grid is one group at a time, 169 of them on the category it opens on. **The search field cannot go through the page's own render**, which would rebuild the input under the caret, so the grid refreshes in place and the category and the query live beside `FACE_TONE`, never stored. And **`faceBtn` needed no change at all**, which is the pleasant part: it already greyed both refusals with their words, so offering the whole of Unicode simply means the surface's own marks are in the grid now, refusing themselves where a member meets them. **733 — the initials are not a section**: the card is *pick an emoji* → *upload an image* → *Currently* with Remove, and what you get with neither is a sentence rather than a row, because initials are not a third answer. Built, and `pictureBody` is now shared with the applicant's 🖼️, which had hand-rolled its own picker and carried no uploader at all. **734 — the reserved-furniture rule stays**, and **Q632 closes as its (a)**: 🍾 🥂 📨 join `SURFACE_EMOJI` in both `design/setup.js` and `packages/server/src/faces.ts`, byte-identical as the parity test requires. The build-time scan Q632 offered as (b) is still not taken. With it, the grounds `c0`–`c5` and drawn marks `m0`–`m2` are **deleted rather than tolerated**, on Ed's standing note the same day — *we're still in alpha, you can mostly ignore backwards compatibility, there are no real documents yet* — so `validPicture` refuses them and SPEC §9.0c names the two shapes for the first time (v0.68, R-046). **735 — downscale and re-encode client-side**, the data URI staying in the event log: 256×256, JPEG at 0.8, `imageOrientation: 'from-image'` so a portrait photograph is not delivered on its side by the very re-encode that strips its EXIF. Three defects closed at once — a phone photo that previewed and then failed on Save, GPS coordinates landing in a hash-chained log that holds answers in plaintext, and unbounded log growth; `LIMITS.picture` comes down from 150,000 to 40,000, set for what we now encode. **The review's own findings**, all fixed with it: the 7px emoji was a specificity accident no rule of that shape could win, so the emoji stopped being an `.av` at all; the *right aligned* half was `.cpv.founded .av` overriding `display` to `inline-flex`, where `place-items`' justify half means nothing — **which was miscentring the initials too**; and the emoji path was **entirely unprobed**, every fixture picture being the empty string, which one 🦉 on the founding cast and a 🖼️ step in the setup-probe now fix. The plan also asked for two things that cannot both hold, `ANSWER` committing both axes in one act and a `deps: ['authorship']` that makes the second of them throw. **Ed, 2026-08-25: *I think five rungs is fine; there is definitely a ladder going from anonymous forever to open forever*** — so the answer is **one setting**, not one card over two. ✍️ leaves the catalogue entirely and 👤 takes a ladder of five, most-private-first: `anonymous` · `anonymousElective` · `sealed` · `sealedElective` · `public`. **778 is open — the surface offers a blind question §9.0a says is not answerable.** Found by the `--delegate-all` walk on its first full run. 🌡️ and 🪜 are `deps: ['ending']`, and `session.ts:1129` refuses an answer to a dependent while its dependency is still collecting: hand over both ⏰ and 🌡️ in a room of one and the rail serves 🌡️'s question with a live ✓ that the module answers `'bar' waits on 'ending' (§9.0a)`. The cascade behind it then stalls, since `ansWaveReady` waits on an answer that cannot be given. Two halves to decide, and the second is the real question: (a) `visible(ans-*)` should also require the host setting's **dependencies** to be settled — but the page holds no copy of the catalogue's `deps`, so this needs a mirrored list and a `spec-check` assertion tying it to `CATALOGUE`; and (b) whether a question that cannot yet be asked **pauses** the cascade or is **looked through** by it — Q416's *if I have to do all of them anyway, they should cascade* argues for looking through, but looking through a question you will be asked later changes the order the founder meets them in, which is the one thing `ORDER` exists to fix. The walk holds ⏰ back meanwhile, with the reason at `journey-walk.mjs`'s `wantDelegate`.

**779–782 were the quorum blind task's dead slider** (plan 14), **built and spent 2026-08-25**. Ed: *clicking on the slider control doesn't appear to do anything, so I can't set my quorum answer.* The plan's own reading — an `input` that never reaches the handler, or a value written to a key the readout does not read — was wrong on both counts and measured to be wrong: the handler fired and the readout followed it the whole time the control was broken. **779** — **two causes, neither of them the event.** `slider()` tested `v === null` for *unset*, and a question nobody has answered is `undefined` (a member's answers object starts empty; the live hydration `continue`s past a null `myAnswer`), so on every real document the unset branch never fired: `value="undefined"` is invalid, so the browser parked the thumb at the midpoint under a readout reading `undefined% — NaN of 5` — **a suggested value, painted**, which is the one thing a blind collection exists not to show, and a click on a thumb where it already sits fires no `input` at all. And the `input` handler called `render()` on every step, which rebuilds the card — so the range input holding the pointer capture was destroyed on the first move of a drag and the thumb froze. Fixed as *unset means no value* and *nothing rebuilds under a press*: the gesture repaints the readout in place (`syncSlider`) with the rail and the commit around it, and the full render waits for `change`. **The no-defaults rule is not touched** — the fix restores it, since before it the control shipped an anchor. **780** — the readout and the ✓ follow: 👥 reads in the founder's chosen form (`55% — 2 of 2` for a share) and the ✓ files the answer, which `slider-walk` asserts. **781** — **every blind slider, because the cause is in `slider()` itself**: 🌡️'s `ans-bar` was broken identically and is fixed by the same two lines; both are walked. **782** — spent on the guard: `npm run slider-walk`, which drags with a real pointer, because nothing else here does. *(Two findings for plan 13's block, out of scope here: with the founder alone on the roster `ansDue()` is false until nothing else is outstanding, so 🌡️'s answer card is unreachable unless somebody has been invited — the walk invites; and delegating both 🌡️ and 👥 empties the rail before 🍾 altogether, which is Q773/Q776's subject.)*

**802–805 were the one measure** (plan 19), **built 2026-08-25 — all four spent.** Ed: *the text area for 'Text' is wider than the constitution text; they should be the same.* The plan asked for no new numbers, the batch pre-flight having claimed this block on 2026-08-24; nothing was renumbered. **802** — **the measurement, and it is not 3px.** At 1600 the two columns differed by the plan's predicted 1.5px a side (the rows' unexplained `+ 3px`); at 1280 the prose ran **24px further out on each side**, because a `.setrow` carries its tab gutter *inside* its `max-width` and `.prose` carried none — so wherever the document column is narrower than the measure the row loses a gutter and the prose does not, and that is the width Ed was looking at. Before: prose text `383…905`, clause text `407…881` at 1280; `502.13…1105.88` against `500.63…1107.38` at 1600. After: `407…881` and `502.13…1105.88` — **0px on both edges at both widths**, title, `.cptext`, `.setrow`, `.prose` and an open `.sugg`'s head all on the same two numbers. **803** — the property pair, `--measure` and `--measure-gutter`, declared on `.doc` and used by `.setrow`, `.prose`, `.doctitle` and `.sugg`: max-width is the measure plus two gutters, padding is one gutter, so the prose now carries the tab column the rows always did and the two agree by construction. The `+ 3px` is gone; nothing in `design/DECISIONS.md` ever explained it, and it was the whole of the wide-window disagreement. **804** — **yes, `ch` resolved differently, and worse than the plan guessed.** It is not that the two columns use different fonts; it is that an *unregistered* custom property substitutes its tokens and resolves `ch` against whoever **uses** it, so `.doctitle`'s own `max-width: 70ch`, read at `--t-lead`, was a column ~150px wider than the prose's and never bound at all — the row it sits in was the only thing holding the title. `--measure` is registered with `@property … syntax: "<length>"`, which resolves `70ch` once, at `.doc`, at document type, and inherits it as a length. Pinning it in `rem` was the alternative and was rejected: `ch` is the right unit for a measure and only the resolution site was wrong. **805** — spent on the last edge, which the plan did not name: `.doc .anch` gave back its left padding with a negative margin and not its right, so a charter paragraph wrapped **8px** earlier than a constitution clause even once the columns agreed. It takes `margin-right: calc(-1 * var(--s2))` now, on the same selector as `.clausehead .headclause` so the two boxes stay identical. **Measured consequences**: `card-audit` at 1600 is finding-for-finding identical to the parent commit, and at 1280 two findings **improve** — P2 *the glyph moves 26px sideways when the card opens* → 2px, and P3 *its left edge moves 18px* → −6px, which are the 1600 values, so the tab-you-click-does-not-move promise now behaves the same at both widths instead of losing a gutter at the narrow one. `founding-golden` unchanged. The session-probe goes from IDENTICAL to 838 diffs and the setup-probe from 136 to 188, **every added diff a `geo.*` one and no counts or html hashes among them** — the frozen references hold the old measure, and re-freezing them is not this plan's to do.

Stated cost, in `design/DECISIONS.md`: at ½ the meter saturates on the derived preference alone, which is what 0.51 has always done. **837** — three vitest cases in `packages/engine-core/test/session.test.ts` (`a document of one`): the floor, an hour of `tick()`s emitting nothing before a judgment, the edge card served, `comparison, adopted` in the one call; then 0.50 against 0.51, and the untouched formula at 0.90. **838** — `spec-check`'s `checkSoloJudgment` pins the `E() > 1` condition as source, verified red on the pre-fix line. **842–849 were a setting that predates you** (plan 29, backlog 50), **built 2026-08-25 — all eight spent, none released.** Ed's ruling: *a setting that predates you is simply what the document says; a power handed to you is news addressed to you*, and the symptom beside it — *I click a queue-card, click OK, then click the queue-card again, then click OK, then the queue card goes.* **The two are separate bugs reported as one experience**, and the second is the more general: a press that reads its own answer out of the view it was made against. **842** — SPEC bumped to **v0.73** (the plan's own text still said v0.71); §9.0a's inheritance bullet says *owed nothing*, and §9.6a time-indexes *had no say* to arrival, excluding the later joiner beside the removed and the never-arrived. **843** — R-016 reversed in `design/SPEC-REASONING.md` by extending its own *a gate opening is the exception* sentence: the general rule underneath both is that **what a member is owed is what happened while they were here**, which leaves the lapsed member owed (they were here) and the grant addressed to whoever it is handed to (a thing that happened). **844** — `oweOnJoining` and all three of its callers deleted rather than emptied, with `settledConstitutionalIds`, its only reader, behind them; every other owing path was already post-arrival and already skipped `arrivedAtT === null`, so the emission was the whole mechanism. The three R-016 tests invert, and `founding.test.ts`'s now also asserts the *next* amendment does reach the arrival — the half of the rule that stays. **845** — `constituted()` into the `news` disjunct. It was a real second bug, not only belt and braces: the `!constituted()` guard three lines above governs the ternary chain and the `||` escapes it, so a member was served the whole settled constitution **before 🍾**, in a document whose founder may still re-set every clause of it, against C8 and F8. **846** — one press, and it took both halves. A pressed key is held **in flight** until `api.cmd`'s promise resolves (which is after the refresh it triggers), and `syncOwedOks` gained the direction it never had — it adds when the module does not owe, as `hydrateS` always has. Symmetry alone flashes the task back for one round trip; the in-flight set alone loses the acknowledgement wherever `hydrateS` does not run. **Only the `set-` half is symmetric**: a delegated question resolving owes no OK in the module at all, so module silence is no evidence about `res-` and reading it as evidence would retire the resolution news. **847** — SURFACE E5's audience column, `CLAUDE.md`'s band rule and its lapsed-member gotcha (the test is now one question — *were you here when it was set?*), plus one new guarded gotcha for the double press. **848** — `journey-walk.mjs` grows a second browser context, which nothing in the project had ever driven: the dev ladder presses every owed OK for every member at once, and `founding-walk.mjs` and both probes are the founder alone in the fixture where no command is sent. An invited guest follows their own invitation pre-🍾 and is asked what is served to them; the founder amends 🌍 at the wire; the guest presses OK once and the task must leave, survive a poll, and survive a reload. **The reload is the tell** — before the fix it fails at the press and passes after the reload, verified by re-running against the pre-fix page. A second pre-Begin assertion was added that the plan did not ask for and the walk immediately earned: **🍾 is not a second chance to serve what predates you**, which is how the stale-module run was caught. `window.__founding` carries `okd` beside `owed`, because *the task is still there* names a symptom and cannot say which of the two mechanisms broke. **849** — `SPEC.md:341`, §9.7½'s admitted applicant, the same reversed clause in a second place. Reasoning: `design/DECISIONS.md`. Expected and not a regression: `npm run ladder` now reports fewer *owed acknowledgements given*, `oweOnJoining` having been most of what it counted.

**858–864 are the topbar face row** (plan 31, backlog 15) — **all seven spent, built 2026-08-26.** Ed: *where we currently say "n in the room" in the topbar we should show a row / stack of user avatars.* **858** — `#faces` beside `#quorum` in the `room` span, written by `renderClock` from `members().filter(m => m.in)`, capped at five with a `+n`. **945 is an abstention resolving a founding question at the act** (2026-08-27, riding R-049 and Q647), claimed by the batch pre-flight for a decision that was **never in the open register**: it was asked from backlog 64's plan while that plan was being written for the overnight draft run, the build assumed the answer, and Ed gave it the next day (*yes — the sign-out resolves it immediately*). The three smaller readings the plan stated in its Context were offered for refusal and none was refused, so all three stand: an abstainer **stays listed** in the 🍾 readout owing nothing rather than dropping out of it; the members who have already answered are **not told**, because a ground shift is a roster move and an abstention is not one; and an abstainer may still submit an answer, which is recorded, served back as their own `myAnswer` and counted towards nothing. **Folded**: SPEC §9.0a's electorate bullet states the moment (**v0.79**, `README.md` following), and `design/SPEC-REASONING.md` R-049 carries the confirmation and the three readings. **Spent.**

**948 is the disclosure rule's other direction** (2026-08-27, riding R-050 and Q770), claimed by the batch-P pre-flight for a decision that was **never in the open register**: it was asked from backlog 31's plan while that plan was being written for the overnight run, the build assumed the answer, and Ed gave it the next day. The question: §3.5a says a proposal keeps the disclosure rung it was made under, and the ruling behind it was argued only for a rung that **loosens** — a proposal made under *Nobody's name, ever* is never named later. The other direction was unnamed: a proposal made under *Names at the close* when the room afterwards tightens to *Nobody's name, ever*. Ed: *Symmetric — the rung at submission governs, always.* So the author who accepted that rung when they proposed is named at the close, and the rule needs no second clause and no per-direction test. **Folded**: SPEC §3.5a's *made under* paragraph now says the rule is symmetric and names the tightening case (**v0.80**, `README.md` following), and R-050 carries the confirmation. **949 is the wallet above its maximum** (2026-08-27), claimed by the batch-P pre-flight for a second decision that was **never in the open register**: it was asked from the promise-coverage plan for ⏱️ (batch O) in its *Questions for Ed* and answered the same day. The ⏱️ clause a room agrees reads *Members start with 4 ✏️ each, up to a maximum of 8*, and the engine treats the maximum as a cap on **accrual** and not on possession, so a motion that cuts the cap leaves members holding more than the clause says they may — locked as intended by `promise-rate.test.ts`'s fold case (*bo held 4 under a cap of 8; the cut to 3 does not claw them back*). The choice was to admit it in the clause or to clamp. Ed: **Clamp on a cap cut.** The narrow reading is the one taken, and it is the only one consistent with what stands: `packages/engine-core/src/tokens.ts` already says *refunds are never forfeited to the cap*, so a refund may still carry a wallet above the maximum between cap changes; what changes is that **a motion or a pen that lowers the cap clamps every wallet to the new maximum at the moment it lands**, and the sentence a member reads becomes true again there. **Folded into SPEC §7**, which now states the clamp. **The code does not do this yet** and the promise test locks the opposite: the clamp is a build of its own — engine-core's rate handling, `promise-rate.test.ts`'s fold case turned, and the ⏱️ amendment path in `engine-bridge`. **980 serves ✋ and 🖼️ at the save, and lets the founding walk past them** (Ed, 2026-08-28, plan-queue backlog entry 179: *✋ and 🖼️ should both appear together after the birth, and not block the path*). They had been rows 10 and 11 of `ORDER`, born one after the other between 🎩 and 💤, and `blocksOrder` treated every non-gate card as a blocker until it settled — so a founder could not reach 💤 until they had OK'd a name and then OK'd a picture, one at a time, in the middle of the constitution. Ed: **both born at the save alongside the pen, and neither holds the queue.** The reasoning, in the order it decides things: **a blank is a real answer** on both — a blank name is Anonymous (SPEC §9.0c: *a name, not a gap*) and a blank picture is initials — so there is nothing the constitution is waiting to learn from either, which is what makes walking past them lossless rather than a deferral. **They are personal and bind nobody**, so they do not belong in the single file the way a setting does. And **they stand above ✒️**, which needed its own argument, the pen's rule being that *every card below it in the order is committed with the very pen it hands over*: the rule does not reach a pair committed with no power at all. The mechanism is a flag, **`blocks: false` on the two card literals**, read by `blocksOrder` and deliberately not `isGate`, which also means news-not-question, hidden-from-strangers, no composer and a dozen other things none of which is true of a personal card. `spec-check`'s `checkOrder` reads the flag off the literals and asserts SURFACE §8's *blocks?* column against it, so the exemption cannot be widened silently; SURFACE F2 and F3 carry the rule, and `journey` asserts the pair adjacent, after 📧 and before 🌍 — position rather than adjacency to the pen, since the walk takes rail entries in document order and may meet 🛡️ first. **They arrive *together*** for a reason worth stating: 🖼️ follows ✋ in `ORDER`, so the instant ✋ stops blocking, `orderReady(mypic)` is true exactly when `orderReady(myname)` is. A **copy correction** rides with it, because serving ✋ at the save serves it *before* 🎩 is answered — so almost every founder meets the member branch of its note first and a clerk sees theirs only by reopening the card, and both branches now have to be true on their own: neither says *optional* as though the other were not, the clerk's naming the *Founded by* line and the member's saying it is how you appear in the room. **One thing the build reasoned about and deliberately did not change**, recorded because plan-queue **95** widens the same predicate one plan later: `nothingElseServed` (`session-view.html`) is `!servedCards().some((c) => !c.isBegin && !remedyOnly(c))`, and `beginOffered` consults it as the **last-resort 🍾 door** whenever `readiness()` is not ready — so two cards that stand served and unsettled make it false. They are **not** exempted, and should not be: an unanswered ✋ is genuinely something being served, and a 🍾 offered over it would be the door opening while a real task stands. Nothing is lost, because both are always committable — ✋ is `ready: () => true` and 🖼️ has no `CHOSEN` entry — so F18 holds (the founder in the `one-voice` dead end is served ✋, 🖼️ and the ✉️ remedy, all three actionable) and the door opens on the next press. Before this change the pair could not be unanswered in that state at all, the single file having made the founder pass them to reach a delegation; after it, the dead end costs two presses more and no reachability. **Spent.** 981 and 982 are open above — SPEC §9.0c's *never asked at the founding*, which this makes sharper, and the `--delegate-all` mood that Q967's rename blinded, found while trying to walk the paragraph above rather than argue it.

**1050–1052 are the three rulings of 2026-08-29 (afternoon) that the register never held**, answered while batch X's plans were being written and recorded here as decided rather than filed above, the way 1035–1037 were. **1050 — *143 stands; 191 becomes §8.1 as a table.*** The question was whether entry 220's measurement lifts entry 143's binding ruling on the SURFACE pass (*refactor, not cull — every row and every cell of every table stays; no retire verdict for a table row, a rule id or a heading*), given that the arithmetic of a cut respecting it reaches 70,494 bytes at best and a 63,000 target cannot be met without cutting text a recorded ruling stands behind. Ed: **143 stands**, and entry 191 is redefined — the SURFACE work owed is now the **§8.1 tabulation**, which is **1006** above, rather than a whole-file cut. Two consequences worth stating: the byte target for SURFACE is whatever the tabulation produces and is not itself the object; and *refactor, not cull* is a ruling about **SURFACE.md**, whose tables are its substance — it is not lifted onto SPEC.md or `CLAUDE.md`, both of which are governed by their own rules (the spec-pass procedure and the five admission questions). **Where this stands 2026-09-01**: the written extraction that **1009** commissioned alongside the tabulation turns out to have been performed already, by entry 191's own commit `18710a9` (see 1009 above), so what entry 191 *became* is exactly what this ruling redefined it as — **1006**'s §8.1 tabulation is the whole of the SURFACE work still owed, and the byte target still follows it rather than the other way about. `SURFACE.md` stands at **95,917 B** against the 70,000 watch, verified by plan 139, which built nothing into it. **1051 — the byte target is *a consequence, never a criterion.*** Put on `CLAUDE.md`: the file carries Ed's *no byte budget* ruling twice (**Q723–731**) — the pruning question is *asked at every extraction and never as a byte cull*, and an unguarded gotcha *is capped by nothing* — while plan-queue watches the file at 100,000 bytes, so a plan aiming at 90,000 is on its face the cull that ruling forbids. Ed: **a consequence, never a criterion.** So nothing is removed because the file is long, every removal is justified by the pruning test or by authorship, and a pass that applies both honestly and lands above the number has **passed**, not failed; the number is reported, never chased. This is the same words the entry-47 audit already used of its own arithmetic (`design/spec-pass/claude-md-audit.md`, *A consequence, not a goal*), now a ruling rather than a session's care. Folded into `CLAUDE.md`'s admission rule by **plan 120**, whose step 6 is the paragraph that carries it. **1052 — *you mark the keepers first.*** The question was how a document pass tells Ed's words from a session's when every commit in the repository is authored `edsaperia` and most carry a `Co-Authored-By: Claude` trailer — 92 commits on `SPEC.md`, 264 on `CLAUDE.md` — so `git blame`'s author field says *100% session-written* about files that are full of Ed's decisions, and taken literally would authorise deleting them. Ed: **you mark the keepers first.** So the order of work inverts: a pass makes one marking sweep over the section and marks every paragraph that carries a human decision — an `Ed, 2026-MM-DD` attribution, a `Qnnn` or entry reference, a verbatim quotation, an answer folded from one — **before** it judges anything for removal, and what carries no mark is the candidate set. Blame is still run, for *which commit* a paragraph arrived in and what that commit was for, but it is corroboration and never the test. Both document plans in batch X are written the other way round — cut-first, provenance as a filter — and are told so in their batch notes; neither ruling nor plan makes Ed himself the marker, and a pass that finds it cannot mark a paragraph either way has found the question its block exists for.

Everything below 260 that does not appear as an open, deferred or backlog item above is spent. Where the content went:

- **309** — the rail crowding at a clause with twelve decisions: settled by Ed 2026-08-17 and built the same day, and settled *against* the option I raised it with. I had proposed a pile in the rail, one entry per clause expanding on click, mirroring the `tab-stack`. Ed: *rather than have queue-card piles, we want to prioritise them in the sidebar in the same way that the tabs prioritise.* Which is right, and cheaper: the rail already had an admission rule (most urgent first, never a ranking over position) and simply had no tiebreak for entries at the **same** clause, so it was falling through to fixture order. Sorting those by the tab stack's own keys makes the two columns agree — whichever decision the gutter would open is the one the rail shows — and needs no new object. Building it exposed that the gutter had no tiebreak either, so the two were promptly made to share one `leverage` comparator rather than two copies of a formula. The general lesson is worth keeping: **when two surfaces annotate the same thing, an ordering they do not share is a disagreement waiting to be noticed.**

- **294** — clauses with many tabs, all three parts closed by Ed on 2026-08-17 and built the same day. **Order** and **volume** went with the `tab-stack`; **filed decisions** with the `filedpile` at the bottom of a card's tab strip, opening on click with the card growing to hold them. Reasoning in the design notes; the named parts are in CLAUDE.md. It also turned up a branch that had never run: the document only swallowed a clause into its record where the clause had nothing live on it, which had never been wrong because until the pile there was no way to reach a filed decision from a busy clause.

- **307** — where 50% is on a retired card, once the incumbent moved to the head: settled by Ed 2026-08-17 as **(a)**, leave it. *I don't think anyone will miss it, and you can understand what happened from the other things on the card.* My recommendation had been (b), a 50% rule in the field; (a) is the better answer for the reason the whole card was rebuilt on — the eyebrow already states the score against the bar, and adding a second device to say a third true thing is how the card got to three bands in the first place.
