1209. **§4 T2's number example names a title that does not exist.** (Raised by the documents pass of 2026-09-07, STYLE.md log §6 item 4.) *"How many ✏️s do members start with? wants a number"* — no card has carried that title; ⏱️ is *Proposal Rate* and states its rule as one sentence (item 79). The T2 row's examples are current. Readings: (a) keep it as an illustration of the rule's shape; (b) replace it with a live title that wants a number — none is a question any more (*Quorum*, *Proposal Pass Threshold* are the nouns the same bullet exempts), which is itself a sign the example has aged; (c) drop the number half and keep *Is the Founder a Member?*. **Ruled by Ed, 2026-09-07, in two parts.** On the examples: *It should be examples* — T2 keeps both and says they are the shape, not cards. And then, unprompted: *But I think we should change the titles! e.g. "Quorum" => "Choose the Quorum"*; asked how far that reaches (nouns only · the two terms of art · everything): *review all titles and use whatever you think is most natural case by case; an imperative or a question; it should be clear the user has a choice to make, and what the nature of that choice is.* So T2's exemption for *Quorum* and *Approval threshold* as nouns is reversed: a settings title is an ask. The review is a copy pass and moved to Backlog under this number, waiting on Q331 (the settled title).

331. **Should a settled setting be titled differently from an outstanding one?** (Ed answered the first half on 2026-08-18: *whatever seems easiest to understand — can you tell what the type of the answer is by the title?* So a title says what kind of answer it wants, and consistency is not the point; four titles changed and two terms of art stayed nouns.) What is left is the half his rule does not reach. A card outstanding is a **question**, and *Is there a machine member?* is exactly right for it. The same card settled is a **rule**, and it stays in the pile at the head of the document as part of the constitution — where *Approval threshold, 66%* reads better than *How sure must the room be? 66%*, because a constitution is a list of what is so and not a list of what was asked. Three ways. (a) **One title throughout**, the question, and accept that the head of the document reads as an interview. (b) **Two labels on one card**, the question while it wants you and the noun once it is settled — truer to both, at the cost of a rule about which shows and of a tab whose name changes under you. (c) **The question is the title and the noun is the value line**, which is nearly what happens already: *When does it end?* over *Thursday 18:00*. Recommendation: **(c)**, on the grounds that it needs nothing new — the pile is read by its glyphs and its values far more than by its titles, and a card nobody has to re-learn is worth more than a heading that reads perfectly. **Ruled by Ed, 2026-09-07: (b), two labels on one card**, against the recommendation — put to him the same morning he made every settings title an ask (Q1209), because *Choose the Quorum · 5* at the head of a constitution is not a rule. The ask while the card wants you, the noun once settled; which shows is the card's state and the tab and rail follow it. STYLE T2 states it; the build is the title plan under Backlog 1209.

189. **"Hot", "warm", "cool" are three different vocabularies wearing one word** **Closed by Ed, 2026-09-07 (Q1210 (a)):** the tiers have left the code and the rail is one size; nothing is left to name.

    **Where it stands (docs pass, 2026-09-07):** the tiers this names have left the code — `design/session.js` has no `'warm'` or `'cool'` and *tier* survives in one comment; every rail entry has been one size since 2026-08-16. Whether anything remains to rename is Ed's (log Q1).

    (raised 2026-08-16, Ed's question — he asked where the terms come from and whether they are well defined; the honest answer is that two of the three are mine and one is the spec's, and they do not mean the same thing). (a) SPEC §8.3's **hot set** is a real defined term: the ~3 races receiving concentrated sampling at any moment — a property of the *router*, global, the same for everybody. (b) SPEC §3.2's **care-map cold** is also defined: a span the group is indifferent about, which keeps its incumbent cheaply and sinks in the feed — a property of the *group's* attitude to a clause. (c) The mockup's **hot / warm / cool tiers** are neither: they are three buckets of the per-member `urgency` scalar at 0.66 and 0.33, invented for the rail's compression ladder (Q104), personal rather than global, and unrelated to (a) or (b) — a card can be mockup-"hot" while not being in the router's hot set, and a care-map-cold span would show as mockup-"cool" only by coincidence. Three fixes, pick one: rename the tiers to something with no thermal meaning (`full` / `brief` / `line`, describing what is drawn rather than what is meant); rename them to what they measure (`yours-most` / `yours` / `background`); or define the collision away by making the tiers actually derive from the router's hot set, which would be a mechanism change rather than a naming one. I lean to the first — the tiers are a *drawing* decision and naming them after the drawing keeps them honestly separate from both spec terms.

196. **Where should the tier thresholds sit?** **Closed by Ed, 2026-09-07 (Q1210 (a)):** no fixed cuts are left in the code to move.

    **Where it stands (docs pass, 2026-09-07):** as 189 — there are no fixed cuts left in the code to move (log Q1).

    (raised 2026-08-16, Ed's ask; the fixture is now rich enough to answer it — Q194 done.) With ten more suggestions spread down the urgency range, the current cuts at **0.66 / 0.33** give 3 hot, 8 warm, 8 cool. The middle bucket being the largest is probably the crowding Ed felt. Three ways to rebalance: (a) raise the warm/cool cut to ~0.45, which moves four entries down to one-liners and leaves ~4 warm; (b) raise both, to ~0.75 / 0.45, which also thins hot to 2 and makes the flame rarer still; (c) stop using fixed cuts and take the top *n* by urgency for each tier, so the ladder's shape is stable however many suggestions exist — the honest version if the rail is meant to feel the same at 20 suggestions and at 60. I lean to (c) with n≈2 hot and n≈5 warm, but it should be looked at rather than reasoned about.

278. **Signed or anonymous — the surface** **Closed by Ed, 2026-09-07 (Q1212 (a)):** every half is built or filed — 👤 and 👁️ in the founding order (SURFACE §8), the signed face (K28, K30; Q1075–1079), the record's reveal under Q996.

No ruling closes it (log Q3).

    (mechanism **settled by Ed 2026-08-17 and folded into SPEC v0.19**; the surface **postponed by Ed 2026-08-17** until the founding-ceremony work, which is where it belongs — the ceremony is what asks these questions) (§3.5a, §9.0a, Appendix A). Kept here only for what is *not* settled: nothing about the surface. Nobody has designed how the founding ceremony asks these questions, how a signed rationale renders beside the blank-disc ones it sits among, or what the record shows when judgments are revealed after a decision. The mechanism half is below.

    **The faces half is closed** (Q854, 2026-08-26). `CLAUDE.md`'s `me` entry had hung *whether other people's faces may appear at all* on this question, and it was never this question's to answer. **Showing who is in the room is membership, and the register is public**: §9.0c settles a name and a picture as personal, binding nobody, and `MemberRowView` in `packages/constitution/src/view.ts` projects name, picture and arrival to every seat by design, with its own note saying why. What §3.5a seals is **whose name is on a proposal** — a document showing fourteen named people and not one named candidate is the ordinary case, and the membership names never pass through the anonymity rung, the list reading the roster row directly. So faces on the register, on the Members list and on the Founded line are not a disclosure question, and no §3.4 citation belongs anywhere near them: §3.4 is *Speech*. What stays open above is the authorship surface and nothing else.

319. **Where do the setup piles live once drafting starts?** **Closed by Ed, 2026-09-07 (Q1213 (a)), as built:** the piles are the constitution at the head of the document (setup-band, constitution-section; Q942 files settled motions behind the rule); the freeze half is retired (Q1196–1199).

    **Where it stands (docs pass, 2026-09-07):** overtaken by the build — the constitution is document text at the head of the charter and its tabs stay for the life of the document (`setup-band`, `constitution-section`; Q942 files settled motions behind the rule); the perpetual-document half asked about §9.5's freeze and thaw, which Q1196–1199 retired. No ruling closes it (log Q4).

    (raised 2026-08-18, the loose end in Ed's *when the ceremony is done we end up with a tab-group at the top of the document next to the title*.) Both setup surfaces now end in exactly that, and `session-view` has nothing of the kind: a live member cannot ask what the bar is, who may be seen, or when the window closes without leaving the document. The obvious answer is that they simply **stay** — it is at the head of the charter, every tab grey, every card read-only, and clicking one opens it over the top of the document exactly as it did during setup. Which would make setup and session literally the same screen in the last place they still differ. Two things to settle first: whether two permanent piles at the top of a charter earn their space in a session where nobody is asking about them, and what happens on a **perpetual** document, where §9.5's freeze and thaw mean the constitution can be re-opened and the group would have live tabs again.

325. *(Partly overtaken 2026-08-18 evening: the file merged into `design/setup.html` (361), so no file carries the name any more — what remains to decide is only what the glossary calls the stage.)* **Should `founding-ceremony` keep its name now that “ceremony” has left the surface?** (raised 2026-08-18.) But the file, the glossary entry and half the reasoning still call it the founding ceremony, which is now a private word for a thing the product calls something else, and that is exactly the drift the glossary exists to stop. (b) **Keep `founding-ceremony` as the internal name** on the grounds that it names the *stage* precisely and internal names may be more technical than copy — which is true of `race` and `adoption-threshold` already. (c) **Rename the concept but keep the file**, which is the worst of both. Recommendation: **(a)**, done as its own mechanical pass so the diff is a rename and nothing else.

417. **The setup surface has no wallet, so nothing teaches what a proposal costs** **Closed by Ed, 2026-09-07 (Q1215 (a)):** there is one surface and it carries its wallets (SURFACE §7); the gesture is R-059 and §7.2's switch.

    **Where it stands (docs pass, 2026-09-07):** overtaken — `setup.html` is a redirect and every surface is the session-view with its wallets (SURFACE §7), and the gesture (c) asked about is ruled: every hold is one second (R-059) and §7.2's commit-gesture switch says whether a commit is a click or a hold. No ruling closes it (log Q6).

    (raised 2026-08-19, from the copy pass). Ed removed "Costs one ✏️, which you get back if you withdraw it" on the right grounds — *the flying pencil teaches this* — but the flying pencil is session-view's, and setup.html has neither an `edit-wallet` in its topbar nor either flight. So a member composing a motion there now sees no price at all, and the withdraw hands back something they never saw leave. Three things would have to travel together, and only the first is mechanical: (a) the wallet in the topbar, its drip and its cap; (b) `arcFrames` / `refundFlight` / the `walletShow`+`walletGhost` render-state pair, lifted out of session-view into the shared layer — which means cards.js, and therefore a session-probe run against the frozen reference; (c) **the gesture**, which is a real design choice rather than a port: session-view spends an edit on a *hold* (the pencil's flight is the progress meter), while a motion here commits on a *click*, and a click has no duration for a pencil to cross. Either the ordinary motion commit becomes a hold like session-view's, or the outbound flight becomes something a click can carry (the pencil leaving the wallet as the card closes). The constitutional route is unaffected — 🏛️ is already a ten-second hold and costs no ✏️.

490. **Does the alpha's usability come before Postgres?** **Closed by Ed, 2026-09-07 (Q1216 (a)):** stage 8 landed 2026-08-21, Resend sends from docs.vote, Postgres stands behind the two-variable cutover; the order is what happened.

    **Where it stands (docs pass, 2026-09-07):** overtaken — stage 8 landed 2026-08-21, invitations send through Resend from docs.vote, and `PgPersistence` exists behind a two-variable cutover (CLAUDE.md `server`, `Persistence`); the order it asked about is history. No ruling recorded (log Q7).

    (raised in housekeeping, 2026-08-20, reading PRODUCTION.md's stage order against what docs.vote can actually do today.) Two stages stand between *live* and *a friend can use it*, and both sit behind stage 6's 2–3 weeks of database work. **Stage 9** (Resend on mail.docs.vote) is the plan's own "the product actually works": until it lands the sandbox sender delivers only to Ed's own address, so an invitation goes nowhere and a document cannot have a second member. **Stage 8** (the surface merge) fills the hole the plan itself names — `session-view.html` is never served, so a constituted document has **no drafting surface**: docs.vote today can found a constitution and then cannot draft the thing the constitution is about. Meanwhile the case for Postgres-first is real and not to be waved away — it is durability, and every day of JSONL is a day where a disk incident loses documents that were somebody's actual constitution, with no backups until stage 11. The tension is that the current order optimises for *not losing* data the alpha is not yet generating, because the alpha cannot yet generate it. Three shapes: **(a)** as written — durability first, on the reasoning that the moment there is anything to lose it is too late to be building the store; **(b)** 9 then 6 — mail is 2–3 days and turns a demo into a product with real users, and those users are what makes stage 6 urgent rather than theoretical; **(c)** 9, then 8, then 6 — the whole alpha experience first, accepting that a JSONL disk holds a handful of Ed-and-friends documents for a month, with a nightly copy off the disk as the cheap interim (an hour's work, not stage 11's drill). My recommendation is **(c) with the interim backup**, and the reason is what the alpha is *for*: the thing that is scarce right now is not durability, it is finding out whether the mechanism survives contact with five real people, and neither of the two stages that lets it be tried is expensive. If it is (a), the honest consequence to accept is that docs.vote stays a founding demo for a month, and the alpha flag should probably say so.

516. **The 🛡️ wording, and whether 🍾 has a wallet.** **Closed by Ed, 2026-09-07 (Q1217 (a)):** (i) superseded by Q507 (one voice, *at will*), Q615 (yes/no titles) and Q1121 (the names); (ii) built — 🍾 has no wallet.

    **Where it stands (docs pass, 2026-09-07):** (ii) is built — 🍾 has no wallet and its commit wears its own glyph (CLAUDE.md, *🍾 has no wallet*); (i) never got a ruling, and the power lines have been rewritten since (Q507 → STYLE audit item 30 in `design/DECISIONS.md`; Q615's yes/no titles; Q1121's names) (log Q8).

    Two threads from Ed, 2026-08-21.
    **(i) 🛡️'s sentence.** *at will* is settled for ✒️ and every line now uses it; *requires assent* is "ok" but not loved. The suggestion that follows Ed's own description of the pair — *a philosophical sword and shield: one writes, one only refuses* — is to make the two clauses mirror each other: **The Founder may change this at will.** / **The Founder may refuse a change the membership makes.** *May change* against *may refuse* says the asymmetry in the verbs themselves, needs no term of art, and reads as one sentence of a document rather than as a rule about a mechanism. Alternatives: *Nothing the membership decides takes effect until the Founder accepts it* (longest, clearest about the consequence); *The Founder has a veto over what the membership decides* (shortest, but *veto* is a borrowed word this vocabulary has avoided); or keep *requires assent*, which is the only one that survives being said about a **setting** as well as about a person. Whichever wins, the negatives follow it: *does not change this at will* / *may not refuse a change the membership makes*.
    **(ii) Does 🍾 have a wallet?** My answer is **no** — and the reason is the family's own test. The four wallets are the four verbs, and the four verbs are a ladder of **who has to agree**: 🪶 nobody (nothing exists yet), ✒️ nobody (you hold the power), ✏️ enough of the room, 🏛️ everybody. Each is a *capacity you hold* — spent and refilled, or held permanently. 🍾 is not a level of authority and not a capacity; it is a **moment**, and it happens once. A wallet holding one thing once is a button with a balance drawn on it. It would also beg a 🥂 wallet for the mirror act, and the close is precisely the act nobody performs — the clock does it. So: not overboard on the four, but 🍾 is where the family stops. **What is worth fixing** is what prompted the question: 🍾's commit currently reads **✒️ Begin**, borrowing the drafting pen for an act that is not drafting — beginning is what *ends* the founding. Options: **(a)** the button becomes **🍾 Begin** and the hold flies the 🍾 itself from the button into the document (a pop, not a spend) — the hold machinery keys on the glyph, so this is a real change rather than a relabel; **(b)** leave it as ✒️ Begin, on the grounds that the founder's last act with the pen is laying it down. I recommend (a).

919. **💤 cannot be rebuilt from the module, and everything below it in the founding order vanishes for every member.** **Closed 2026-09-07 (Q1224), verified against the tree:** (a) built (`hydrateFromModule` splits the rung from the day count); (b) built by another road — `hydrateFromModule` rebuilds `S.seen` from `csState` on every hydrate, so the live path never depends on page-local seen for a setting (session-view.html, the CARDS loop after `owedOks`), the birth acts are marked seen there, and ✋/🖼️ answer off `view.identity` (Q645). **Correction, later the same morning (the seat-matrix re-read, Q1205): that was wrong.** The CARDS loop lived in `hydrateS`, which runs once at boot; the 4s poll ran `hydrateValues` alone, the value half. A member's page open across a later founder act never learned the setting settled, `blocksOrder` hid every card below it, and the band stopped dead for as long as the tab stayed open, while a page booted a minute later carried everything — the walk's whole member-hat cluster. **Built 2026-09-07:** the loop is `hydrateSeen(withOks)`; boot calls it with the acknowledgement half, the poll without (an OK pressed between two polls must not be un-pressed by a view fetched before the command landed, Q846's family). The mistake worth naming: I read the loop and not its caller, and *rebuilt on every hydrate* was true of a function the poll never called.

    **Where it stands (docs pass, 2026-09-07):** (a) is built — `hydrateFromModule` splits the rung from the day count (`design/session-view.html:9572–9573`, entry 166); whether (b), `S.seen` rebuilt on every poll, landed is unverified (log Q15).

    *(seat matrix, first run 2026-08-27 — a page finding the run made, recorded and not fixed; it is the one thing standing between the harness and exit 0.)* `hydrateFromModule`'s 💤 line writes the **day count** into `S.lapse` — the field the card's rung radio reads (`days` | `never`) — and never sets `S.lapseDays`, the number the *They lapse* rung carries; so on any document whose 💤 is a number of days, `CHOSEN.lapse` is false after every reload and every poll, 💤 reads as unsettled, and `orderReady` withholds every card below it in `ORDER` — 💡 ⚖️ 🏛️ ⏱️ 🤖 ⏰ 🌡️ 👥 👤 👁️ 📄 — from every member's page and from the founder's own after a reload. The run showed it four ways: the founder reloaded at 🍾 was asked 💤 again (`rail ["lapse"]`); `early` and `lapsed` were owed 💡 and ⚖️ by the module and carried neither (E4, *the module owes it too: a page finding*); `late` was owed ⏰ at the close and carried nothing (E5 `ending`); and after the ladder's reload the founder's rail read `["lapse", …]` with 💤 long since set. The fixture never sees it because the fixture never rehydrates, and `journey` never sees it because its guest asserts nothing below 💤. The harness works round the founder's half only — 💤 answered on the card after the reload, then the minute over the wire — and the members' half cannot be worked round. A second, smaller half: `S.seen` and `nameSet`/`picSet` are rebuilt only by `hydrateS` at boot, so a page open through a founder's later act never learns the setting is settled until it reloads. **(a)** Fix the hydration line: the rung into `S.lapse` (`days`/`never`) and the count into `S.lapseDays` — two lines, and `journey` gains an assertion below 💤 on the guest. **(b)** (a), plus rebuild `S.seen` from the module on every poll, the way `okd` already is (`syncOwedOks`), so an open page learns of a settling it did not perform. **(c)** Leave it and let the seat matrix stay red on it. I recommend **(a) now and (b) as its own decision**, since (b) changes what a poll may do to the page the reader is looking at. Until (a) lands the seat matrix exits 1 with fifteen findings, every one of them this. — **Answered 2026-08-29 (Ed): (b)** — *Also rebuild the page's record of what has been settled on every poll.* So both halves, and the second is the one that was held back for its own decision: the hydration line splits (the rung into `S.lapse`, the day count into `S.lapseDays`), **and** `S.seen` is rebuilt from the module on every poll the way `okd` already is (`syncOwedOks`), so a page open through a founder's later act learns of a settling it did not perform. Ed has ruled on what (b) costs — a poll may now change what the reader is looking at — so the build does not re-ask it. **Answered, owed, not built**, and it stays here until a plan lands it; `journey` gains an assertion below 💤 on the guest, and the seat matrix stops exiting 1 on this.

920. **A clerk founder is served the voice they do not hold, and 🍾 waits on it for ever.** **Verified NOT built on 2026-09-07 (Q1224), then built the same morning as (a):** the fold wrote the roster and never `convenor.isMember`, and the server served `convenorRecord().isMember` verbatim (server.ts, the view's `convenor`), so a clerk's document said `isMember: true` for ever — the seat matrix's whole clerk cascade (`no begin card to hold · readiness ready · rail ["grant-voice"]`, seen again this morning under Q1205). `convenorRecord()` now reports `isMember` from the roster and the fold keeps the struct in step; `identity.test.ts`'s 🎩 re-tick case asserts both directions.

    **Where it stands (docs pass, 2026-09-07):** answered (a), owed — the fold now compares the answer against the roster (`packages/constitution/src/session.ts:351`), but `convenorRecord()` still returns the struct with its `isMember` field (`session.ts:2900`); not verified as the ruled shape (log Q15).

    *(seat matrix, first run 2026-08-27, clerk hat — a fold finding, recorded and not fixed.)* `set-convenor-membership { isMember: false }` moves the founder off the roster and records the act (`membershipSet: true`), but the fold never touches `convenor.isMember` — the struct field set once at creation (`session.ts` L112, the `created` fold) — and `convenorRecord()` hands that struct back verbatim, so `view.convenor.isMember` stays `true` on a clerk's document and the page's `viewerIsMember()` reads the clerk as a member. On the clerk document the founder's rail carried `grant-voice` as news before 🍾 (`no begin card to hold · readiness {"ready":true,…} · rail ["grant-voice"]`), `beginOffered` held 🍾 shut behind the voice's OK — which the harness rightly refuses to give for a clerk — and the document never began, so every later row on that hat is the same finding cascading (E4, E5, E21, E24, the lapse wait, both ladder rungs). No walk founds as a clerk (`journey`, `ladder`, `founding-walk` all found a member), which is how it stayed invisible; 🎩's own case in `founding.test.ts` reads the roster, not the view. **(a)** `convenorRecord()` (or the view builder) reports `isMember` from the roster — `members.has(convenor.id)` — and the struct field is retired or kept in step by the fold; one case on the clerk's view. **(b)** Keep the field and update it in the `convenor-membership-set` fold. ## CLAUDE.md, two guarded gotchas reduced 2026-09-07 (Q1241, Q1242)

By the eviction rule (Q736): a gotcha whose mistake is caught by a named automated guard reduces to one line and its post-mortem moves here. Both paragraphs verbatim as CLAUDE.md held them on 2026-09-07, before the reduction.

**The double fire (Q1241; guard: `npm run journey`'s refused list).** A completed hold clicks for you, and that click must not look like the user's. The hold's timer calls `click()` itself; the browser then delivers its own click on pointerup, and the guard that swallows that trailing half keyed on a flag the synthetic click had just cleared — so **every held commit on this surface fired twice** (Ed, 2026-08-22: *during the birth, after entering the email, the Link card opens immediately*). The two clicks land a millisecond apart, and `closeThen` defers a commit behind the collapse, so `S.open` is still set when the second arrives and the whole act runs again: on 📧 that is a second `POST /api/docs` asking for the address the first had just **reserved for itself**, answered truthfully with *that address is taken* — and the page did the right thing with the wrong news and walked the founder back to 📍. `penHoldFired` is true for exactly the duration of the synthetic dispatch, so inside a click handler it means precisely *this click is the hold's own*, and the flag is left alone for the real one. The birth also guards its own send, so no future double press can take the address from the creation making it. *Why the journey walk is the guard:* its own comment of 2026-08-22 — *a refused command is a failure even when the walk recovers from it* — was written for exactly this bug, which the walk had driven straight through; the second 📧 send's 409 now lands in `refused` and the walk is red.

**🎩 on a reloaded document (Q1242; guard: `npm run ladder`'s session rung).** 🎩 is settled once the document begins, and `settled()` must say so (Ed's live walk, 2026-08-21). 🎩 is not a catalogue setting, so `csState('hat')` is null and `hydrateS` can reconstruct it from nothing: on any reloaded live document it stood unanswered for ever. Harmless until the gates joined `ORDER` — then everything below 🎩 waited on a question that could not settle, so **💡 and ⚖️ never reached the rail, no gate could be acknowledged, no ✏️ wallet ever arrived, 🪪 never appeared, and most of the constitution's clauses were invisible**. §9.6a locks 🎩 at the start, and a locked card is settled: `S.seen.has('hat') || constituted()`. The general lesson is the one this file already teaches about the fixture — **a card whose settledness lives only in `S` is a card the live path cannot rebuild**, so every such card needs a truth the module can answer for. *Why the ladder is the guard:* the ladder bar reloads the page after every press, so its session rung is a reloaded live document past 🍾, and the rung checks *the ✏️ wallet is drawn* — the very thing this regression made never arrive.

What the walk establishes about engine-core's `Constitution`, field by field.

**Room-agreed (→ `RoomSettings`, the constitution proper):**

| engine field | card | notes |
|---|---|---|
| `adoptionThresholdStart/End` | ✒️ approval threshold | shape implicit (start=end ⇒ fixed); see 341 |
| `windowStartMs/EndMs` | ⏰ when does it end | perpetual = no end; start semantics are 342 |

**Room-agreed but missing from the engine entirely:**

| setting | card | engine today |
|---|---|---|

| judgments-reveal | 👁️ | absent |

**Engine tuning (→ `EngineTuning`, never on a card, never in a motion):**

— now the adoption floor, SPEC §4.2 — ✍️ signing, 👁️ judgments, 🌍

holds both bags — `adoptionThresholdStart` (:22) beside `cooldownMs` (:42),

335. **Split `Constitution` into what the room agreed and what the engine is tuned to** **Closed by Ed, 2026-09-07 (Q1267 (c)): done by the constitution package.** The room-agreed half — the 18-setting catalogue, the consent rule, the motions — left engine-core's reach on 2026-08-19 as `@draft/constitution`; engine-core's own `Constitution` stays one object, tuned by Appendix A and the operator's variables, and that is accepted. REVIEW-creation-session.md, kept for this, is deleted; its §7 is in this file above.

    **Where it stands (docs pass, 2026-09-07):** half done — SPEC's Appendix A is *Engine tuning* and §9.7.1 holds the settings (Q562); `packages/engine-core/src/types.ts` still declares one `Constitution` interface with `hotSetSize` beside the threshold (lines 16–19).

    (raised 2026-08-18, PLAN.md §2.2; expanded after Ed asked why it matters). engine-core has one object holding both — the threshold, the grant, the drip, the stake and the window on one side, and `hotSetSize`, `explorationEvery`, `boutGapMs`, `deadlockEpsilon`, `cooldownMs`, `redraftLimit` on the other. Three things go wrong while they share a name. The **record** published at the close would list a tuning constant beside the threshold as though the room had agreed it. The **motion** machinery routes on whether a setting is constitutional, and with one object there is nothing stopping somebody moving to amend `boutGapMs`. And the **ceremony** has no definable output: what the founding questions produce *is* the room’s half of this object, and it cannot produce half of a thing. The cost is a rename across engine-core and sim-harness today, against a data migration once real documents exist with saved settings. Recommendation: **now**. The only reason it is a question at all is that it touches a package that should not change without Ed’s word. **Status 2026-08-18:** the in-depth review Ed asked for is delivered as REVIEW-creation-session.md; its §7 is the definitive field-by-field mapping, and the split is one commit once he has read it (338’s answer decides one field’s home). *The document-level half landed 2026-08-22 (spec pass 1, Q562): Appendix A is now* Engine tuning *and holds only what nobody is asked; the settings are §9.7.1. The engine-core object is still one.*

1283. **`feed()` drops deadlocked races from serving, where SPEC §8.3b serves them until nothing is left for *you*.** (Found by the router re-read of 2026-09-07, Q1262 — an aside outside that item.) `feed()` filters `allRaces` to the non-deadlocked before it builds a hand, while §8.3b (R-072) says a deadlocked race *is served to you as an ordinary race, and is disclosed as deadlocked only once it has nothing left to ask you*. `nothingElseToJudge` honours the per-participant half — it asks whether *you* have a usable comparison on each deadlocked race — but the serving half reads global: once a race is deadlocked, nobody is dealt its pairs, whether or not they have judged it. Either the spec's sentence or the filter is wrong, and it is a mechanism question: does a member who has never judged a deadlocked race still get its pairs? For Ed. **Ruled by Ed, 2026-09-07: (a), the spec is right — asked for the recommendation first and given it:** deadlock is a fact about the evidence so far, a member who has never judged the race is the one source that fact does not cover (and what a bridge needs, §6.3), and dropping it from their feed withholds the question and then discloses the deadlock when they can do nothing — the freeze's shape. **Built the same afternoon:** `feed()` keeps a deadlocked race for a participant with no usable comparison on it, through one `deadlockStillAsks` test the empty-queue check reads too; `deadlock-serving.test.ts` serves the race to the unjudged member and not to the judged one.

## The applicant's live page (Q1281, built 2026-09-07)

**What 1281 was.** The server served an applicant (an `app:` cookie) a privacy-shaped payload with no `view` key — deliberate since stage 3's defect 7, so that no member's email, no question and no answer reached a seat outside the room — and the live page's boot had a door branch (`data.stranger`) and a member branch and no applicant branch. An applicant's payload has `stranger` falsy, so it fell through to `remoteCS(data)`, whose getters read `self.v.view.*` unguarded (`closed`, `closedAt`, `canPropose`, `canJudge`, `settingState`), and `clockState` was the first to throw: *Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'closed')*. Anybody who applied to a real document at docs.vote got a blank surface, for as long as applicants have existed.

**Why no walk ever saw it.** Three things stood between the defect and every guard. `liveBoot()`'s promise chain ended in `.catch((e) => console.warn('[live] boot', e && e.message))`, which swallowed the throw, so Playwright's `pageerror` hook — which every walk installs — never fired. `scripts/applicants-walk.mjs`, the one walk with an applicant in it, drove the applicant's submit by `fetch` from inside the guest page and never looked at the guest's rail, so a page that rendered nothing was indistinguishable from one that rendered everything. And `scripts/seat-matrix.mjs` caught the snapshot's throw, marked the seat `unstood` and dropped it from every audience, so the run reported itself green over it until the 2026-09-07 re-read (Q1205) made an unstood seat a printed line.

**The design: an applicant is a stranger who has knocked.** The seat matrix already said so, in its `strangers` predicate's comment. So the applicant's payload is now **the stranger's payload plus the application**: `strangerView(doc, nowMs, session)` — the rules, the gates, the text where 🌍 lets a link-holder read it, the register on the same rung, the holding sentence — with `stranger: false` so the page's door branch does not fire, `me` the applicant's seat, `applicant` their own record (`id`, `email`, `status`, `name`, `picture`, `words`, `motion`) and one new field, `judged`. The chamber's rungs are `closed · link · public`; the old applicant gate (`rung !== 'closed'`, null reading as no) and the door's `canRead` (`link | public`) agree on every one, so nothing an applicant could read before is withheld now and nothing new is shown. `judged` is how many of the electorate have voted on the admit motion — **a count, never who** (SPEC §3.5): the applicant's own card had promised *n of E have voted on it* since Q397 and had no live number to print. On the constitutional route it is the motion's answers; on the ordinary route the application is a one-candidate race in the engine (`admit:<id>`, §9.7½) and the count is the distinct members with a standing judgment on that candidate — keyed on the candidate rather than the race, because a race that adopts leaves `races()` while the motion still awaits the crown's assent, and never counting the applicant themselves, whose own voice the bridge lends the race as its author (`RaceView.distinctMovers` would have counted it). A carried motion reads as the whole electorate, as the page's fixture readout does.

On the page, `applicantAsView(d)` beside `strangerAsView` returns the stranger's projection with `me` and one `view.applicants` row in the shape `remoteCS`'s `applicantRecords` indexes; `hydrateApplicant` is the applicant's provisional layer, written from the record only where the record holds a value — the server holds nothing until Submit, so a null never overwrites a name being typed — with `submitted` derived from the status (`started · verified` no; `submitted · proposed · admitted · refused` yes). `liveBoot()` gained the branch; the poll gained the case and moves the viewer off `'applicant'` exactly as it does off `'stranger'`. **Submit goes over the wire**: `remoteCS`'s `submitApplication` shim was a no-op that returned `undefined`, which the handler read as success; it is `api.cmd('submit-application', fields)` now, and the handler — written against `api.cmd`'s contract for this day (Q346) — puts a refusal under the control that tried (E33). The applicant's charter column, read-only state and pulse follow the door's (`atTheDoor()` — the two seats outside the room), and their band opens every settings tab as the stranger's read-only settled card (Q1183) where it used to wrap an empty open paragraph. Two small things came with it: the applicant's ✓ on the name and words cards now follows the typing (their cards commit with `data-close`, which `refreshCommit` never reached, so the ✓ stayed dark until something else re-rendered), and `liveBoot()`'s catch **rethrows** out of the chain, so a boot failure is an uncaught error again.

**What asserts it now.** `npm run applicants-walk` reads the guest's page after the link — `window.__founding().viewer` is `'applicant'` and the rail holds `apply` — then fills the application in and submits it **on the surface** (name, an emoji, the words, Submit) and asserts the card reads *Submitted*; with the rethrow its `pageerror` hook fires. `npm run seat-matrix`'s `knock` step asserts the same two facts and throws otherwise, and an `unstood` seat is exit 1. A server test (`server.test.ts`, *the applicant is served the door plus their application (Q1281)*) asserts the payload's shape — `view.settings`, `view.gates`, `stranger: false`, `applicant.id`, `applicant.judged` at 0, then 0 after the applicant's own submit, then 1 after one member's judgment with the race adopted — and that no member's email and no question ever ride it. What is **not** covered: a refused applicant's card still reads *Submitted* (the fixture's behaviour, unchanged); 🪪 Admissions is absent from the applicant's `view.settings` exactly as from the stranger's (Q1280's territory).

## Two audience defects from the seat-matrix re-read (Q1280, Q1282, built 2026-09-07)

Both were found by the same instrument on the same day as Q1281 and are the same shape: a seat outside the electorate, or outside the room, served something the page's predicates were not written for. Ed asked for the three to ship together (*fix 1282 and 1280 first, then push*).

**Q1280 — the stranger's settled Admissions card had no rule block.** Opened by link on a live document, 🌍's card showed its rule as a block with the inert *Chosen by the Founder ✒️* radio and 🗑️ · OK, as Q1183 rules; 🪪's showed the strip, nothing, 🗑️ · OK. The page was not at fault: `ctx.headFor` prints `decisionLine(c)` for every settled setting, and `decisionLine` has an admission branch. What it lacked was the value — the door's payload built its `view.settings` as `CATALOGUE.filter((e) => e.kind !== 'personal' && e.id !== 'admission')`. That exclusion is from the door's first build (2026-08-21), when the setting was still called `membership` and its value was the roster list itself, a thing with no sentence to print; Q903 (2026-08-27) renamed it `admission` and made it a priced rule like 🥾, and the filter came along under the new name without anybody asking what it was for. The fix is the filter's removal — the door serves every non-personal rule, 🪪 among them — and the door's top-level `admission` price stays, since the stranger's Apply arithmetic reads it. A server test asserts the row is there. The applicant, who reads the door's payload since Q1281, gets the same row by the same change.

**Q1282 — a lapsed member was offered a constitutional answer the module refuses.** The motion card's `mustAct` was *viewer is a member, has not answered, is not excluded by the motion*, with no test of whether the membership was active. A lapse leaves the motion electorate (§9.5a), so the module refused the answer — *is not in the motion's electorate* — after the page had put the 🏛️ card in the rail and let the member press it. That is the `may*` gotcha exactly: an act you cannot take must not be offered. `viewerLapsed()` reads the viewer's own row from `memberRecords()` — the module's on the fixture, `view.members` through `remoteCS` live, both of which already carried `lapsed` for the register's *Lapsed* subsection (Y10) — and `mustAct`'s motion branch asks it. The card stays in the rail as waiting, which is what a decision the viewer has no say in looks like everywhere else on the surface; SURFACE E10's audience column already said *every active member*, so no rule moved. The 1282 note had said *as `canJudge` does*; `canJudge` is the document's judging gate and knows nothing of who is asking, so the predicate is the viewer's row instead. Guard: the seat-matrix's lapsed seat at E10, which was one of the six findings the 2026-09-07 re-read left red. The same run then reported the lapsed seat on **E21** — the admit card, whose audience cell reads *the membership* where E10's reads *every active member* — as not carrying it: the same person, two rows, two answers. The bridge suspends a lapsed participant in the engine on the lapse, so the ordinary route refuses them exactly as the constitutional one does, and the page is consistent as built; which cell is right is Q1284 (recommend E21's reads *every active member* for the card, the applicant's row staying register text everybody reads).

**Q1284, Ed's ruling (2026-09-08):** *It should be served to every active member. Lapsed members never see it as a settled grey tab, because if they were seeing things they wouldn't be lapsed. If they log in while the question is still open, then they stop being lapsed and they are served it.* E21's audience cell reads *every active member* from this date; the page stands as Q1282 built it. The ruling states a fact the code held only in part when it was made: `seen()` refuses a lapsed member on purpose (*revival is memberReturn's — an act, not a read*), so a lapsed member whose ninety-day cookie is still good could open the page lapsed and meet the grey tabs Ed says they never see — the follow-up put to him next.

**The follow-up, ruled the same day: a read revives** (SPEC v0.110, R-096). Ed chose it over keeping act-only revival with a sentence on the page (explaining a state that should not exist) and over ending the cookie at the lapse (a lapsed member unable even to read until their mail arrives). `seen()` now returns a lapsed member — and a lapsed crown — on their first read and reports something to commit, so the server's view path persists the return before it builds the view, and the first page they see is the room counting them. Three tests flipped or grew (`begin`, `membership`, `promise-lapse`); the bundle re-froze. The seat-matrix's lapsed seat, built on *a read does not revive*, now asserts the opposite: its `wait` step shuts the page until the clock lapses the seat, reopens it, and fails unless the founder's next view shows the row returned; from there the seat is an ordinary member, `every active member` no longer carves it out, and the only thing a lapsed member is ever served is mail (E22). The seat-matrix's header still records the Q919/Q920 history that named the lapsed seat's findings; that history stands as written.

## ⏳ means *waiting for other people to vote* — the entry lights on what can still be asked (Q1202, built 2026-09-08)

**What the hand-lit entry did wrong.** Since the pair deck (Q1200) a race's rail entry was lit while the served hand held a card on the race and filed ⏳ the moment it did not — `itemsFromView`'s `dealt` was the whole test. The hand is ten cards drawn from a hot set of three races, so in any room busier than the deck step's two races an entry filed ⏳ after a judgment while the engine could still ask that member a pair on the race, and re-lit later when the router's hot set came back round to the clause — `room-bots --heat 1` showed it on a nine-candidate race. A member working *by section* (Ed's second mode of engagement, below) met a grey tab on a clause they could still vote on.

**The ruling** (Ed, 2026-09-07, with neither of the two readings the build had offered): *⏳ should mean "waiting for other people to vote". If there are things you can do, it should show the symbol of that action, even if it's not urgent. My reasoning: there are two ways of engaging with a doc; resolve recommended tasks by urgency, and work on a particular section. For the latter, you don't want actions you can do to be hidden from you.* On 2026-09-08 he chose to build it as described — askability *and* the pair, so every lit entry opens a card.

**The build.** One test in the engine: `askOnRace(r, participantId)` — the deadlock filter (§8.3b, `deadlockStillAsks`) then `bestPairFor` on the race's own fit — is what the feed's two dealing loops, the empty-queue check and the new public read all call, so the hand and the per-race answer cannot disagree; `edgeCard` builds the card they all deal. `Session.askOn(participantId, raceId)` is the read: the pair the race would deal this participant, or null once nothing is left (unknown race, judged out, a race of their own text alone under R-062); `ParticipantApi.askOn(raceId)` renders it blind through the same `renderCard` as `nextCards`, with `urgency` 0 — a pair outside the hand is below everything in it and has no feed to be relative to — and no clock, since whether a pair is left does not depend on the time. The server draws the hand *before* the clause rows and each row gains `askable` (dealt, or `askOn` non-null) and `ask` (the pair, only where the hand holds no card on the race; null where it does, the hand's card being the card). The page: `rc = dealt[0] || r.ask || null`, the entry lit on `askable || rc`, ⏳ only on `!askable && judged` — one site, the same `LIVE_HOOKS.judge` posting the same `judge-race`, which accepts any pair (no served-card check) so a pair the hand never held judges as it stands. The ⏳ card stays the ledger (Q1201). The fixture is untouched: `itemsFromView` is live-only, so the probes could not move.

**Why the pair rides the view rather than a pair-on-demand route.** Blinder — one read, the same projection, no new endpoint whose answer would have to be re-argued against §3.5; and cheaper — the press opens the card from what the view already holds, no round trip, which is also why `ask` is sent only for the races the hand lacks. The cost is a few hundred bytes per undealt askable race on every poll, bounded by the number of live races.

**The guard, and what it took to reach the state.** `askable.test.ts` (engine: the undealt pair, the judged-out null, R-062, deadlock's two halves, blindness on the API), the server's Q1202 test (eleven single-challenger races against a hand of ten — the eleventh row carries its own pair; a dealt row carries none; a judged-out row files; no `"value"` on the wire), and `npm run journey`'s *askable* case. The walk's case was the expensive part: a race judged by the founder with a pair left *and* out of the hot set needs five races with the target valued lowest, and ⏱️ is one number since R-083 — the grant and cap are the mechanism's fixed 3 — so the wallets could not be raised at the founding. The third seat the walk already invites and never lands (`cy…`) is what pays for it: their three proposals make the target (two wordings on the gap after the last clause) and a neighbour, the founder's one makes another, and the founder's verdicts price them — *approve* lifts the neighbour, *keep* twice pins the target's leader at the coin flip, below every other race's — so the target is fifth of five and out of the hot set with its rival pair unjudged. The precondition is read off the wire (no card on the target in the hand) and is its own FAIL line, so a walk that lands the target in the hand says *not exercised* rather than passing on the deck's behaviour. Two lessons kept: a walk's server must be booted with `DRAFT_BASE_URL` naming the host the walk attaches to (the CI comment already said so; against a `localhost` link the deck step's cookie jar is empty and reads *log in first*), and under `--shape=…` the wallets are still three, so the case runs there too.

**What the walk found on its first run: every gap race shares one incumbent id.** The incumbent is positional — `incumbentIdFor` hashes the text the contested spans displace (§4.4) — so two insertions at different lines, both displacing nothing, get the same `inc:` id, and so would two clauses with identical wording. `raceView`'s `touches` matched a judgment to a race on *either* side against a set holding the incumbent, so the founder's verdict on the neighbour gap was filed under the target too: the target read `judged` before anybody had judged it, its ledger listed a foreign pair, and the walk's count came back 4 where 3 stood. The clause rows now use `onRace` — both sides in the race — which also keeps a salience diagonal (one side in each of two races) out of a clause's ledger, where the page could never draw it; the records keep `touches`, since their set holds candidate ids alone. Guard: the server's Q1202 test, two gap races sharing an incumbent, one judged, the other untouched.

## Every settings title is an ask; a settled card wears its noun (Q1209, Q331 (b), built 2026-09-08)

**The rulings.** Ed, 2026-09-07, on Q1209 — a question that had only asked about T2's examples: *It should be examples. But I think we should change the titles! e.g. "Quorum" => "Choose the Quorum"*; and on the scope: *review all titles and use whatever you think is most natural case by case; an imperative or a question; it should be clear the user has a choice to make, and what the nature of that choice is.* A bare noun is not an ask. Ed, 2026-09-07, on Q331 (b): **two labels on one card** — the ask while the card is outstanding, the noun once it is settled; which shows is the card's state; the tab and the rail follow the card. *The pile at the head of the document reads as rules, the rail as asks.* Ed, 2026-09-08: the table below approved as it stood.

**The table** — twenty-two cards, `design/copy.js`'s CARDS block, `t` the ask and `n` the noun:

| key | today | ask (outstanding) | noun (settled) | why |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| title | Title | Name the Document | Title | the first act — an imperative says something is wanted |
| myemail | Your Email | Enter Your Email | Your Email | a field, so *enter* |
| slug | Link | Choose the Link | Link | the machine suggests one and you may change it, so *choose* |
| shape | What Type of Document Is This? | (kept) | Document Type | already a question |
| admission | Admissions | How Does Somebody Join? | Admissions | three prices on one scale — the question names what is priced |
| invite | Invite a Member | (kept) | — | a door: no settled state, one label |
| remove | Remove a Member | (kept) | — | a door |
| hat | Is the Founder a Member? | (kept) | Founder’s Membership | already a question |
| applications | Applications | Can Strangers Apply? | Applications | one switch, yes or no |
| myname | Your Name | Choose Your Name | Your Name | how you appear in the room — a choice |
| mypic | Your Picture | Choose Your Picture | Your Picture | three blocks to choose from |
| text | Text | (kept) | Text | exempt — 📝 is never a task and never an OK (SURFACE K31) |
| ending | When Does It End? | (kept) | Ending | *never* is one of the answers, so not *End Date* |
| bar | Proposal Pass Threshold | Set the Proposal Pass Threshold | Proposal Pass Threshold | Ed's own words for the noun (entry 215); the imperative adds the ask |
| pace | Rising Approval Threshold? | Does the Threshold Rise Over Time? | Rising Threshold | today's title was a noun with a question mark, not a sentence |
| quorum | Quorum | Choose the Quorum | Quorum | Ed's example |
| authorship | Anonymous Proposals | Are Proposals Anonymous? | Anonymous Proposals | yes or no |
| judgments | When Are Votes Revealed? | (kept) | Vote Reveal | already a question |
| rate | Proposal Rate | Set the Proposal Rate | Proposal Rate | three numbers in one sentence, so *set* |
| chamber | Visibility | Who Can See the Document? | Visibility | a ladder of readers — the question names them |
| removal | How Is a Member Removed? | (kept) | Removals | already a question |
| lapse | Do Memberships Lapse? | (kept) | Lapsing | already a question |

Not in the table and unchanged: the power tabs (`pwTitle`, Q615) and the doors' power questions (entry 94) — T2 keeps them as questions in every state. Title Case throughout (T1). The applicant's five tasks (`APPCARDS`) are not settings and keep their one label each; their literals moved from the page into copy.js's `appcards` unchanged, because a member reads them.

**The `labelOf` seam.** One helper in setup.js beside `stateOf` — `labelOf(c, ctx)` — is the only thing that decides which label a card shows, and every title site that used to read `c.t` on a settings card reads through it: the tab's tooltip and screen-reader name (`chipHtml`), the rail entry's name and tooltip (`railEntry`), the card head's title where a card still has one (`cardHtml`), and the founder's own `ans-*` answer cards (which carry `n` too). The stranger's and the applicant's contexts inherit `stateOf` through their own `mustAct`/`waiting`, so a settled rule at the door reads `done` and wears the noun — the pile reads as rules to a stranger too — and a rule the room is still deciding wears the ask.

**A name in a sentence is not a title: `nounOf`.** The first card-audit after the switch read 🍾's readiness sentence as *🌍 Who Can See the Document? is waiting on 🪪 …* — `settingNamed` had been routed through `labelOf`, and a question embedded mid-sentence is not a sentence. Ed's ruling is about what the tab and the rail wear; a setting named inside a sentence or a readout line is a name, and a name is the noun in every state. So `nounOf(c)` (`c.n || c.t`, a door keeping its one label) sits beside `labelOf` and the six sentence sites take it: `settingNamed` (🍾's readiness holds, 👑's list and the *behind* line), the motion records' *Returns “…” to the founder's reserve* and its reserve-motion body, the amendment-news sentence (*The membership has changed quorum from…*), and 🍾's *· settled* / *· still being decided* lines. Two helpers, one rule each: a title follows the card's state, a name never does.

**One call beyond the plan's letter: `news` wears the noun.** The plan wrote the predicate as `done` alone. A settings card is in `news` when it is decided and owes the reader an OK (a constitutional rule set before they arrived, or a delegated question resolved); its rail entry then read *Choose the Quorum* over *decided; it waits for your OK* — an ask-shaped title on a card that offers no choice, which is exactly what Ed's ask-title is meant to make clear. So `labelOf` returns the noun in `done` and `news`, the ask in `ask`, `wait` and `yours`. `wait` keeps the ask deliberately: the choice is still being made, and the founder's tab over a delegated question reading *Choose the Quorum — waiting on others* is true. Ed can reverse the `news` half in one line if he would rather the rail's news read as asks.

**Where the rule is stated.** SURFACE §9's head (the rule, once), §6's setup alphabet (a pointer), §8's *asks · settled* column (both labels per row); STYLE T2 (the copy rule and the pair of examples); CLAUDE.md's gotcha and the `labelOf` glossary entry. **The guard**: `scripts/founding-walk.mjs` asserts 👥's rail entry reads *Choose the Quorum* while outstanding and its front tab's name reads *Quorum* once the founder has set it (skipped for the settled half under `--delegate=quorum`); the founding golden, the copy-source golden, the walk copy golden and the probes' reference were re-frozen in the same commit, which is the proof of the words.

## Three checkers over SURFACE's tables, and what their first run found (Q1239, Ed 2026-09-07; built 2026-09-08)

**The ruling, and the rule the build carried above every other.** Ed, 2026-09-07: *I want to check all three, but where they disagree with the code we should check which is right*; 2026-09-08: build all three now. So a disagreement between a table and the code is a numbered finding for Ed — the cell verbatim, the code line, a reading, recommendation first — and the checker lands red and stays red until he rules. **Nothing was bent to pass: no checker softened, no cell reworded, no line of product code changed.** The findings are QUESTIONS 1286 (a)–(e).

**What each reads.** `checkSetupAlphabet` (SURFACE §6, marker `setup-alphabet`): the state set and its test order against `stateOf`'s ternary and the intro sentence; the hue column against `HUE` through a five-word map; each branch of `markOf` against a cell and each cell against a branch (a done tab keeps the subject glyph, a grant wears its power's glyph, the fall-through `ask → glyph · wait → ⏳ · yours → ✏️ · else TICK`, and the wait-keeps-its-glyph guard read for the kind it names); *in the rail?* against `servedCards`'s three filters; *pins?* against `entryOf`'s `pinned:` literal and `mine`. `checkSockets` (§7.1, marker `sockets`): every class cell has a selector in `system.css`; every class the two socket renderers can set — `renderWallet`'s `className`, its `' full'`-style fragments, `classList.add/toggle`, and the `class="…"` of the markup written into the socket, plus `renderPowerWallets`'s, plus `showSay`'s `className` alone — has a row; `empty` is never struck (`.notheld::after` is the strike); every `.gone` rule is `visibility: hidden`; `.gonewallet` is `display: none`; and the `gone` row's class is what `renderWallet`'s `closedMode` branch sets. The bubble's own anatomy (`saysym`, `saytxt`, `in`) is deliberately outside the reverse pass: the row is the bubble, not its parts, where the socket's inner spans are rows in their own right. `checkLifecycle` (§2, marker `lifecycle`): rows L1–L9 exactly, each a key of `journey-walk.mjs`'s `LIFECYCLE` literal, each key printed by an `L('Ln')` line. The walk itself asserts each row's *Close* and *Persistence* on the live path: L1 every founder set's tab grey after the loop; L2 ✋ typed and Saved through its card, the row, and a reload; L3 the answer entry leaving the rail and the host's count where the page's `roomExists()`; L4 the deck's ✓ and ⏳ filing; L5 the ✏️ entry pinned; L6 the card closed on send and the clause's *checking their email*; L7 the change line on the acknowledged clause after the reload; L8 no grant served again after a reload and the sockets held; L9 🗑️ on ⏱️'s number and on ✋'s text.

**The first run's findings, by letter (QUESTIONS 1286 holds the cells and code in full).** **(a)** §6's `wait` row says a delegated card waiting on the room keeps its glyph and leaves the rail *ordinary or constitutional alike (Q517, Ed 2026-08-29)*; `markOf` keeps the glyph and `servedCards` drops the entry only where `c.kind === 'constitutional'`, and ⏱️ and 🤖 are ordinary and delegable. Two red lines, one per code site. **(b)** §7.1's `gone` row names `gonewallet` for the closed page; `renderWallet`'s `closedMode` branch sets `className = 'wallet'` and empties the socket, so ✏️'s socket is an emptied pill with `.navbar .wallet`'s ground while only the three power sockets take the class. **(c)** `renderWallet` draws `pwhen`, the countdown, and the table names it only inside two look cells. **(d)** the `full` row's class has no rule in any stylesheet — the *no countdown* look is the renderer omitting `.pwhen`. **(e)** `npm run journey`'s `L9 🗑️ · FAIL: ⏱️`: `REVERTKEYS()` carries `dripMin` and `rateBy` but not `dripN` and `dripUnit`, so 🗑️ restores the stored minutes and leaves the typed number on the card, where the commit path reads it first — the document untouched, the card wrong, a product defect filed rather than fixed.

**Two things the first run taught the walk, neither a finding.** The L6 line first asserted copy.js's *Check your inbox* against a clause that reads *The Founder is checking their email for a link* — the cell's own words, so the walk now asserts those. And every L3 line read *count null* under `--delegate-all`: the card draws *(n of E have answered so far)* only where `roomExists()`, and that mood is a room of one, so the count is asserted where the page says a room exists and said as *no count yet* otherwise — the page's precondition, read rather than assumed, and printed so Ed can overrule it. (a)'s reachable half — the ⏳ watcher on an ordinary delegated setting in a room of two or more — is reached by neither journey mood; every `ans-*` entry left the rail, ⏱️'s included, because `tasksFor` lists an answer task only while it is owed.

**The harness lesson, for whoever boots the next walk server by hand.** The deck step posts from Node with the page's cookie jar read for the walk's base; the server builds its magic links from `DRAFT_BASE_URL` (config.ts), defaulting to `localhost` — so a server booted without it mails a `localhost` link, the page lives there, and the jar read for `127.0.0.1` is empty: *deck · FAIL: could not raise the floor above the room · "log in first"*, and a pre-existing TypeError at the ledger step behind it. CI exports the variable before booting; the hand-booted server must too. Not a product finding.

**Where things stand at the commit.** `spec-check` red on five lines, `journey` red on one; `test`, `lint`, `typecheck`, `build`, `copy-check` and `probe --strict` (IDENTICAL, 0 diffs) green. A push would redden CI's `ci` and `walks` jobs until Ed rules on 1286.

**The ruling** (QUESTIONS 1237, verbatim): *Answered by Ed, 2026-09-07, (b), once the four were described to him. F5 (~1,700 characters) is 🍾's visibility rule followed by a description of the six-block power table that §9's 🍾 row also gives; K31 (~3,500) is 📝's two modes followed by the edit-mode geometry that §9's 📝 row states in outline; F21 (~2,700) is Membership's five statuses in prose that §8's band table has columns for; F19 (~1,600) is 🍾's readout vocabulary, long because it is complete.
