**Seen and not built:** 1294 (the column renders no markdown at all; a toggle alone toggles nothing), 1305 (the drawing is a hard-edged width fill; the suspect is closeness clamping to 1 at the bar's span, to be measured on a local room), 1306–1308, and 1309 — the dev host restarted at 11:47 and took Ed's room with it, which explains his three *no such document* reports and the unspent ✏️.

## Q1310: bots on docs.vote (Ed, 2026-09-10)

**The ruling, verbatim.** From Ed's answer to 1309 (the dev host had restarted under his first bot room and taken it with it): *we can have bot users in prod — we're still in alpha*. And on the door, against a proposal to catch a `.bot@` local part on the host: *why don't we catch all emails to \*@bots.docs.vote instead, since they could never be confused for a real email address* — confirmed, when asked, as the **server-side** catch (Reading 1) over a real mailbox at that subdomain.

**Why it was needed.** `room-bots` (2026-09-06) seated a bot by reading `GET /api/dev/outbox` for invitations to `*.bot@` addresses and following the links. Production has no such route — decision 437 deleted it from the artifact rather than flag-gating it — the Resend key is set there, and a link cannot be forged outside the host (a random token, stored hashed, one use). So a bot invited on docs.vote was a bounce to a domain that has never bounced, and the only host a bot room could run on was the one that loses every document at the next idle sleep (1309).

**What was built** (branch `bots-1310`, worktree `draft-wt-bots`, 2026-09-10):

- **The mailer catches bot mail** (`packages/server/src/mailer.ts`). `isBotAddress` is the rule: the part after the last `@`, lower-cased, equals `bots.docs.vote` exactly — `x@bots.docs.vote.evil.com` and `x@notbots.docs.vote` are strangers. In the Resend branch a bot's mail is filed in the **bot outbox** (`bots-outbox.jsonl` in the data dir, the dev outbox's row shape: `at`, `to`, `subject`, `text`, `link`) and returns before the provider is reached, so it is neither sent nor a bounce; the durable outbox marks the row delivered. In the dev branch it lands in the dev outbox as before **and** in the bot outbox, so `room-bots` works against a dev server with or without a key, and 📬 and the walks see what they always saw. The reserved-TLD refusal (`deliverable`, Q680) is untouched and is a different thing: it refuses, this redirects. `outboxTail` is the one reader behind both routes.
- **A keyed route that ships** (`packages/server/src/server.ts`). `GET /api/bots/outbox` serves the tail, newest first, to the bearer of `DRAFT_BOT_KEY` (`config.ts`, `botKey`; an empty variable is unset). Unset, it answers 404 with an unknown path's body, so a host without the key exposes nothing. `bearerOk` parses `Authorization: Bearer <key>` and compares with `timingSafeEqual` after a length check, the cookie check's own discipline; a wrong or missing key is 401 with `{ error: 'unauthorized' }` and nothing else, and wrong keys alone are rate-limited per IP (`tooMany('bots')`), since the legitimate reader polls every three seconds and the window is ten minutes at twenty. It sits deliberately **outside** the `DEV:` label, beside the dev route it mirrors; `scripts/build-server.mjs`'s `NEVER_IN_PROD` names `/api/dev/` and is not tripped, and the built artifact carries the route (grepped after the build). `verify-deploy` gains *the bot outbox is closed to a stranger (Q1310)*: a bare request and a wrong bearer must each answer 401 or 404, never 200.
- **`room-bots` reads it** (`scripts/room-bots.mjs`). A bot is any address at `bots.docs.vote`; `nameOf` maps `ada.lovelace@bots.docs.vote` to *Ada Lovelace*; the `.bot@` convention is gone from the header, the help and the arrival line. `--key=<key>` (the `=` form so a key never splits on a shell; the space form still works) or `DRAFT_BOT_KEY` in the environment selects `GET /api/bots/outbox` with the bearer header, else `GET /api/dev/outbox` as before; the refusal at start names both routes and, with a key, says whether it was refused (401) or the host has none (404). Everything else — temperaments, opinions, shapes, the relogin on a spent link, the tally — is as it was.
- **Docs and config.** `render.yaml` declares `DRAFT_BOT_KEY` (`sync: false`) on both services. `docs/OPERATING.md` §2 gains the variable's row, §9's store row states that idle sleep on the free plan is a restart (Ed accepted it: dev rooms are disposable), and a new **§10 Bots on docs.vote** gives the subdomain rule, the key, the command, what a leaked key allows and how it is rotated. `PRODUCTION.md`'s security list gains a Q1310 table for the keyed door. `README.md`'s walks row says `room-bots` alone also runs against docs.vote. CLAUDE.md: `room-bots` and `dev-outbox` amended, `bot-outbox` added under `server`, `mail-fold` points at it.
- **Tests** (`packages/server/test/bots.test.ts`, five): with a Resend key configured, mail to `ada@bots.docs.vote` never reaches the provider (a fetch wrapper counts anything aimed at `api.resend.com` while passing the test's own traffic through) and lands in the bot outbox with its link, a real address still going to the provider; the domain rule exact on eight addresses; the route 404 without a key whatever is sent, 401 without detail on a missing, wrong, longer, shorter or schemeless key, 200 with the right one — then a document founded by `founder@bots.docs.vote` over the production mailer, its creation link read out of the route and followed, an invitation to a bot riding the durable outbox into the same file and seating the bot, the outbox counting nothing failed; and in dev mode a bot's mail in both outboxes, a member's in the dev one alone, two files and not one read twice.

**The live proof.** A server from the worktree on 8317 with `RESEND_API_KEY=dummy DRAFT_BOT_KEY=testkey`: the route answered 401 bare and 401 wrong; a document founded by `founder@bots.docs.vote` had its creation mail in the bot outbox (`[mail→bot outbox→founder@bots.docs.vote] Create “Bot Room …”` in the server log); the one call that did reach Resend was the operator's own birth notification to the compiled-in `notifyEmail` — not a bot's, and the right behaviour — refused by the dummy key and dropped as *fired and forgotten* says; three bots invited through `invite`, all four mails filed; `node scripts/room-bots.mjs <url> --key=testkey --min=1s --max=2s` seated all three on its first poll, and the founder too — its creation link being spent, it asked for a login and the login mail arrived through the same file, which is the relogin path proved on the production branch — and in one minute the room ran 73 judgments, 53 proposals, 3 motions, 3 withdrawals and 32 adoptions with one ordinary refusal and no other.

**Decisions taken in the build, for Ed to reverse if he likes.** (a) The header form is `Authorization: Bearer <key>`, the shape Resend itself uses and the one `fetch` sends without ceremony; a query-string key was rejected because it lands in request logs. (b) The file is `bots-outbox.jsonl`, beside `outbox.jsonl`, the same shape, ephemeral like it. (c) The dev branch files a bot's mail in **both** outboxes rather than only the bot one, so nothing that reads the dev outbox today — 📬, `journey`, `room-walk`'s link reader — changes behaviour. (d) The limiter counts wrong keys only; a right key is never throttled. (e) OPERATING's new material is a top-level §10 rather than a subsection of §9, since it is about production and §9 is the dev host. (f) `botKey` is optional on `ServerConfig` so the five test boots that build a config literal keep compiling.

**Rejected doors.** *Minting links by hand on the host* — a shell trip into the Render service per re-login, which is what a spent one-use link costs every time a runner restarts. *A real catch-all mailbox over IMAP* at `bots.docs.vote` — a mailbox to run, a client to write, a credential to keep, and a delay on every invitation, for mail nobody reads.
## Q1294, Q1304 (lane half), Q1307: the column renders markdown (Ed, 2026-09-10, (a))

**The ruling** (Ed, 2026-09-10 12:36, Q1294 (a), carrying Q1304's lane half and Q1307). The charter column rendered no markdown at all: `renderDoc` printed every clause through `esc`, so `**bold**` showed its asterisks and a `- ` line its dash, and headings worked only because the engine keyed a `# ` line as a heading block. The editing lane already rendered inline marks (`mdToHtml`, since Ed's 2026-08-17 ruling that a candidate's text *is* markdown), and K22 said *inline only*. Ed ruled six things: the reading column renders the inline marks in every clause, post-🍾 and on the closed page alike, and a `- ` line is a **bullet block** beside the `# ` heading block — a kind decided per line, never a list object spanning lines; a typed `# ` or `- ` in a lane previews as it will land and the marker survives serialisation, so what is proposed is the source; the `[]` toggle moves to the foot row and flips the **whole column** in edit mode, B and I staying on the lane, no toggle outside edit mode; `linkify` runs after the marks render, over text nodes only, never inside a code span; the pre-🍾 column treats `- ` as it treats `# `; K22 amended and §9's 📝 row says where the toggle sits.

**What was built** (7039edc). One reading of a line's marker, `mdBlock` in cards.js, shared by the page's `blocksOf`, `relabel` and `textDivs` and by the lane's preview, so a line that is a heading in one place is a heading in every place. `mdLine` — `mdToHtml` then `linkifyHtml`, which walks the rendered string's tag/text segments and links only outside a `<code>` depth — is the one rendering of a clause for reading, used by session.js's `blockHtml` at the heading, both paragraph branches and the editing card's head, and by `clauseHeadHtml` for every card's head. A bullet line is `{ t: 'p', bullet: true, x }` with the dash off the text, exactly as a heading holds `x` without its hashes; `originOf` carries `bullet` as it carries `level`, and `headOf` puts `- ` back on a hunk as it puts the hashes back. `laneBlocks` takes kinds rather than head flags and reads the block's own text first: a typed marker outranks the origin (a paragraph retyped as a heading *is* one now), the marker's characters come off the front of the diff pieces into a dimmed `.mdmark` span, still text. The `[]` button is drawn by `proposalRowHtml` when its host hands the mode in, and a mousedown on it flips `laneMode`, rebuilds the column with `renderAll`, and puts the focused lane's caret back converted through `richToSource`/`sourceToRich`. In source mode `PROSE()` wears `mdsrc`, every block prints `esc(line.x)` behind its marker in a `.nocaret` span — so `leadLen` subtracts it and `startDraftFromTyping`'s offsets stay offsets into `line.x` — and the column takes the lane's monospace. CSS: one `.bullet` rule for `p.bullet`, the pre-🍾 `div.bullet` and `.lp.bullet`, the dot an inline-block `::before` (never content: nothing counts it, no caret lands in it), consecutive bullets tightened by `:has(+ .bullet)` alone.

**The decisions each part took.**
- *Where the marker lives in a lane.* Two conventions met: a heading **origin** has always shown in the lane without its `# ` (the class from the origin, `headOf` re-adding the marker on the hunk), while Ed's ruling wants a **typed** marker kept as text. Kept both rather than unifying on marker-in-text, because unifying would change `currentTextFor` and every caret offset measured against the column's `h2`, which prints no marker. So an origin-heading block shows without its marker and a typed one shows its marker dimmed; `hunksOf` is unchanged, and a typed `# ` inside a heading origin's lane would double the hashes — a pre-existing edge, unchanged.
- *What source mode shows for a heading.* The `h2` stays an `h2` (the fold triangle, the TOC and `id="sec-n"` hang on it); the marker is put back in front as a `.nocaret` span and the font goes monospace. A truer source view would flatten the heading to a plain mono line; the fold controls would then have nowhere to sit, so the structure stays and only the text changes.
- *The toggle's place on the row.* Beside 🗑️ at the left, not beside the commit: a view switch next to ✏️ reads as a second commit, and §9.1's grammar puts the act at the right and the bin at the left; a cold control belongs with the bin's side.
- *No toggle on the pre-🍾 row.* The founder's column is already the characters (`relabel` strips only the block markers into classes); a rendered/source switch there would need inline rendering inside a contenteditable that harvests its own text, a different machine. The page passes no `mode`, so the row draws none. Ed may want it there later.
- *The fixture.* The larder clause became a bullet run of three with an `*italic*` in one and a `**bold**` in the clause after, so the probes and the card-copy golden carry the rendering; the 792 pre-freeze session-probe diffs were the three new lines shifting every later index key and every rect by 68px.

**Rejected**, each named in `cards.js`'s comment so the next reader does not re-propose it: nested lists (a depth is a relation between lines, and one block is one line), numbered lists (a number is a count over lines — the engine would have to renumber across hunks), tables (a row is several cells and the header another row), block quotes (a run), and link syntax (a docs.vote address is already a link by `linkify`; any other target is a door out of the document). Each either spans lines or needs a mapping layer between the page and the footprint, which is the one thing `blocksOf` exists to avoid.

**Verified** headless against the design server and the frozen reference: the marks and bullets render in the column, on a card's head and on the closed page; the lane previews both markers and round-trips them through `readLane`/`htmlToMd`; the toggle flips the column and every lane both ways with the caret kept; the pre-🍾 column makes `div.bullet` beside `div.docline.lvlN`; `mdLine` links an address in prose and leaves one in a code span; no page errors. Playwright's synthetic Enter in a contenteditable neither splits a lane block nor makes the first founding line a div, identically on the reference page — the harness, not the build. Guards: lint, spec-check, copy-check, both probes (re-frozen), journey on a fresh server, all green.


## Q1305 and Q1308: the wash and the strange card, measured on a local bot room (2026-09-10)

**Q1305 — the wash never filled.** Ed: *the wash saturation rises but there is no left-to-right fill*. The drawing was sound (a bar whose width is `--fill`, its colour urgency); the number was the trouble. Measured straight from the engine: the author's derived preference (§3.3) alone fits a leader probability near 0.80 on a newborn race, and closeness read |2p − 1| against the bar's span, so at a bar of 60 the meter read 100% before anybody had judged, 99% at 80, 74% at 90 — full at birth, dipping only when the room split, and a room voting against reading full too, as a magnitude should. Three readings put to Ed: the lesser of the race's two distances to resolution — the bar's and the floor's (distinct movers over F, §4.2) — recommended and chosen, with his amendment: *min of bar and floor distance, but don't need to say anywhere which of the two a race is waiting on*; dropping the derived preference from the closeness fit (0 until a second voice, then a jump); leaving the engine and drawing measured comparisons over the floor (a count, the bar's distance gone). Built as R-101, SPEC v0.115: a newborn race reads 1/F, each new judge is a step whichever way they vote, a repeat judge none. The measurement script was a throwaway vitest file, deleted.

**Q1308 — the strange card.** Reproduced on a local room of twelve bots at bar 90 (`room-bots --heat 1`, founded over the API with an AI-usage charter). Three things, two of them defects. (i) A race whose contested span covers two blocks — a bot's *merge* shape, or any patch across neighbours — headed its card with the first block alone (`currentTextFor(keys[0])`) while every candidate ran on into the second: Ed's screenshot exactly. The head reads the whole run now (`runTextFor`, `headOpts`, every clause-headed card), and so does the diff base a candidate is marked against. (ii) A race that inserts a line between two clauses — a bot's *insert* shape — has an empty contested span, and `keysOfSpan` keyed it to the line at `start`, the clause after the gap, so its card read *The clause as it stands* over a neighbour with an unrelated sentence proposed: a replacement, to any reader. `siteOfSpan` gives such a race the draft's own shape (Q261): the gap key, the block before as `insertAfterKey` (the read side's held-open `insert-anchor`), and the insert head; a crown question and a park on an inserted line take the same site; the column draws one anchor per item in a gap rather than `find`'s first. The insert head's sentence was one fixture string — *the charter runs straight from Bringing a Guest to Guests Staying Over* — that would have printed the fixture's headings on any live document; it names the neighbours in their own first words now (copy.js `head.nothing` and its three edges), and a live insertion, bringing no heading, draws none. (iii) The second pair under *Your vote on this clause* is Q1201's ledger beneath a live pair, by design. SURFACE M19 states (i) and (ii).

**Merged the same afternoon:** the markdown column (Q1294, md-1294, 7039edc) and the bot door (Q1310, bots-1310, e4303f3), each built by a subagent in a hand-made sibling worktree while the main tree took Q1305 and Q1308; the one real conflict was cards.js's head, which takes both — the gap sentence handed in, and `mdLine` over the clause text.

## Q1306: 🗑️ per site on a patch (Ed, 2026-09-10, (a))

**The report** (Ed's first bot room on dev.docs.vote, 2026-09-10): *When I am in edit mode and am making a patch (edit in two places), the 🗑️ for the edit in one place should only discard that edit, not the whole patch.* Until this every 🗑️ on the surface meant the same thing — the proposal-row's at the foot of the window (`row-discard`, *Discard the whole draft*) and the 🗑️ on each editing card (`draft-cancel`, *Discard this draft*) both called `dropDraft()`, so a patch of two places lost both to a press on either.

**The ruling, (a)** (Ed, 2026-09-10 12:48): an editing card's 🗑️ discards its own site of the draft; the proposal row's 🗑️ keeps meaning discard all; a patch with one site left is a plain candidate; with none left the draft goes. The alternatives were the status quo with a re-worded tooltip, and making the row's 🗑️ per-site too — neither survives the report: the row stands for the whole draft (K18, one row that does not move) and is the one bin a member can reach without finding a card.

**What was built.** `dropDraftSite(site)` beside `dropDraft()` in session.js: takes one site out of `d.sites`, re-syncs `d.keys`, re-derives the gap bookkeeping the draft carries at draft level — `gapKey` and `insertAfterKey` are set by `startDraft` on the draft, not the site, so after a discard they are read back off whatever gap site remains, or deleted — and moves `focusKey` off the site that has gone; with nothing left it hands over to `dropDraft()`. The click dispatcher hands `act` the card's own `data-site`, and `draft-cancel` on a draft of more than one site collapses that one card (`collapseCard`, the singular cards.js already exported for a patch's set) and drops that one site, leaving `openId` on the draft so the other cards stay open; on a one-site draft, and from the ⚔️ desk holding no site, the press is exactly what it was. The column needs no change: a discarded site's blocks are simply no longer swallowed, so the next render prints the paragraph, held still on that key as the whole-draft discard always was. The row derives *n places changed* and its commit from `sites.length`, so a patch at one site reads as a plain candidate without anything being told.

**Copy.** `T.row.discardThis` — *Discard this change — nothing has been spent on it* — on the editing card's 🗑️ and the ⚔️ desk's, matching `discardAll`'s register; `discardDraft` (*Discard this draft — nothing has been spent on it yet*) is retired, its only two users being those. The *yet* went with it: nothing is spent on a change before Propose, and the row's sentence never said it.

**Guards.** `npm run journey`'s new *site bin* step, after *typing*: a second site makes the draft a patch — two cards — and the **second** card's 🗑️ is pressed, asserting one site left with the first site's key and text intact, its own place back (a clause's words as they were, read with the gutter stripped; a gap closed with its anchor and `gapKey` gone), one editing card, `openId` still the draft's, edit mode still on, the row still there, and the tooltip. Where the second site goes is the document's to say: a clause two blocks clear of the first site where there is one — a neighbour would join the run instead (K15) — and otherwise a **gap** after the last clause outside the draft, a gap never joining a run (Q261); the walk's own document is two adjacent clauses, so its default branch takes the gap `G2` after `L1` beside the `X` in `L0`, and `--new-clause`, whose first site is that gap, takes `L0`. The first shape of the step demanded the clearance alone and was red on both branches for that reason. The second site rather than the first so that what the walk goes on to propose is the site it typed first in both branches; under `--empty-text` the step stands down, an empty document having one clause. Headless on the fixture (`scripts/_bin.tmp.mjs`, deleted): two clause sites → A's 🗑️ → one site, A's paragraph back, B's lane keeps its typing; then the row's 🗑️ → no draft; a gap site beside a clause site discarded alone → `gapKey` and `insertAfterKey` gone and no `insert-anchor`; the clause site discarded with the gap staying → the anchor and both keys kept; a one-site draft's card 🗑️ → the draft gone and `openId` null. No page errors in any of them.

## Q1311: every gap site carries its own anchor (Ed, 2026-09-10)

**The ruling** (Ed, 2026-09-10 16:04: *fix it now*, on the hole Q1306's build recorded as its decision (iii)): a patch holding two gap sites — a new clause after clause 2 and another after clause 6 — draws two held-open anchors and two editing cards, one per gap. The gap bookkeeping moves onto the site; nothing else changes.

**The shape it was.** `startDraft` wrote `gapKey` and `insertAfterKey` — the gap's key and the block it follows, which the read side uses to place the held-open `insert-anchor` — onto the **draft**, one pair per draft, so the second gap overwrote the first's and the column's anchor loop (`SUGGS.filter((g) => g.insertAfterKey === line.key)`) drew one anchor for whichever wrote last, with the other gap's card nowhere; `dropDraftSite` (Q1306) re-derived the pair from whichever gap site survived a discard. A rail entry on a draft's gap found *the* anchor by the draft's id alone, and the sections a draft stood in counted one gap's neighbour.

**The shape now.** A gap site is born with its own pair (`gapFields` in `addDraftSite`, session.js), `startDraft` writes nothing at draft level, `dropDraftSite` drops the site and re-derives nothing, and a hydrated draft whose gap site lacks the pair is given it (`setData`). The column lists **holders** once per render — `gapHolders`: one per gap site of anything with `sites`, one per live item carrying the pair on itself — and draws each on its own anchor; a draft's anchors carry `data-site`, so `anchorForEntry` finds a draft's gap anchor by the site's key and a live item's by id as before; a draft draws a card on every one of its anchors, a live item once (`cardDone`); `suggestionSections` reads every site's neighbour; `headOpts` reads the gap off its holder (`gapOf`). `hunksOf` (session-view.html) already built the insertion hunk from the site's own key and needed no change. **The live items are untouched**: `itemsFromView`'s races, crowns and parks (`siteOfSpan`) have no `sites` and carry the pair on themselves, which is exactly the second branch of `gapHolders`, and the fixture's `insert-quiet` — `insertAfterKey` with no `gapKey` — goes the same way; their anchors carry no `data-site`, so the session probe's markup is byte-identical.

**Rejected.** Mirroring the first gap site's pair onto the draft, which would have kept every live-item reader working with no change: it keeps the one-anchor path alive on a draft, so the second gap still needs its own path, and a discard has to re-derive the mirror — two truths where the site can be the one. A per-draft list of gaps (`d.gaps`) kept in step with `d.sites`: the same two truths, one array over.

**Taken alone.** (i) The anchor emission is one helper, `gapsAfter(key)`, called at every way out of the column loop — the heading branch's three exits and the writing branch's `continue` included. Before this a gap after a heading, or after a clause the draft had swallowed, fell through the `continue` above the old loop and drew nothing (a live race on such a gap had nowhere to stand either, against M19); the walk's default shape — a draft on `L0`, a gap `G1` after it — lands exactly there, so the hole had to close for the step to exist. (ii) Noticed and left, being the row's and not the gap's: the proposal-row's middle (*n places changed*) and its commit's greyness are computed at render, and typing into a lane re-marks the lane without re-rendering the row — so a gap site, which opens empty, reads *0 places* and a greyed commit until something else renders. Q1089's count is right at every render; it is the refresh that is missing. (iii) Noticed and left, fixture-only: `blockBeforeGap` compares `keyNum`, and the session fixture's named keys (`guests`, `sanctions`) read −1, so on the fixture every gap's `insertAfterKey` is the last named block; the live host keys every line `L<n>` and is unaffected.

**Guards.** `npm run journey`'s *two gaps* · *gap bin* · *gaps back* steps after *site bin*, on both shapes: gaps are added at the edges of clauses outside the draft until it holds two (default: `G1` after the swallowed `L0`, `G2` after `L1`; `--new-clause`, already holding `G2`: `G0` at the head and `G1`), asserting two gap sites each with its own `insertAfterKey`, nothing on the draft, two anchors keyed by site, a card per site with its typing, a rail entry per site none hidden; then the first-added gap's 🗑️, asserting the other gap's anchor, card and text stand; then the rest binned, asserting the draft is its first site again. The *site bin* step reads the sites' gap keys instead of the draft's. Headless on the fixture (`scripts/_gaps.tmp.mjs`, deleted): two gaps → 🗑️ on the first → the second stands with its text; the reverse order; a gap after a swallowed clause and after a heading each anchored; the fixture's `insert-quiet` one anchor without `data-site`; no page errors.

**Decisions taken here, for Ed to reverse if he wants.** (i) The ⚔️ desk's 🗑️ takes the same rule and the same tooltip — it holds a site of the same draft, and a desk draft beside an editing-card site is a patch like any other. (ii) After a site discard no caret is placed: the remaining card keeps its lane but focus is where the render leaves it, as it is after the whole-draft discard; putting the caret into the first remaining lane would be one line (`land`) if wanted. (iii) `d.gapKey`/`insertAfterKey` stay one-per-draft, as `startDraft` left them: a draft holding two gap sites draws one anchor today and did before this; the discard re-derives from the first remaining gap. (iv) SURFACE row 431's commit column and K31's *the only bin* sentence were amended beside K17–K18, since both stated the old rule. (v) Noticed and left: the row's 🗑️ handler drops the draft without clearing `openId`, so the page's open id names a card that no longer exists until the next open; every render tolerates it and it predates this — a question rather than a fix.

## The subagents' five calls, put to Ed one at a time (2026-09-10, 15:12–16:05)

Five decisions the two afternoon builds (Q1294's markdown column, Q1306's 🗑️ per site) and the bot door (Q1310) made without him, each asked as one multiple-choice question with the background in the body, recommended option first.

1. **Where the `[]` source toggle sits.** Built at the left of the proposal row beside 🗑️. Offered: as built · the centre of the row · the right beside ✏️ · the riding strip with 📝. Ed: *top right of the edit box, identical to the existing composer control. You can put bold and italic there too.* Read as one control strip — **B**, *I*, `[]` — at the top right of the lifted column in edit mode, the per-lane B/I retired; built as Q1294 (b) on branch `lane-controls-1294`, its own section below.
2. **How the bot key travels.** Built as an `Authorization: Bearer` header, constant-time compared, wrong keys rate-limited, the route absent with no key set. Offered: as built · `?key=` in the query string (openable in a tab, but written into every access log and pasted link) · a custom header (the same secrecy, one more name). Ed: **Bearer header** — stands.
3. **The ⚔️ desk's 🗑️.** Built to take Q1306's per-site rule and tooltip, so a bridge being written at another site survives the desk's bin. Offered: as built · the desk discards the whole draft (two cards, one glyph, two meanings). Ed: **same rule as any card** — stands.
4. **The caret after a site discard.** Built with no caret placed: the page does not move, the paragraph that came back is under the pointer, one click before typing resumes. Offered: as built · the caret into the surviving site (a scroll if it is off screen) · only when that site is on screen (two behaviours for one press). Ed: **no caret, stay put** — stands.
5. **Two gap sites in one patch draw one anchor.** Built as found: the gap bookkeeping on the draft, `dropDraftSite` re-deriving the one anchor. Offered: fix now · file as a question · leave unrecorded. Ed: **fix it now** — Q1311, branch `gap-sites-1311`, its own section below.

## Q1312: rival wordings a member never sees (Ed, 2026-09-10 — closed, *keep the deal, say nothing*)

Ed, on his second look at the bot room: *one thing I noticed when I was testing in the bot room is that I didn't see any races at all*; asked which of three readings matched, he chose *only one-candidate cards* — he voted on the bots' proposals, and every card was one wording against the clause, never two rival wordings on one clause.

**Reproduced, and not a defect.** A fresh twelve-bot room on a keyed cooldown-0 server (`found-races.mjs`, a bot founder, eight clauses, bar 60, the bots at a three-to-twelve-second cadence, default heat 0.6): within a minute the founder's view held rival races — over fifteen minutes 51 of the bots' 64 proposals aimed at contested clauses, the biggest race held 7 wordings, 5 races held rivals at once, nothing refused. The engine forms rivals as designed. What a member is dealt is SPEC §8.3's hand as R-062 shaped it: while a race's rival gate is shut, `bestPairFor` serves incumbent pairs first — each challenger against the clause — and a rival pair only once the member's incumbent pairs on that race are spent, or once one challenger has `rivalGateMinComparisons` non-derived comparisons against the incumbent and beats it at `rivalGateProb`. A challenger-against-clause judgment is the displacement evidence adoption needs; a rival-against-rival one does not move the bar. In a lively room wordings keep arriving, so a person meets a one-wording card at every press and sees two side by side only in the sealed record; the quick card does not say that other wordings are racing on its clause.

**Offered and declined**, recommended first: keep the deal and say so on the card (one line, *one of 4 wordings racing here*, a count on the view); keep the deal and say nothing; deal rival pairs sooner (a §8.3 amendment, judgments spent where they do not move the bar); list the whole field on the card (a new card shape, the record's reveal moved into the race's lifetime). Ed: **keep the deal, say nothing.** SPEC §8.3, R-062 and the quick card stand unchanged.

## Q1294 (b): the lane controls move to the column (Ed, 2026-09-10)

**The question.** Q1294 (a), built that morning, put the one `[]` source toggle — which flips the whole column, every clause and every open lane, between rendered and source in edit mode — on the proposal-row at the foot of the window, beside 🗑️, while **B** and *I* stayed at the top right of each editing card's lane, acting on that lane's selection. Ed was asked where `[]` should sit.

**The ruling** (Ed, 2026-09-10 16:00, verbatim): *"top right of the edit box, identical to the existing composer control. You can put bold and italic there too."*

**The reading.** *The edit box* is the lifted column of SURFACE K31 — the whole prose column raised onto a card when 📝 is pressed — and *the existing composer control* is the per-lane B · *I* strip and its treatment. So the column gets **one** control strip at its top right, B · *I* · `[]`, drawn with the classes, sizes and tooltips the lane's B and *I* had, `[]` carrying its pressed state while the column shows source; the per-lane controls go, so a patch of three sites has one strip, not three; `[]` leaves the row. Nothing in the code cast doubt on the reading: the lane's controls were already bound to a single column-wide state (`laneRaw`) and the row's `[]` already found the focused lane at the press, so the strip is the two joined at the place Ed named.

**What moved.** `laneCtlHtml` in cards.js's pure layer draws the strip — the grammar owns the three tooltips, `G.fmt.bold` / `italic` / `mdMode`, unchanged — and `laneBoxHtml` no longer draws a `.lanectl` of its own; the lane is the whole box, its air made symmetric (`--s3` top and bottom, where the control row's 4 + 22 px had stood above 8). session.js's `renderDoc` draws the strip exactly where it draws the proposal-row — edit mode, a reader who may propose, the document open — as `.editctl`, a zero-height sticky box before the column's `.prose`, outside the contenteditable (a button inside one is harvested text, the `sectoggle` lesson). `proposalRowHtml` drops its `mode` and the row is 🗑️, the count and the commit again. The `[]` handler is the same code on the strip: a prevented mousedown, the focused lane's caret read out and put back converted (`richToSource` / `sourceToRich`), one `renderAll`. B and *I* find the lane at the press — `document.activeElement`'s `[data-lane]`, which the prevented mousedown leaves focused — do what they always did (execCommand in rich mode, the selection wrapped in the characters in source mode) and call that lane's own re-mark through a `laneRemark` WeakMap the lane loop fills. system.css: `.editctl` and `.editctl .lanectl` placed, `.lanebox .lanectl` and `.proposalrow .lmode` gone, `.lfmt:disabled` added.

**Rejected.**
- *Left, beside 🗑️* — where (a) had put it, on §9.1's argument that a cold control belongs on the bin's side. It put the view switch a viewport away from the text it switches and apart from B and *I*, which act on the same text; and Ed did not choose it.
- *Centre of the row* — the middle is the count's (*2 places changed*), and the row is click-transparent there by design (Ed's QA, 2026-08-30): a button in the middle would need a ground the row is not allowed to have.
- *Right, beside ✏️* — a view switch next to the commit reads as a second commit; §9.1 puts the act at the right and nothing else.
- *The riding strip* — 📝's pile with the ✒️ 🛡️ tabs beneath it. Every object in a tab column is a door into a card; a mode button among them would be the one thing there that is not a tab, and B and *I* could not have joined it.

**Decisions taken here, not put to Ed.**
- *The strip rides.* Ed said *top right of the edit box*; the box in edit mode runs off the foot of the page, so a strip fixed at its top corner is out of reach after one screen of scrolling. It is sticky at the card's top edge exactly as the row is sticky at its foot and the 📝 tab at the left — *the viewport is the card* — resting inside the card's 24px top padding (1px in, centring a 22px strip) and, when it has left its rest, taking a ground and the tab's `--shadow-md` (`detached`, set by `syncEditCtl` on each scroll frame) since it is then over the prose rather than beside it. The sticky box's own top *is* the card's top edge — the column's negative top margin, the one that pays for the card's padding, collapses through an empty block — so the strip needs no lift and no measurement, unlike the tab, which sits after the band and measures its own line. The first cut lifted it by the card's padding and measured 23px *above* the card, the collapse having already paid that distance; the fix is 1px in and the sticky `top` 1px under the tab's, measured at the card's top + 1 at rest and level with the tab riding.
- *B and I disabled while no lane holds the caret.* The per-lane pair was never disabled (there was always a lane to act on); the column's pair has no lane until a draft exists, and a press then would have nothing to bold. Disabled rather than acting on the last lane touched, because a control that acts somewhere you are not looking is the phantom-power shape. `syncEditCtl` reads `document.activeElement` on every focus change (focusout a tick late, since it fires before the new focus lands), scroll frame and render. `[]` is never disabled — it needs no lane.
- *`data-act="col-mode"`*, not `row-mode` kept: no walk or tool pressed the old name (grepped `scripts/`, `design/tools/`, the tests), and a name that says *row* on a control that left the row is the kind of lie the glossary exists to prevent.
- *Order B · I · `[]`*, the two acts first and the view switch last, as the parent session specified.
- *No strip before 🍾.* The row's `[]` never reached the founder's pre-🍾 column (the page passed no `mode`: the column is the characters already, and there are no lanes), so the strip does not either; the founder's column has neither B nor *I*, as before.
- *The ⚔️ desk's blank lane* drew B and *I* too, but their handlers were bound only inside the `[data-lane]` loop, so on the desk they were dead buttons; they go with the rest, and the desk's lane gains real ones the moment typing opens a draft in edit mode.

**Guards and verification** are in the commit message: lint, spec-check, copy-check (no string moved — the three tooltips keep their keys), the session probe's diffs read one by one before the re-freeze, journey on both shapes against a fresh cooldown-0 server, and a headless walk of the fixture measuring the strip's rest against the card's corner.

**Decisions taken here, for Ed to reverse if he wants.** (i) The ⚔️ desk's 🗑️ takes the same rule and the same tooltip — it holds a site of the same draft, and a desk draft beside an editing-card site is a patch like any other. (ii) After a site discard no caret is placed: the remaining card keeps its lane but focus is where the render leaves it, as it is after the whole-draft discard; putting the caret into the first remaining lane would be one line (`land`) if wanted. (iii) `d.gapKey`/`insertAfterKey` stay one-per-draft, as `startDraft` left them: a draft holding two gap sites draws one anchor today and did before this; the discard re-derives from the first remaining gap. (iv) SURFACE row 431's commit column and K31's *the only bin* sentence were amended beside K17–K18, since both stated the old rule. (v) Noticed and left: the row's 🗑️ handler drops the draft without clearing `openId`, so the page's open id names a card that no longer exists until the next open; every render tolerates it and it predates this — a question rather than a fix.

## Q1319: a motion in flight fills its rail entry (Ed, 2026-09-11)

**Ed's words** (2026-09-11 14:22, his bot room on docs.vote, document 1): *Constitutional setting proposals don't seem to have the wash progress bar.*

**The cause.** A rail entry's `--fill` (`railEntry`, setup.js) is *100% for anything only yours to decide, how far the room has got on anything that is theirs* — `c.in / E` where `ctx.isRoom(c)`. `isRoom` in session-view.html is `delegated(c.key)`: true for a **delegated question** and nothing else. A 🏛️ motion in flight on a settled setting is the room's too — the assembly route of SPEC §9.6a, every member answering — but the setting under it is founder-held or already resolved, so `isRoom` read false, the entry took the founder's `100%` from the moment the motion was put, and its tooltip was the setting's label rather than a count. The wash was full and never moved, which is what Ed saw. `resolveCounts` had never read the motion at all: it wrote `c.in` from the setting's own question (`answeredCount`, or `E` once resolved by ceremony), and on a founder-set setting that is 0 — the live `settingState` adapter reports `answeredCount: 0` where no question ever ran — so the count under the bar was as wrong as the bar.

**The fix.** Two edits, one seam. `resolveCounts` (session-view.html) now also writes `c.motionIn` on every setting: the answers a 🏛️ motion in flight on it holds (`liveMotionRec(c)`, `rec.answers.size` — the live adapter's `size` is the view's `answeredCount`, the fixture's a Map), `undefined` where none is in flight. `railEntry` (setup.js) treats a defined `c.motionIn` as *theirs*: the bar is the motion's answers over `ctx.E` (the page's `E()`, which live is the view's `electorateSize` — the motion's own electorate, `motionElectorate()`), and the tooltip the same *n of E have answered* a delegated question wears. The mover's own accept is counted from the put (SPEC §9.6, `openMotion`'s `motion-answer` on open), so a fresh motion in a room of two reads *1 of 2*, half-washed, and the entry files as the mover's ⏳ wait with the same bar (Q1286 (a)). The state, mark and label of the entry are untouched — `mustAct` / `waiting` / `news` already keyed on `motionOn(c)` ahead of `isRoom`; only the bar and the tooltip were behind.

**What the fill reads on each kind of entry now.** A **delegated question** collecting: the question's answers over E, *n of E have answered* — unchanged. A **founder-held setting** with nothing in flight: 100%, the label — unchanged. A **settled setting resolved by ceremony**, nothing in flight: E of E, 100% — unchanged. A **setting with a 🏛️ motion in flight**, whoever holds it: the motion's answers over E, *n of E have answered*, moving as each member answers and full once everyone has (a *keep* blocks a 🏛️ motion without settling it, so *E of E* under ⏳ is a real state); once the motion settles or is withdrawn the entry reads as its setting again. An **ordinary-route motion** (✏️, staked and raced in the engine): no closeness on the page at all — unchanged, and the gap below.

**The guards.** `npm run journey`'s new `motionFillOnAmended` step, after the second seat's OK on the founder's 🌍 amendment: the member puts 🌍 back to *closed* on the assembly route over the wire (the composer's 🏛️ hold is `powers-walk`'s), and the founder's entry must read *1 of 2 have answered · fill 50%* while the mover's is a ⏳ with the same bar; the founder answers *keep* and it must read *2 of 2 · 100% · ⏳*; the member withdraws and the count must be gone. Red on the pre-fix page at exactly Ed's symptom — `{"fill":"100%","title":"Who Can See the Document?"}` on both seats — green after. The setup-probe's `motions` scenario moved on all twelve steps from `hold-assembly` on, every one of them the 🌡️ entry's `title` alone: the label giving way to *1 of 3 → 2 of 3 → 3 of 3 have answered* as the fixture's three seats answer, mark, state, label, caption and geometry identical; re-frozen with `qa:freeze`, which also caught up `design/reference/session.js` with the Q1311 merge (a byte-copy behind since then, invisible to the session-probe because the fixture holds no two-gap draft).

**The ordinary-route gap** (noted, not built — CLAUDE.md's `motion` entry: *ordinary adjudication in the page is still a dev seam*). An ✏️ motion on an ordinary setting is a one-candidate race in the engine (`engine-bridge.openSetMotion`), and its closeness would be the race's `closeness` exactly as a text race's `evidence-meter` is; but the server's `view()` filters `settingId` races out of `clauses`, so the page never sees the race at all, and the module's `MotionView.answeredCount` is 0 on the ordinary route by construction. Building it would take: the view carrying the setting-races' `closeness` (or the whole blind projection) keyed by motion id, the live adapter's `motionRecords()` handing it through, `resolveCounts` or `railEntry` reading a closeness rather than a count for an ordinary motion (a magnitude, never a direction — the meter's rule), and a tooltip sentence in `copy.js` for a race rather than a roll-call, since *n of E have answered* is the wrong sentence for evidence. `powers-walk` already raises an ordinary motion on ⏰ and would be the guard.

**Decisions taken alone, for Ed to reverse.** (i) The motion's count lives **beside** `c.in` (`c.motionIn`), not in its place. `c.in` is the setting's own question, and `ansTaskFor` reads `c.in < E()` as *the question is still open*: a motion's count written over a ceremony-resolved setting's `E` would have served that question's answer card again to anybody in its audience. The one reader of the new field is `railEntry`. (ii) On a **delegated, ceremony-resolved** setting with a 🏛️ motion in flight the motion's count wins over the resolution's *E of E*, since the bar is about what the room is doing now — the rail's state was already the motion's. (iii) The tooltip sentence *n of E have answered* stays the literal it was in `railEntry` (setup.js) rather than moving to `copy.js`: it predates this and moving it is a copy pass, not this fix; noted as drift against *every string a member can read lives in `design/copy.js`*. (iv) SURFACE §6's *wait* row already says *fill = how far the room has got*, which the fix makes true of a motion; nothing there was amended. (v) The walk asserts *1 of 2* and *2 of 2* literally — the journey room is exactly founder and one guest, GUEST2 being invited and never arriving — rather than deriving E from the view, so a change to the room's size fails loudly here instead of silently passing.
